classFeature.name: Wild Shape (Alternate)
entries: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you shape-shift into a Beast form, using either the Tiny Beast Shape or Minor Beast Shape stat block. You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Number of Uses
entries: You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

items.name: Bestial Traits
entries: You know six Bestial Traits that you meet the prerequisites for, and you have a budget of two Trait Points to spend on them. When you transform, you can spend Trait Points to add Bestial Traits that you know to the stat block you chose for the duration of that transformation. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can change your list of known traits with other eligible traits.
When you reach certain Druid levels, your number of known Traits, and your number of Trait Points both increase, as shown in the Bestial Traits table.

These traits represent the specific kind of beast you turn into. A table of suggested combinations for different kinds of animals is listed at the end of this document. The DM may decide that you can only choose trait combinations contained in this table.

items.name: Rules While Shape-Shifted
entries: While in a form, you retain your personality, memories, and ability to speak, and the following rules apply:

entries.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Druid level.

entries.name: Game Statistics
entries: Your game statistics are replaced by the chosen stat block, but you retain your class features; languages; and feats. You also retain your skill and saving throw proficiencies, in addition to gaining the proficiencies listed on the stat block. If a skill or saving throw modifier in the Beast's stat block is higher than yours, use the one in the stat block.

entries.name: No Spellcasting
entries: You can't cast spells, but shape-shifting doesn't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB} or otherwise interfere with a spell you've already cast.

entries.name: Objects
entries: When you transform, you choose whether your equipment falls in your space, merges into your new form, or is worn by it. Worn equipment functions as normal, but the DM decides whether it's practical for the new form to wear a piece of equipment based on the creature's size and shape. Your equipment doesn't change size or shape to match the new form, and any equipment that the new form can't wear must either fall to the ground or merge with the form. Equipment that merges with the form has no effect while you're in that form.

entries.name: All traits known
entries: The purpose of Known Traits is to streamline decision-making. Choosing two options from six is faster than choosing from sixteen.

For greater flexibility, your DM may allow you to ignore Known Traits or Forms entirely and access the full list. This option is best suited to experienced players who can plan ahead without slowing the game down.
{@note See {@variantrule Alternate Wild Shape Rules|Spaghetti0Patreon}}

subclassFeature.name: Smartphone Owner
entries: You have somehow come into the possession of a Smartphone - a strange, futuristic device that seemingly contains limitless knowledge. The origins and purpose of this device are mysterious, even to you. What is clear is that only you can be responsible for making use of the vast knowledge it holds.

subclassFeature.name: Smartphone Spells
entries: When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Smartphone Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. These count as Artificer spells for you, but don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

subclassFeature.name: Smartphone
entries: You are the proud owner of a mysterious magical device which puts unlimited information at your fingertips. The device is a Tiny object in the shape of a thin rectangle. If you lose your Smartphone or if it is destroyed, you can recreate it over the course of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The previous one, if it still exists, then ceases to work. The phone has the following functions:

items.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use your Smartphone as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Artificer spells. When you cast one of your Smartphone spells through it, you can ignore any costly material components.

items.name: Tutorials
entries: Over the course of 10 minutes, you can learn how to best use a set of tools by watching instructional recordings developed by helpful strangers. You gain proficiency with one type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice. Once you use this benefit, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, at which point you lose this proficiency.

items.name: Utilities
entries: Your Smartphone can be used to mimic certain pieces of equipment:

items: It can store limitless written information.
It can emit light like a {@item Candle|XPHB}, but doesn't burn out.
It displays the current time of day like a clock.

subclassFeature.name: Info Lookup
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can use your Smartphone to search for helpful information about a creature that you can see within 30 feet, doing one of the following:

items.name: Learn Stats
entries: You learn if the target has any {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and if so, you learn what they are.

items.name: Find Weakness
entries: You explain the creature's weak points to one of your allies within 30 feet. That ally has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack it makes against the target before the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Damage Subscription Plan
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature that you have targeted with your Info Lookup feature within the past hour, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage to it.

subclassFeature.name: Smartphone Overcharge
entries: When you cast certain spells through your Smartphone, you can cause the melding of magic and technology to enhance the spell. You can cast each of the following spells once without expending a spell slot, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Color Spray{@footnote *|{@i *If you are using the 5.5e version of {@spell Color Spray|XPHB}, each target uses its initial Constitution save, instead of rolling twice.}}
entries: Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must succeed on a Constitution save or take Radiant damage equal to {@damage 1d8} + your Artificer level, or half as much on a success.

items.name: Enthrall
entries: Select one of the spell's targets within 5 feet of you. That creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its save as you show it a fun and addictive game on your phone.

items.name: Sending
entries: Instead of you and the target each sending a message, you can freely engage in conversation for 1 minute. If the spell fails, you hear an odd beeping noise.

subclassFeature.name: Virtual Assistant
entries: You have upgraded your Smartphone to have artificial intelligence, granting it a voice and a personality. The Smartphone has an Intelligence score of 20 (+5), Wisdom of 15 (+2) and Charisma of 10 (+0). It can speak the languages you know, and is friendly toward you and your allies. If you create a new Smartphone, the intelligence transfers to the new phone.

items.name: Autonomous Function
entries: Your Smartphone can store magical knowledge. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can cast the {@spell Contingency|XPHB} spell without a spell slot or components. When you do, you need not expend the spell slot for the contingent spell, but you must provide any costly components for it as normal.

items.name: Quick Lookup
entries: When you use Info Lookup, you can target two different creatures at once. If you use Find Weakness twice, you must choose two different allies.

subclassFeature.name: Brutewright
entries: {@i Two Minds, One Body}

Brutewrights are Artificers who have subjected themselves to radical experiments in physical augmentation with mutagens. As a result, they now harbor two selves: a brilliant master of mutagenics, and a savage, musclebound alter-ego. This internal duality is both a source of power and a personal struggle.

subclassFeature.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice.
In addition, when you brew a potion using the crafting rules in the Dungeon Master's Guide, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

subclassFeature.name: Brutewright Spells
entries: When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Brutewright Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Brutish Transformation
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can surrender your keen mind and give way to a hulking brute. Being in your Brute form imparts the below effects on you for 10 minutes, or until you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end them early. You can use this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times your Artificer level. Any remaining points go away when the feature ends.

items.name: Brutish Strength
entries: Whenever you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} or a damage roll using Strength, you can use your Intelligence modifier in place of Strength. In addition, when you use the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} option of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can use your spell save DC instead of the normal DC. However, whenever you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} using Intelligence, you don't add your Intelligence modifier to the check, unless it's negative.

items.name: Smashing Strikes
entries: When you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and deal damage, you can deal Bludgeoning damage equal to {@damage 1d8} plus your Strength or Intelligence modifier, instead of the normal damage for an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d8} damage of the same type as the attack.

items.name: Spell Restriction
entries: You can only cast and/or {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on a spell if it only targets yourself, or if it appears on the Brutewright Spells table and deals damage.

subclassFeature.name: Mutagenic Shot
entries: While you have your {@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB} in hand, you can take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch a creature and briefly enhance its capabilities. Choose between Strength, Dexterity and Constitution. The target has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} using the chosen ability score until the start of your next turn.

You can't use this feature while you're in your Brute form, and you can only use it a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Assault
entries: You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Extra Attack
entries: While you are in your Brute form, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.

items.name: Swift Mutagen
entries: Once per turn when you cast an Artificer spell on an ally within 5 feet of you, you can use your Mutagenic Shot feature on that ally as part of the same action. This expends a use of your Mutagenic Shot as normal, and if the spell targets multiple allies, you choose which one gains the benefit.

subclassFeature.name: Augment Specialization
entries: Your mutagenic expertise allows you to shape your Brute form and your allies to be tougher, faster or larger. Select one of the below options. You can change your selection whenever you gain an Artificer level.

items.name: Adrenal Flood
entries: While you are in your Brute Form, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet and you have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. When you deal the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you can move up to 10 feet without expending movement or provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, provided your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} isn't 0.

In addition, when you use your Mutagenic Shot feature, the target moves swiftly until the start of your next turn. Its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled and it can make one additional attack when it takes the {@action Attack|XPHB} action.

items.name: Hulking Size
entries: While you are in your Brute form, if you are smaller than Large, you become Large and the damage die for your Smashing Strikes becomes a {@damage d10}. If there isn't enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesn't change. When you deal the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you can push the target 15 feet straight away from you.

In addition, when you use your Mutagenic Shot feature, the target's melee attacks are enhanced until the start of your next turn. Its reach is 5 feet greater than normal, and on a hit it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage.

items.name: Ironclad Endurance
entries: Choose one damage type other than Force. While you are in your Brute form, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that damage type. You can change your selection whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you roll the extra damage of your Smashing Strikes, you also gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that roll.

In addition, when you use your Mutagenic Shot feature, the target gains the damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} you chose until the start of your next turn. It also gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Artificer level.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Two Minds
entries: You and your Brutish self have reached a point of equilibrium, and can work with synergy.

items.name: Adapt Augment
entries: You can now change your choice of Augment Specialization when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Free Transformation
entries: You can remain in your Brute form indefinitely. Furthermore, when you transform into your Brute form, you can do so without expending a use of Brutish Transformation, but you don't gain any {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} when you transform in this way.

items.name: Brutal Smash
entries: The extra damage of your Smashing Strikes increases to {@damage 2d8} (or {@damage 2d10} for Hulking Size).

items.name: Supercharged Shot
entries: When you use your Mutagenic Shot feature, you can extend its benefits (including any enhancements from your Augment Specialization) to last for 1 minute. You then can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Reliquarian
entries: {@i Harness the Power of Divine Relics}

Reliquarians harness the divine magic hidden within relics: ancient religious artefacts, channelling their power by crafting special housings called Reliquaries. Witnesses tell of these artisans producing miracles from their Reliquaries - both merciful and terrible.

items.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice.

items.name: Divine Crafting
entries: {@item Holy Water|XPHB} is added to the list of items you can create with your Tinker's Magic feature. Also, when you craft a magic item with divine properties, the amount of time required to craft it is halved.

entries.name: Ruling for Divine Crafting
entries: Your DM will have final say on what counts as having divine properties. As a rule of thumb, anything that is described as divine or holy, or anything that casts a Cleric or Paladin spell would be appropriate.

subclassFeature.name: Reliquarian Spells
entries: When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Reliquarian Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Whenever you gain an Artificer level, you can exchange one of these spells for another spell of the same level from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric}. You cannot exchange the spells you gain at level 3 in this way.

subclassFeature.name: Reliquary
entries: You are in possession of a relic of divine origin. Use the Relic Origins table to determine the origin of your relic, or work with your DM to determine a new origin. When you gain this subclass, you construct a special housing to contain the relic and harness its divine power: the resulting artifact is your Reliquary. Both the relic and the Reliquary are Tiny objects with an appearance you describe. If you lose the Reliquary, you regain it when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.caption: Relic Origins
rows: The relic is a body part from the corpse of a god's Chosen.
The relic is a tool once utilised by a holy figure.
The relic is the shard of a weapon used to slay an angel.
The relic is an object stained with the blood of a saint.

entries: You can use the Reliquary as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB} for your Artificer spells, and while you are holding it, you gain the following benefits.

items.name: Holy Light
entries: When you deal damage with an Artificer spell, you can change the damage type to Radiant.

items.name: Channel Relic
entries: You can channel the relic's divine power to unleash miraculous effects. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can activate the relic for 1 hour, or until you activate it again. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while the relic is active, you can release one of the following effects. Once you activate the relic, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a spell slot to use it again (no action required).

items.name: Blessing
entries: You bolster one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. That creature gains the benefits of the {@spell Bless|XPHB} spell until the start of your next turn, as if you had cast it.

items.name: Protection
entries: One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself gains a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d6} plus half your Artificer level (round up), and it can immediately move up to 5 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

items.name: Wrath
entries: Searing light shines from the relic. Each creature in a 30-foot long, 5-foot wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} extending from yourself must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take {@damage 1d8} Radiant damage. The damage increases to {@damage 2d8} when you reach level 5, to {@damage 3d8} at level 9, and to {@damage 4d8} at level 15 as an Artificer.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Reliquary
entries: Select one of the following benefits. You can change your selection whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, or when you activate your relic's Channel Relic feature.

items.name: Holy Blessing
entries: When a creature under the effects of your {@spell Guidance|XPHB} or {@spell Bless|XPHB} spell rolls a 1 on that spell's d4, it can reroll the die until it rolls higher than a 1.

items.name: Divine Mercy
entries: When you grant one or more creatures {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with an Artificer spell, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the result to the healing total. You can do so only once per casting.
This benefit also extends to the {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} granted by your Channel Relic: Protection feature.

items.name: Celestial Wrath
entries: When you deal Radiant damage with an Artificer spell, you can roll {@dice 1d8} and add the result to that damage roll. You can do so only once per casting.
In addition, when a creature succeeds on its save against your Channel Relic: Wrath feature, it still takes half damage.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Armorer
entries: You have learned to infuse your relic's divine power into the armaments you create. Whenever you create a magic weapon, {@item Shield|XPHB} or suit of armor with your Replicate Magic Item feature, it gains additional benefits, depending on what type of item it is.

items.name: Armor
entries: A creature wearing this armor gains {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic and Radiant damage.

items.name: Shield
entries: When a creature wielding this {@item Shield|XPHB} is missed by an attack, the attacker is rebuked, causing it to take {@damage 1d4} Radiant damage, provided it is within 10 feet of the {@item Shield|XPHB}. This damage increases to {@damage 2d4} when you reach level 15 as an Artificer.

items.name: Weapon
entries: When the attacker hits with this weapon, it can choose to deal Radiant damage instead of its normal damage type. Once per turn when the weapon deals Radiant damage in this way, it deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d6} when you reach level 15 as an Artificer.

items.name: Perfected Reliquary
entries: You now simultaneously gain all three benefits of your Improved Reliquary feature.

items.name: Miracle
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can call on your Reliquary to perform a divine miracle. You immediately cast one spell of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell list|spells|class=Cleric} that has an Action casting time, ignoring any Material components. The spell's level can't exceed half your Artificer level (round up, maximum level 9).

Once you use this action, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless the feature was used to cast a level 7+ spell, in which case you can't use it again until you finish {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB|Long Rests}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Unsated
entries: {@i Stalk and Cause Terror to Your Victims}

You are the cause of that shiver that runs down a person's spine when nothing appears to be there - that feeling of being watched, or more accurately, hunted. Barbarians of this path embrace dark powers over fear, gained from unnerving otherworldly sources that few dare name, and even fewer seek willingly.

subclassFeature.name: Lurker in the Dark
entries: You are at home within darkness, its shroud making you more difficult to detect and more frightening. If you make an ability check with either the {@skill Stealth|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill while in {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} or {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}, you add your Rage Damage bonus to the check's total.

subclassFeature.name: Curse of Victimhood
entries: When you activate your Rage, you can curse one creature you can see within 30 feet to be your victim until your Rage ends, or until the creature dies or is targeted by the {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} spell. While your Rage is active and you have no cursed targets, you can move the curse to a different creature you can see within 30 feet as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

Once per turn, when you hit a cursed target with an attack, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and Strength modifier) or be subjected to one of the following effects until the start of your next turn. You choose which before the creature makes the save.

items.name: Afraid
entries: The creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, as your terrifying presence fills its mind.

items.name: Impotent
entries: The creature's attacks feel useless. It subtracts half your Barbarian level (round up) from the damage rolls of its attacks.

items.name: Unsteady
entries: If the creature moves at least 5 feet on its turn, when it ends its turn it gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, having inexplicably tripped.

subclassFeature.name: Pursuit of the Unsated
entries: While your Rage is active, your pursuit of your victims is nigh unstoppable, granting you the following benefits:

items.name: Uncontainable
entries: When your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 by an effect, such as the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, any attempt you make to end that effect that would normally require an action only takes a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} for you.

items.name: Unrelenting Pursuit
entries: You ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and other effects that would cause you to move more slowly, such as the {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB} spell, provided you are moving toward the target of your curse.

items.name: Victim Sight
entries: You always know the location of the target of your Curse of Victimhood, and you have a special form of {@sense Truesight|XPHB} to a range of 60 feet, which can only be used to see the cursed creature.

subclassFeature.name: Scopasthesia
entries: While your Rage is active, nearby creatures have the uneasy feeling that something is right behind them, silently watching. When a creature within 30 feet of you moves at least 5 feet away from you for the first time on a turn, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target, as if you were right behind it all along. You do so immediately before the creature leaves its space, who must then choose to stay in its space or continue the move. If it would trigger one on this turn, you can make an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} against the creature as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Fear's Embodiment
entries: While your Rage is active you become an embodiment of fear itself, unknowable and inescapable. You gain the following benefits until your Rage ends:

items.name: Fear Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Curse Improvement
entries: When a creature fails its saving throw against your Curse of Victimhood, you can apply two effects to it, instead of one.

items.name: Cursed Strike
entries: The Psychic damage you deal with Curse of Victimhood increases to {@damage 1d12}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Banshee
entries: {@i Scream with Undead Fury}

Banshees are woeful undead, terrorizing all that dare venture near with their deadly wail. You have somehow taken on the terrible traits of a Banshee, whether through training, an encounter with a banshee you survived or some other origin. Barbarians of this path embody physical characteristics of the Banshee: pale skin, gaunt features and moments of translucency.

subclassFeature.name: Horrifying Visage
entries: Your frightening appearance makes those around you uneasy. You gain proficiency with the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill. If you already have this proficiency, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Banshee's Scream
entries: You gain the capability to infuse the Banshee's horrible scream into your Rage. As a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to activate or maintain your Rage, you can unleash a Banshee's Scream in a 15-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} originating from your space. Choose one of the following options when you activate your Rage. The saving throw DC for these effects is equal to 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and your Strength modifier.

items.name: Shockwave Scream
entries: Each creature in the area must make a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from you. Objects that aren't being worn or carried are automatically pushed.

items.name: Debilitating Scream
entries: Each creature in the area that can hear you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. While {@condition Deafened|XPHB} in this way, it cannot take {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saving throws to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

items.name: Horrifying Scream
entries: Each creature in the area must make a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Momentary Incorporeality
entries: You have developed a limited form of the Banshee's incorporeality, which you can activate for moments at a time in the following ways.

items.name: Incorporeal Defense
entries: When you are hit by an attack that deals Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that instance of damage. If your Rage is active, you gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} instead.

items.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the ability to move through creatures and objects as if they were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} until the end of your next turn. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage.

You can use one of these options a number of times equal to your Strength modifier (minimum once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Dreadful Screech
entries: Your Banshee's Scream has become more powerful. You can now choose to cause the scream to manifest as a 5-foot wide and 30-foot long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}, instead of a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. In addition, your scream options improve in the following ways:

items.name: Shockwave Scream
entries: Creatures that fail their saving throw additionally have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Debilitating Scream
entries: Creatures that fail their saving throw additionally have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Horrifying Scream
entries: Creatures that fail their saving throw have a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0 while they have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition from this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Banshee Manifestation
entries: You can now choose which Banshee's Scream option to use each time you use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to screech. Additionally, you have learned to channel the Banshee's most dreadful and dangerous ability: its Wail. You learn the following additional Banshee's Scream option:

items.name: Wail
entries: Each creature in the area must make a Constitution saving throw or take {@damage 8d6} Psychic damage, taking half as much damage on a success. If this effect reduces the creature's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to fewer than your Barbarian level, it instead drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once you use this Banshee's Scream option, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Extreme Focus
entries: {@i Be Focussed, Precise and Intentional}

Barbarians of the Path of Extreme Focus are often raised in environments under threat of psionic monsters, such as mind flayers or aboleths. They train in mental disciplines which allow them to fortify their minds against these threats. When they rage, instead of channeling emotion, these barbarians channel determination and focus, sharpening their senses and permitting greater control of their movements.

subclassFeature.name: Focussed Rage
entries: When you activate your Rage, you enter an extremely attentive and focussed state. You gain one of the following benefits of your choice until the rage ends:

items.name: Attentive
entries: You gain a +5 bonus to ability checks using the {@skill Insight|XPHB} and {@skill Perception|XPHB} skills.

items.name: Mental Protection
entries: You add your Rage Damage bonus to your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

items.name: Critical Focus
entries: Your attack rolls with weapons and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19-20 on the d20.
When you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to extend your rage, you can choose to switch your current benefit for another.

subclassFeature.name: Calculated Recklessness
entries: Your heightened focus grants you the capacity to be more thoughtful with your reckless attacks. When you use your Reckless Attack, you do not provoke {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} from all attackers. Instead, only creatures you hit with an attack roll on the turn you activate it gain the {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Reflexive Retaliation
entries: Your heightened attentiveness allows you to take advantage of momentary lapses in your foes' defense. When you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to your AC until the start of your next turn. If this causes the triggering attack to miss, you can make a melee weapon attack against the attacker as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, if it is within reach.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Control
entries: You have gained the ability to cleanse your mind of mality, and can cleanse the minds of your allies as well. When you start your turn with the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB} or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions, you can immediately end one of those conditions by emptying your mind (no action required).
Alternatively, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to touch a creature with one of these conditions and immediately end it on them, as you empty their mind and help them regain control.
You can end a condition in this way a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Perfected Mind
entries: You have perfected your control over your mind, making it impenetrable to your foes and allowing you to focus on multiple things at once. While your Rage is active, you no longer have to choose between your Focussed Rage options, and simultaneously gain the benefits of all three.
In addition, while your Rage is active you gain the benefits of the {@spell Mind Blank|XPHB} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Horde
entries: Barbarians of the Path of the Horde develop their power by forming strong bonds with their comrades, and by exclusively attacking in groups. Their connection to their horde results in a mystical link, allowing the group to freely share tactics, resiliences and skills.

subclassFeature.name: Group Demoralize
entries: While accompanied by your horde, you are especially imposing. You have proficiency with the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill. If you already have this proficiency, choose another skill from the list available to Barbarians at level 1. If you make a check with the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill while two or more of your allies are within 5 feet of you, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with the check.

subclassFeature.name: Exploit Defenses
entries: You can reveal weaknesses in your enemies' defense, granting your horde the perfect opportunity to strike. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a melee attack while your Rage is active, you can mark that creature until the start of your next turn. When one of your allies makes an attack against a marked target, you can grant that creature a bonus to hit equal to your Rage Damage bonus (no action required). On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to half your Barbarian level (round up) and the mark disappears.

subclassFeature.name: Horde's Resilience
entries: When you activate your Rage, you can select a number of creatures equal to your Rage Damage bonus that are within 30 feet of you. Until the Rage ends, they gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to one damage type that you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Horde's Assault
entries: You can direct your fury into your horde, causing your allies to strike. When you activate your Rage, or as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while your Rage is active, you can direct a willing creature within 30 feet of you to use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a weapon attack against a target you can see, provided the target is within range.

subclassFeature.name: Horde's Surge
entries: When one of your allies within 30 feet of you reduces a hostile creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can immediately use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a weapon attack.

subclassFeature.name: College of Mime
entries: {@i Work Magical Wonders in Silent Performances}

Bards of this college put together precise and practiced silent routines, pantomiming the presence of nonexistent entities. The secret that these bards hold, however, is that they have learned to mime objects and beings into existence, creating unexpected invisible entities which they can use both artistically and offensively.

subclassFeature.name: Pantomime Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to incorporate your spells into your silent act. Whenever you cast a Bard spell, you can ignore any Verbal or Material components that aren't costly or consumed. When you do so, you must perform a Somatic component for the spell, even if it doesn't usually have one, usually in the form of a mime routine.

When you cast a spell in this way, you can attempt to obscure the fact that you are casting a spell. Creatures that can see you when you cast the spell can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC, understanding that you cast a spell on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Invisible Shield
entries: You gain the ability to develop an invisible shield-like force field to ward off incoming attacks. When you or a creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to roll and expend a Bardic Inspiration die to create a shield. The shield has a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to two times the number rolled, and takes damage instead of the target. The shield lasts until the end of the current turn, or until it runs out of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, at which point it audibly shatters and any damage not absorbed by the shield carries over to the target.

subclassFeature.name: Mime Routines
entries: By infusing magic into your pantomime act, you can produce special effects that allow you to seemingly break the laws of physics. You learn the following acts:

items.name: Defy Gravity
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you grant yourself a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover for 1 minute, as you climb non-existent objects, swim through air, or some other amusing act.

items.name: Invisible Box
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you attempt to trap a creature within 5 feet of you inside an invisible box of magical force. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or be trapped in the box. While trapped, the creature has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} and is unable to move. The box is an object with AC equal to 12 + your Charisma modifier, and a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Bard level. The box vanishes after 1 minute, or when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

items.name: Sudden Gust
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, an apparent strong gust of wind emerges from your space in a 50-foot-long, 10-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each creature of your choice in that area (potentially including yourself) must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be pushed 30 feet in the wind's direction.
You can use one of these acts a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Unseen Spells
entries: You gain the ability to fold your spells into your pantomime routine. When you use your Pantomime Spellcasting feature, you can choose to make the spell's effects invisible to creatures without {@sense Truesight|XPHB}, resulting in the following effects:

items.name: Unseen Hazards
entries: Creatures that cannot see the spell subtract {@dice 1d4} from any saving throw they make to avoid or resist it.

items.name: Unseen Strike
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any attack roll you make with the spell against a creature that cannot see it.

items.name: Unseen Summons
entries: Any creature or object summoned by the spell has the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for the spell's duration. An {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creature must roll {@dice 1d4} at the end of any turn on which they made an attack or cast a spell. On a roll of 1, the condition ends on it.

If the spell has no visual elements to begin with, then using this feature confers no benefit. Furthermore, if the spell only affects targets that see its effects, such as with {@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB}, then any creature without {@sense Truesight|XPHB} is unaffected by the spell.
Once you cast a spell in this way, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: College of Angst
entries: {@i Wake Me Up Inside (Can't Wake Up)}

Bards of the College of Angst claim to harbour a deep emptiness in their soul, which they channel into dreary expressions of dark despair. Wielding profound power over emotions, their performances inspire rebellion in their allies and drown their foes in misery. Forever misunderstood, these Bards broadcast their agony for all to hear.

subclassFeature.name: Dabbler in Dark Magics
entries: Your dark feelings have granted you even darker magic. Enchantment and Necromancy spells from the {@filter Warlock spell list|spells|class=Warlock|school=E;N} are added to the Bard spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Tormented Muse
entries: Whenever you give an ally a Bardic Inspiration die, your performance stirs a deeply held dark emotion from it. When the ally uses the Bardic Inspiration die, the emotion bursts forth and provides an additional effect, based on whether the die benefits an ability check, attack roll or saving throw.

items.name: Anger (attack roll)
entries: Immediately after the attack roll, the target of the attack must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of the attacker's next turn. The attacker is the source of the fear.

items.name: Fear (saving throw)
entries: The ally's fear flares and makes it more wary of its situation. It adds the result of the die roll to its AC until the start of its next turn.

items.name: Sorrow (ability check)
entries: The ally's sorrow wells up, creating an emotional barrier. It gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number rolled on the Bardic Inspiration die plus your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: If Misery is Contagious Then Let Me Be Your Plague
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can begin a performance, laced with dour magic which leaves its listeners mired in angst. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Inspire Angst
entries: When you start the performance, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your subsequent turns, you can force a number of creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) that can see or hear you and are within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, a creature gains one level of Angst, to a maximum of 3. Refer to the Angst Effects table to determine the effects on the creature, which are cumulative with each added level.
You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} as part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to grant an ally a Bardic Inspiration die.

items.name: Duration
entries: The performance lasts for a maximum of 1 minute. It ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or choose to end it early (no action required).

items.name: Ending the Effect
entries: An affected creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, reducing its level of Angst by 1 on a success. If a creature succeeds on its initial save, or otherwise reduces its level of Angst to 0, it automatically succeeds on all subsequent saving throws it makes against this performance.
An affected creature automatically loses all levels of Angst when the performance ends, or if it is affected by the {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} spells.

entries.caption: Angst Effects
rows: 1 - The creature begins to feel the weight of its emotion pull it down.
The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks.
2 - The creature is overwhelmed by its dark emotions.
The target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls.
3 - The creature is despondent. It can do little more than brood.
The target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Not Just a Phase
entries: Your misery festers, twisting into dreadful might. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Crippling Angst
entries: If a creature fails its saving throw against your Inspire Angst by 5 or more, it gains two levels of Angst, instead of one.

items.name: I'm (Not) Okay
entries: When you become {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB} or gain the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you can empower your performances with the pain of your current existence. For the next minute, your spell save DC increases by 2 and whenever a creature rolls one of your Bardic Inspiration dice, it can add 2 to the roll's total.
Once you use this benefit, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: College of Vanity
entries: {@i Obsess in your Incredible Self}

Bards of the College of Vanity value nothing more than the admiration of their perfect selves; admiration from others, but also themselves. These self-interested bards brave the risks of adventuring for a shot at attaining glory and recognition. Not to mention, it would be a crime to not share that face with the world.

subclassFeature.name: Self-Interested
entries: You are easily distracted by reflections of yourself, your shadow, or even thoughts about yourself. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw you make to avoid or end the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, and any save that requires you to see an effect to be affected by it, such as a {@creature Medusa|XMM}'s Gaze.

subclassFeature.name: Vain Inspiration
entries: When you use your Bardic Inspiration feature to inspire an ally, you get caught up in your own hype and also inspire yourself. The Bardic Inspiration die you grant yourself is a {@dice d4}. The feature otherwise benefits you as it would any other creature.
The size of the die you grant yourself increases when you reach certain levels in this class: {@dice 1d6} at level 10 and {@dice 1d8} at level 15.

subclassFeature.name: Center of Attention
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can attempt to force those around you to pay attention to you. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of yourself must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, a creature has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While it is {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, Wisdom checks and Charisma checks made to engage, observe, or otherwise deal with creatures other than you. An affected creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. The effect ends early for all targets if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if you use this feature again.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can restore the use of this feature by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Inflated Confidence
entries: When you roll a Bardic Inspiration die granted to you by your Vain Inspiration and it causes you to succeed on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, your own success inspires you further, causing the die to not be spent. You can retain a die in this way no more than once per use of your Bardic Inspiration feature.

subclassFeature.name: Celebration Domain
entries: {@i Celebrate your Allies' Accomplishments}

Celebrations may not be essential for survival, but they are paramount to living: this is the ethos carried by clerics of the Celebration Domain and the deities they worship. Clerics of this domain are renowned for their exuberant parties and banquets, which are open to all that wish to celebrate. They are also infamous for an abundance of holy days throughout the calendar year, supplying them ample opportunities to be festive.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Celebration Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Celebration Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Charm Person|XPHB}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB}, {@spell Tasha's Hideous Laughter|XPHB}
{@spell Create Food and Water|XPHB}, {@spell Hypnotic Pattern|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Congratulatory Flourish
entries: Whenever you see another creature within 60 feet of you succeed on an attack roll or ability check, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to create a brief celebratory flourish, creating some sort of audible or visual effect of your choice, such as a burst of spectral confetti or a brief jingle. The creature can reroll one {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} that it makes within the next hour, drawing inspiration and confidence from the congratulation.
Once you target a creature with this ability, you can't target it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Infectious Festivities
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity and let loose an immense festive atmosphere, emanating in a 30-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} from a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Creatures within the area hear spectral music, feel the exhilaration of a party, and experience the effects of party libations. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move the party area up to 30 feet to a different point you can see.

You and your allies within the area gain a bonus to Charisma checks and Wisdom saving throws. This bonus is equal to the number of their allies who are also in the area, including themself, to a maximum of your Wisdom modifier (minimum bonus of +1). The party area lasts for 1 minute, until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or until you use this feature again.

subclassFeature.name: Party Favors
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can grant one creature you can see within 30 feet of you a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Cleric level plus your Wisdom modifier. While the creature has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, it gains one of the following benefits of your choice:

items.name: Boldness
entries: The creature has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Exhilaration
entries: The creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 15 feet.

items.name: Fancy Steps
entries: The creature cannot be targeted by {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Restoring Celebration
entries: When you take a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can shower your party with the congratulations of your deity. You and each ally that participates in the rest gains one of the following benefits of their choice:

items.name: Healing
entries: It regains twice as many {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from rolling {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice}.

items.name: Firework Strike
entries: Once before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when the creature hits a target with an attack, it can subject the target to concentrated party energy, dealing an additional {@damage 4d10} Radiant damage and the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Spell Recovery
entries: It rolls {@dice 1d6} and regains one expended spell slot of a level up to the number rolled.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Creation Domain
entries: {@i Shape the World and Conjure Life}

Clerics of the Creation Domain worship deities that were expressly involved in the creation of the universe, the shaping of the world and the genesis of life. Their worship grants them powers to shape and reshape the natural world around them, and to create facsimiles of life through conjuration magic.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Creation Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Creation Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Entangle|XPHB}, {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB}, {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB}
{@spell Create Food and Water|XPHB}, {@spell Plant Growth|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Reshape Creation
entries: You have a special ability to reshape things that you create with your spells. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can select one creature or object that you have conjured with a spell and reshape it into another form offered by the spell. The spell must be a Cleric spell from the Conjuration school. This change does not cause the target's current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to increase, nor cause it to lose any conditions.
For example, you could use this action to change a bat conjured by {@spell Find Familiar|XPHB} into a spider.

subclassFeature.name: Natural Genesis
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use your Channel Divinity to temporarily create a localised natural formation that you describe, originating from within 60 feet of yourself. The formation remains for 10 minutes, and creates one of the following effects of your choice.

items: You create a natural obstruction such as a river or quicksand, forming {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} in a shape you describe in a 20-foot radius around the origin point.

You create a Large or smaller natural object such as a tree or a boulder in an unoccupied space on the ground at the origin point, which can be used as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} by creatures its size or smaller.

subclassFeature.name: Create Life
entries: Your deity grants you a limited capability to create new life. You always have the {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB} spell prepared, which is your Creation Spell. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can exchange {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB} for a different spell, which becomes your Creation Spell in its place. The new spell must be a Cleric, Druid or Wizard spell that is of a level you can prepare as a Cleric, and its only effect must be to summon one creature for the spell's duration, such as Summon Plant or {@spell Summon Celestial|XPHB}.
In addition, your ability to cast the spell is enhanced in the following ways.

items.name: No Materials Required
entries: You can cast your Creation Spell without the need for Material Components.

items.name: Magical Strikes
entries: When the summoned creature deals Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage, it can choose to change the damage type to Radiant.

items.name: Conferred Miracles
entries: Whenever you cast a Cleric spell with a range other than {@filter 'Self'|spells|class=cleric|range=!self} you can originate it from the summoned creature's space.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Disciple
entries: Your magical creations become more grounded in reality. Whenever you cast your Creation spell using a level 1-5 spell slot, you can remove the spell's requirement for you to {@status Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate} on it. The spell ends early if you cast it again.

In addition, you can now cast Cleric spells with a range of {@filter 'Self'|spells|class=cleric} through the summoned creature's space. The effects of such spells treat the summoned creature as though it were the caster.

subclassFeature.name: Luck Domain
entries: {@i Manipulate Fortune with Divine Luck}

As much as some gods would like you to believe that the world and fate are set and perfectly ordered, to many it is apparent that fate is largely up to chance. As a result, gods of luck or good fortune, such as Tymora or Haela Brightaxe are often prayed to for good fortune, whether it be in battle or in everyday life. Priests of such deities and temples devoted to them are uncommon, since their faith tends not to stress a need for intermediaries. Such priests exist out in the world, channeling their good fortune to those who need it.
Clerics of the Luck domain tend to be chaotic, enjoying the twists of fate laid before them, but have been granted the ability to tilt luck in their own favor from time to time.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Luck Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Luck Domain Spells
rows: {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Second Chance
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 30 feet of you rolls for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and rolls a 1 or a 20 on the d20, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to alter fate and cause the creature to roll again, and they must use the new roll.
Once you use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Lucky Charm
entries: Your deity grants you the ability to bestow good fortune to your allies. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity and choose a number of creatures up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum one creature) that you can see within 30 feet of you and grant them luck for 1 minute.
When an affected creature fails a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, it can reroll the d20 and must use the new roll. The effect then ends.

subclassFeature.name: Blessing of Fortune or Misfortune
entries: You gain an increased capability to impose fortune or misfortune on yourself and those around you.

When you start casting {@spell Bless|XPHB} or {@spell Bane|XPHB}, you can choose to have the spell not require {@status Concentration|XPHB} for this casting. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Peek Behind the Curtain
entries: Your devotion to the forces of luck and chance have blessed you with the power to bestow incredible luck. You always have the {@spell Foresight|XPHB} spell prepared.

When you cast the spell, while it is active you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to transfer its effects to a different willing creature you touch. The spell immediately ends on its previous target, and the new target gains its benefits for the remainder of its duration, or until you transfer it again. You can transfer the spell's effects in this way a number of times up to your Wisdom modifier per casting of the spell (minimum once).

subclassFeature.name: Rocket Warrior
entries: {@i Dominate the Battlefield in Three Dimensions}

Rocket Warriors equip themselves with advanced propulsion devices which send them rocketing through open air and space to inflict attacks with devastating momentum. These warriors are most commonly found voyaging the astral sea, utilising their aerial prowess to great strategic advantage - the high ground is always theirs; no enemy is safe.

subclassFeature.name: Rocket Pack
entries: You have developed, inherited, or found a device capable of propelling you forward with great speed and momentum. As part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can fit the pack to a suit of armor, which it remains a part of until you use this process to transfer it to different armor. While you are wearing the fitted suit of armor, you gain the following benefits.

items.name: Fuel Points
entries: The Rocket Pack does not require fuel, but can only be used a certain amount before it must be recharged. It has the capacity for a number of Fuel Points equal to twice your Fighter level. After 1 minute of not spending any Fuel Points, the pack regains all expended points.

items.name: Liftoff
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can produce the effects of the {@spell Levitate|XPHB} spell on yourself without requiring {@status Concentration|XPHB}. At the end of any of your turns where the effect was active, you expend one Fuel Point. You can end the effect at any time (no action required), and it ends immediately if you have no fuel points remaining.

items.name: Rocket Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can expend 2 Fuel Points and 10 feet of movement to propel yourself up to 20 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. If you immediately follow this movement with a Melee weapon attack, on a hit you deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage of the weapon's type. If you use Action Surge, you can use this ability one additional time on that turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Rocket Strike
entries: When you use your Rocket Strike, you can now expend additional Fuel Points to increase its potency. For each additional point you spend, the distance you can move increases by 5 feet, and for every two additional points, the extra damage increases by {@damage 1d8}. The maximum number of additional points you can spend at once is equal to half your Fighter level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Refuel
entries: When you use your Second Wind feature to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, your Rocket Pack regains a number of Fuel Points equal to half its maximum capacity (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Aeronaut
entries: Your Rocket Pack's Liftoff feature improves.

items.name: Rocket Flight
entries: When you use Liftoff, you can now grant yourself a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, in addition to the effects of the {@spell Levitate|XPHB} spell. You must expend two Fuel Points at the end of your turns when you do so, instead of one - if this leaves you with only 1 point remaining, the {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} ends.

items.name: Evasive Maneuvers
entries: While you are in the air using Liftoff, if you make a saving throw against an area of effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend 2 Fuel Points and move 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. If this movement moves you out of range of the effect, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the save and suffer no effects on a success.

subclassFeature.name: True Rocketeer
entries: Your Rocket Pack's Liftoff feature improves again, allowing you to achieve true, sustained flight.

items.name: Improved Rocket Flight
entries: Your Liftoff and Rocket Flight features no longer expend Fuel Points at the end of your turns. The effect still ends early if you have 0 Fuel Points remaining, and the pack doesn't regain Fuel Points due to inactivity while it is active.

items.name: Boost
entries: When you activate Rocket Flight, or when you start your turn with it active, you can expend 1–3 Fuel Points. For each point you spend, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Aerial Dominance
entries: You can now use your Rocket Strike feature any number of times on your turn, provided you expend the necessary movement and Fuel Points.

subclassFeature.name: Mimic Knight
entries: You have magically bonded with a mimic, a shapeshifting monster with a habit for disguising itself as inanimate objects. Through your training, it serves as your weapon, armor or shield - alive and deadly. Together, you adapt, deceive and strike with cunning.

subclassFeature.name: Mimic Companion
entries: You have trained your mimic to take the form of your armaments instead of acting on its own.

items.name: Devour Item
entries: Over the course of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the mimic can devour one piece of non-magical equipment. The item must be a Simple or Martial melee weapon, a {@item Shield|XPHB}, or a suit of armor, and is destroyed in the process. Thereafter, whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the mimic can take the form of one of the objects it has previously devoured, granting the corresponding benefits below while you have it equipped.

items.name: Magic Mimicry
entries: The mimic can also devour a magical version of one of the above listed items. Rather than destroying the magic item, it temporarily merges with your mimic. The item is harmlessly regurgitated if the mimic devours another one, if it is destroyed or if you die. While your mimic is transformed into an item of the same category as the devoured magic item, it gains the item's magical properties, even if it isn't the same kind of weapon or armor.

items.name: Mimic's Bite
entries: In certain situations (described below), your mimic is able to bite a target. Choose Acid or Piercing damage. The target takes {@damage 1d6} damage of the chosen type. This damage increases to {@damage 2d6} when you reach level 15 in this class.

items.name: Re-spawn
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can summon a new mimic, which knows all of the mundane forms that the previous one did. If you already have a mimic from this feature, the old one is destroyed when the new one appears.

items.name: Weapon Shift
entries: Immediately before you make an attack roll using the mimic, you can command it to take the shape of another devoured weapon (no action required).

items.name: Mimic Mastery
entries: Practice with your shifting weapon allows you to prepare an additional {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery}, which you can only use when attacking with the mimic.

items.name: Bite
entries: Once per turn, you can use your Mimic's Bite when you hit a target with an attack roll using the mimic.

items.name: Sticky Grasp
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and take the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} option, you can do so without needing a free hand. You can only {@condition Grappled|XPHB|Grapple} one creature in this way at a time per mimic with this feature.

items.name: Bite
entries: When a creature starts its turn {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you, you can use your Mimic's Bite on it.

items.name: Engulfing Form (Armor Only)
entries: You can don and doff the armor as a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action. In addition, a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by your Sticky Grasp has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to escape the Grapple.

items.name: Quick Grasp (Shield Only)
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to use your {@item Shield|XPHB}'s Sticky Grasp.

subclassFeature.name: Mundane Mimicry
entries: As an action, you can command your mimic to temporarily replicate the form of a Small or Tiny object you can see within 30 feet of you. The mimic appears like a near-perfect imitation of that object for 1 hour or until you command it to return to its normal form (no action required). Its true nature can be discerned by a creature who succeeds on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check by taking the {@action Study|XPHB} action. The DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
If a creature touches the mimic for the first time on a turn or starts its turn touching it while it's in this state, you can use your Mimic's Bite on it.

subclassFeature.name: Adhesive Form
entries: While you have your mimic equipped, you gain a benefit:

items.name: Reactive Grasp (Shield)
entries: When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to use your {@item Shield|XPHB}'s Sticky Grasp against the attacker.

items.name: Reposition (Weapon)
entries: When you hit a Large or smaller creature with the mimic, you can move the target horizontally to an unoccupied space within your reach.

items.name: Sticky Shell (Armor)
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can climb difficult surfaces, even ceilings, while keeping your hands free and without needing to make an ability check.

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Offspring
entries: Your mimic has spawned an offspring. You now have two mimics, and can equip each of them separately. The second mimic follows the same rules as the original and can turn into all the same forms the original can, but merges with magic items separately.

subclassFeature.name: Mimic Spawning
entries: You always have the {@spell Animate Objects|XPHB} spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components, and your spellcasting ability for it is Constitution. When you cast the spell, you create mimics in the form of objects you choose in unoccupied spaces within the spell's range, instead of animating existing objects, which vanish when the spell ends.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Unbreakable Adhesive
entries: You gain the following benefits.

items.name: No Escape
entries: When a creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you teleports or is forcefully moved away from you, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw against your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} DC. On a failure, you maintain the Grapple and travel with the target.

items.name: Ensnare
entries: When a creature succeeds on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} to avoid or escape being {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to cause it to fail instead and take Acid damage equal to {@damage 1d6} + half your Fighter level.

subclassFeature.name: Kinetic Knight
entries: {@i Toss, Toss… Kaboom!}

Kinetic Knights channel evocation magic into objects to manipulate the potential energy within. The release of this energy causes their weaponry to erupt in highly destructive explosions. Whether you studied the arcane to attain this power or were simply born with it, you find that making things go boom is often the best solution to a given problem.

subclassFeature.name: Kinetic Armaments
entries: You are able to activate the latent kinetic energy within everyday objects, turning them into deadly weapons.

items.name: Improvised Proficiency
entries: You have proficiency with {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons}, and when you attack with one you can roll {@damage 1d8} for its damage, instead of {@damage 1d4}, and it has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} (20/60) properties for you.

items.name: Improvised Mastery
entries: You can select {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons} as one of your weapon choices for your {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery} feature. An improvised weapon's Mastery property depends on whether it can be wielded in one or two hands: {@itemMastery Sap|XPHB} for one-handed, and {@itemMastery Push|XPHB} for two-handed.

subclassFeature.name: Kinetic Charge
entries: You can charge your weapons and ammunition with excess kinetic energy, causing them to explode.

items.name: Kinetic Modifier
entries: When you select this subclass, choose your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma modifier to be your Kinetic modifier. Some features call for your Kinetic DC, which is equal to 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and your Kinetic modifier.

items.name: Kinetic Explosion
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit with an attack made with a weapon or an improvised weapon, you can imbue the weapon or its ammunition with explosive energy, changing its damage type to Force and creating a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} explosion which originates from the weapon or projectile. Roll {@dice 3d6} and select one of the following effects. Each creature, other than you, and each object that isn't being worn or carried in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} is subjected to the chosen effect.

items.name: Rending Blast
entries: Targets in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} take Force damage equal to the roll. An affected creature can make a Dexterity saving throw against your Kinetic DC, taking half as much damage on a success.

items.name: Pushing Blast
entries: Targets in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} are pushed a number of feet away from the explosion's origin equal to the roll. An affected creature can make a Strength saving throw against your Kinetic DC, and isn't pushed on a success. A Huge or larger creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw.

items.name: Uses
entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Kinetic modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Reflexive Toss
entries: When you are targeted by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to throw off the attack with a quickly charged explosion. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check with a DC equal to the attacker's attack roll. On a success, the attack automatically misses you. If you successfully throw off a melee attack, both you and the attacker are also pushed back 10 feet in opposite directions by the explosion.

Once you use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a use of your Kinetic Charge to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Volatile Explosions
entries: When you use your Kinetic Explosion, if you roll a 6 on any of the d6s, you can roll another {@dice d6} for each 6 rolled and add the result to the total. If the new die also rolls a 6, you can roll another, following the same process, and so on, to a maximum number of extra dice equal to your Kinetic modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Compounding Energy
entries: The roll for your Kinetic Explosion feature increases to {@dice 4d6}. It increases again by {@dice 1d6} at Fighter levels 15 ({@dice 5d6}) and 18 ({@dice 6d6}).

subclassFeature.name: Molecular Acceleration
entries: You turn your control over kinetic energy inward, enhancing your agility. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and you gain a bonus to your Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) and Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks equal to your Kinetic modifier (minimum +1).

subclassFeature.name: Improved Kinetic Charge
entries: Your Kinetic Charge feature improves.

items.name: Megaton Blast
entries: When you use your Kinetic Explosion, you can expend additional uses of Kinetic Charge to increase the size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} by 10 feet for each charge beyond the first.

items.name: Recharge
entries: When you use your Second Wind to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you also regain one expended use of your Kinetic Charge.

subclassFeature.name: Kinetic Detonation
entries: When you use your Kinetic Explosion feature, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to amplify the effects. The explosion creates both effects, instead of choosing one. A target creature only makes one saving throw against this combined effect: you choose whether it is a Strength or Dexterity save. Regardless of your choice, a creature has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on a failed save. Furthermore, Huge and larger creatures do not automatically succeed on their saving throw.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend one use of your Kinetic Charge to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: The Foolish Warrior
entries: {@i Stumble through Combat With Incredible Luck}

Foolish Warriors obliviously breeze through combat with extraordinary luck, barely dodging out of the way of hazards and stumbling into successful maneuvers. This luck may be supernatural in nature, the result of some blessing or curse, or perhaps your foolish warrior just has random chance on their side.

subclassFeature.name: Lucky Break
entries: You have a wellspring of luck, called Lucky Breaks.

items.name: Uses
entries: You have three Lucky Breaks. You gain one more use when you reach levels 7, 10, and 15 in this class.
