You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Lucky Break DC
entries: Some of your features use your Lucky Break DC, which is equal to 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and your Constitution modifier.

items.name: Lucky Break Die
entries: Some of your features use your Lucky Break die, which is a {@dice d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Unexpectedly Elusive
entries: You have an oddly potent knack for avoiding unseen threats. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against traps, and creatures do not gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against you from the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} or {@condition Invisible|XPHB} conditions.

In addition, when you are hit by an attack, you can expend a Lucky Break to roll your Lucky Break die and subtract the result from the attack roll, potentially turning it into a miss, as you stumble out of harm's way.

subclassFeature.name: Accidental Strike
entries: Sometimes when you fumble a weapon attack, the event cascades into your enemies being harmed anyway. For example, an errant arrow might ricochet around a room and cause a light fixture to fall on an enemy.

Once per turn when you miss with a weapon attack, you can expend a Lucky Break to force one creature of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Dexterity saving throw against your Lucky Break DC. On a failure, the creature takes Piercing, Bludgeoning, or Slashing damage (your choice) equal to one roll of your Lucky Break die plus your Fighter level.

subclassFeature.name: Fumblemaker
entries: Your good fortune has evolved to become your enemies' misfortune. When a creature misses you with an attack roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend a Lucky Break and inadvertently cause the enemy to fumble. Choose one of the following effects to occur:

items.name: Stuck
entries: The attacker's weapon or ammunition gets embedded in the ground or some other element of the environment within 5 feet of you. Once on its turn, a creature within 5 feet of the object can attempt to retrieve it by making a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your Lucky Break DC. On a failure, the object remains stuck in place.

items.name: Slip
entries: The creature makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Lucky Break DC. On a failure, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and it cannot stand up until the start of its next turn.

items.name: Whoops
entries: The creature rolls the attack again, but targets a different creature of your choice within the weapon's range, as the attack ricochets, it overshoots its swing, or some other unlikely series of events occurs.

subclassFeature.name: Brave Flail
entries: You have become well accustomed to facing threats that are well above your pay grade, and have learned a clever trick to calm your nerves in the face of extreme danger.

As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can shut your eyes tightly for 1 minute. You have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, and while {@condition Blinded|XPHB} in this way you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions.
You do not suffer {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks due to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.
You add your Lucky Break die to the damage rolls of your weapon attacks.

entries: You can end this effect at any time by opening your eyes (no action required). Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Incredible Luck
entries: Your luck magnifies, granting you the following benefits:

items.name: Lucky Break Die Improvement
entries: Your Lucky Break die becomes a {@dice d8}.

items.name: Overflowing Luck
entries: When you are in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and roll a 1 or a 20 on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you regain one expended Lucky Break.

subclassFeature.name: Accidental Success
entries: Whenever you roll for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} and roll a 1 on the d20, you can expend one Lucky Break to turn it into a 20. You do not regain a Lucky Break from your Incredible Luck feature when you do so.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Urban Jungle
entries: {@i Become One with the City}

Druids of the Circle of the Urban Jungle regard cities as living ecosystems. Where others see lampposts and cobblestones, these druids see perches, tendons, and conduits. Embracing human structures as an extant part of nature, these druids embrace civil magic to take the forms of animate artificial objects.

entries.subclassFeature: Circle of the Urban Jungle Spells|Druid|XPHB|Urban Jungle|Spaghetti0Patreon|3|Spaghetti0Patreon

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Urban Jungle Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Urban Jungle Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. In addition, you can cast spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

entries.caption: Circle of the Urban Jungle Spells
rows: {@spell Alarm|XPHB}, {@spell Brickfall|Spaghetti0Patreon}, {@spell Bubbling Tar|Spaghetti0Patreon}, {@spell Locate Object|XPHB}, {@spell Mason's Touch|Spaghetti0Patreon}
{@spell Beacon of the Boulevard|Spaghetti0Patreon}, {@spell Wall of Stone|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Urban Lifestyle
entries: A lifetime spent in cities has granted you certain skills. You gain proficiency with one set of {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} of your choice, and you learn two common languages of your choice. In addition, when you take the {@action Study|XPHB} action while within a city, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the Intelligence check.

subclassFeature.name: Urbanshape
entries: You can assume special forms called Urbanshapes, transforming into seemingly mundane pieces of the urban environment. Whenever you use your Wild Shape feature, you can use the {@creature Urban Element|Spaghetti0Patreon} or {@creature Urban Edifice|Spaghetti0Patreon} stat block instead of that of a Beast. Your Wild Shape feature is affected in the following ways when you assume an Urbanshape - it otherwise follows the normal rules for transforming into a beast.

items.name: Appearance
entries: You determine the appearance of your new form when you enter it, which must be that of some sort of object - typically a piece of street furniture, a lamppost or some other urban fixture. This choice will affect the form's size and the damage type of its Slam attack, as detailed in the stat blocks.

items.name: Urban Traits
entries: You know four Urban Traits of your choice that you meet the prerequisites for. The list of Urban Traits is detailed at the end of this subclass' description. You can exchange your selections for other eligible options whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you enter an Urbanshape, you can apply up to two Urban Aspects to the Urbanshape's form, which last while you remain in that form.

items.name: Unarmed Strikes
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} and take the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} option, you can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Strength for the saving throw DC.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Architecture
entries: Your Urbanshapes improve in the following ways.

items.name: Forceful Slam
entries: When you hit with your Urbanshape's Slam attack, you can choose to deal Force damage, instead of its normal damage type.

items.name: More Traits
entries: The number of Urban Traits you know increases to 6, and the number you choose when you enter an Urbanshape increases to 3.

subclassFeature.name: Constructed Cover
entries: The constructed nature of your Urbanshapes grants special protections to your allies or yourself. Your Urbanshape improves in one of the following ways, depending on your form.

items.name: Urban Element
entries: If you don't move on your turn, you gain {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} until you next move.

items.name: Urban Edifice
entries: Your allies within 5 feet of you can use your form as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

subclassFeature.name: Metropolis Avatar
entries: When you enter an Urbanshape, or as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while you are in one, you can enhance your Urbanshape for 1 minute, granting the following benefits. Once you enhance your Urbanshape in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend a level 6+ spell slot (no action required) to use it again.

items.name: Shifting Form
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or as part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to activate this feature, you can change your current Urbanshape to another, allowing you to change which stat block you are using and/or your current Urban Traits. You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} as normal when changing forms in this way, but cannot benefit from the Urban Edifice's Extra Temporary Hit Points trait.

items.name: Urban Potency
entries: Your Urban Traits improve, as denoted by their Potency effect.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Chimera
entries: Druids of the Circle of the Chimera are touched by a vile corruption, granting them the power to transform into twisted fusions of nature's creations. The forest dreads the appearance of their accursed forms.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Chimera Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Chimera Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. In addition, you can cast spells from this feature while you're in a Wild Shape form.

subclassFeature.name: Chimeric Wild Shape
entries: You can transform into unsettling fusions of different beasts. Whenever you use your Wild Shape, you can select two different beasts, instead of one, transforming into a monster embodying traits of both creatures. Your Wild Shape is affected in the following ways when you transform in this way.

items.name: Primary Form
entries: When you transform, choose one of the forms to be the Primary Form. You gain the statistics of your Primary form as normal.

items.name: Secondary Form
entries: The other form serves as your Secondary Form. You gain the following elements of your Secondary Form: its senses, Speeds, Traits, actions, Bonus Actions and Reactions.

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: The number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} you gain changes to twice your Druid level.

items.name: Armor Class
entries: You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1).

items.name: Druidic Potency
entries: You can use your spell attack bonus and your spell save DC in place of any attack bonus or saving throw DC provided by your Wild Shape forms.

items.name: Appearance
entries: Your new form keeps your Primary Form's body and head, but gains characteristics of your Secondary, usually resulting in a two-headed beast.

subclassFeature.name: Chimeric Strikes
entries: You gain the following benefits while you are in your Chimeric Wild Shape form.

items.name: Hybrid Strikes
entries: If you take one of the actions provided by one of your Wild Shape forms, you can take an action provided by the other Wild Shape form as part of the same action. Neither of these actions can make use of Multiattack.

items.name: Magical Strikes
entries: Whenever you hit with an attack from a Wild Shape form, you can change the damage type to Force.

subclassFeature.name: Exotic Forms
entries: You are now able to incorporate non-Beast creatures into your Chimeric Wild Shape. Your number of Known Forms for your Wild Shape increases by 2, and certain monsters are added to the list of forms you can learn, shown on the Exotic Forms table. You can only use these forms as a selection for the Secondary Form of your Chimeric Wild Shape.

entries.caption: Exotic Forms
rows: {@creature Black Dragon Wyrmling|XMM}, {@creature Bronze Dragon Wyrmling|XMM}, {@creature Green Dragon Wyrmling|XMM}
{@creature Death Dog|XMM}, {@creature Giant Vulture|XMM}, {@creature Peryton|XMM}, {@creature Stirge|XMM}

subclassFeature.name: Chimeric Triad
entries: When you use your Chimeric Wild Shape, you can now choose three different forms, instead of two, allowing you to take elements of all three creatures at once. The third stat block is incorporated in the same way as the Secondary Form. Only one of your Secondary Forms can be an Exotic Form.
In addition, when you use Hybrid Strikes, you can now take one action from each of your forms.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Lycan
entries: {@i Tear with Fang & Sunder with Spellcraft}

Druids of the Circle of the Lycan perform foul, accursed rites to hijack their ability to Wild Shape, allowing them to transform into twisted hybrids of their normal forms and that of nature's creations. Often mistaken for lycanthropes, these outcasts rend their foes with sharpened fang and claw, in terrifying tandem with spellcraft.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Lycan Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of the Lycan Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of the Lycan Spells
rows: {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Primal Savagery|Spaghetti0Patreon}, {@spell Wrathful Smite|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Hybrid Form
entries: When you use your Wild Shape feature, after selecting which Beast you want to transform into, you can choose to turn into a hybrid between your normal form and that of the beast you chose. Using your Hybrid Form affects Wild Shape in the following ways.

items.name: Duration
entries: The duration of the transformation changes to 10 minutes.

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Druid level.

items.name: Game Statistics
entries: Your body changes in ways such that you gain the Beast's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Speeds}, its senses, its Traits, and its Actions, Bonus Actions and Reactions, but no other elements of its stat block.

items.name: Bestial Strikes
entries: When you make an attack from one of the Beast's Actions, Bonus Actions or Reactions, you can use your spell attack bonus instead of the normal attack bonus, and you can add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll, instead of the normal damage bonus. In addition, you can use your spell save DC in place of any DCs included in the stat block.

items.name: Spellcasting
entries: Shape-shifting in this way does not prevent you from casting your Druid spells.

subclassFeature.name: Hybrid Attacks
entries: While you are in your Hybrid Form, if you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action using one of your Bestial Strikes and don't use Multiattack, you can do one of the following as part of the same action.

items: You can take one additional action from the Beast's stat block. This action cannot benefit from Multiattack.
You can cast one of your Druid cantrips with an action casting time.

subclassFeature.name: Death Touch
entries: While you are in your Hybrid Form, whenever you deal damage with your Bestial Strikes, you can change the damage type to Necrotic.

subclassFeature.name: Accursed Growth
entries: Your lycanthropic transformation now causes an immense growth of new flesh, granting you the following benefits while in your Hybrid Form.

items.name: Growth
entries: When you transform you can choose to become Large. While Large, you can use your Wisdom modifier in place of your Strength or Constitution whenever you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} using one of those abilities.

items.name: Regeneration
entries: When you start your turn in your Hybrid Form, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Druid level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Spellcraft
entries: While you are in your Hybrid Form, whenever you take the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make a Bestial Strike that would normally require an action.
Starting at Druid level 18, you can make two Bestial Strikes with this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, instead of one.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Bark
entries: {@i Defend Forests with Martial Prowess}

Druids of the Circle of Bark typically hail from dense forests, nearly untouched by the outside world. Fiercely protective of their homes, these druids train to blend their primal magic with martial prowess, favoring close quarters combat to draw enemies into their spell effects. Legends tell of these warriors wading into battle with skin as thick as bark. In truth, they draw power from ancient trees to transmute matter into bark, both to protect themselves, and to encase any foe foolish enough to intrude on their lands.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Spells
entries: Your connection to this circle ensures that you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of Bark Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Barkskin Warrior
entries: Your primal connection to trees allows you to take on the form of a primal warrior, constantly producing thick bark. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, or as a part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to cast {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} or {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB}, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to enter your Barkskin Warrior form for 10 minutes. It ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or if you dismiss it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

items.name: Regenerating Bark
entries: When you enter the form, and again at the start of each of your turns, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Druid level (round up).

items.name: Spell Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the damage of spells you have cast, and your movement cannot be hindered by them.

items.name: Restricting Bark
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can encase the target in a brittle layer of bark, reducing its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If you hit the creature multiple times, the {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn.
In addition, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Restraining Bark
entries: Your Restricting Bark grows stronger and more debilitating. Once per turn when you use your Restricting Bark feature, you can force the target to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn, or until a creature within 5 feet of it uses its action to break it free. On a success, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is still reduced as normal.

subclassFeature.name: Reeling Roots
entries: Resembling the sturdy roots of a tree, you can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cause tendrils to shoot out from your body, drawing your enemies toward you. Choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1 creature). Each target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, a creature takes Bludgeoning damage equal to {@damage 2d8} plus your Wisdom modifier, is pulled up to 30 feet toward you and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. On a success, it takes half as much damage and is not pulled or {@condition Restrained|XPHB}.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Improvisation
entries: {@i Be Prepared for Anything at Any Time}

Warriors of Improvisation always expect the unexpected. They do not believe in carrying weapons, as there is always something usable for self defense in one's surroundings. These monks are just as likely to be seen striking foes with a ladder or a rope as they are with their fists.

subclassFeature.name: Improviser
entries: Your training has ensured that you are prepared for any scenario, regardless of the tools at hand. You are proficient with {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons}. Further, any object that isn't a Simple or Martial weapon counts as a Monk Weapon for you provided that it weighs between 1/5 lbs and 10 lbs.
When you pick up an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon}, it falls into one of two categories:

items.name: One-handed
entries: {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons} that are easily wielded in one hand, such as a chair leg or a piece of cutlery. These weapons have the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property for you. If the weapon weighs 2 lbs or less, it also has the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property for you, with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

items.name: Two-handed
entries: {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons} that require two hands to wield effectively, such as a bar stool, or a ladder. These weapons have the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property for you. If the weapon is 5 feet or longer on one of its sides, it also has the {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach} property for you.

subclassFeature.name: Improvised Weapon Adept
entries: Your quick wit and scrappy training allow you to use {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons} with impressive skill. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, select one {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Mastery} property each for One-handed and Two-handed {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons}, choosing from the following options:

items.name: One-handed
entries: {@itemMastery Nick|XPHB}, {@itemMastery Sap|XPHB} or {@itemMastery Vex|XPHB}.

items.name: Two-handed
entries: {@itemMastery Cleave|XPHB}, {@itemMastery Push|XPHB} or {@itemMastery Topple|XPHB}.

You can use the chosen Mastery property with any attack you make with an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon} of the appropriate category until you next finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

Alternatively, at the start of your turn you can expend 1 Focus Point to exchange one of your selections for another eligible option as you quickly adapt to a new weapon or a new set of circumstances (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Empowered Improvised Weapons
entries: You are able to extend the mystical energy of your Monk's Focus to {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons}. As a result, when you attack with an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon} you can change its damage type to Force.

The first strike you make with an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon} is infused with additional energy. The first time you deal damage with a particular object, you add one Martial Arts die to the damage roll. You can deal this damage no more than once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Quick Deflect
entries: While you are wielding one or more {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapons}, you can interpose them between yourself and your foes to protect yourself from harm. You can expend 1 Focus Point to use your Deflect Attacks feature without using your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, but the damage you reduce is halved (round up) when you do so. Each time you use this feature, the cost increases by 1 Focus Point, and it resets to 1 Focus Point at the start of your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improvised Weapon Master
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} and select {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery} properties with your Improvised Weapon Adept feature, you can now choose two properties each for One-handed and Two-handed Weapons instead of one. This affects your {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon} attacks in the following ways, depending on the weapon's category:

items.name: One-handed
entries: You select which of the two Mastery properties to use each time you make an attack with a weapon of this category. In addition, whenever you would make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with your Martial Arts or Flurry of Blows features, you can replace it with an attack with one of these weapons.

items.name: Two-handed
entries: Whenever you make an attack with one of these weapons, you can use both Mastery properties simultaneously.

subclassFeature.name: Way of Claw and Fang
entries: {@i Use Animal-Inspired Techniques in your Martial Arts}

The core inspiration for many martial arts styles is drawn from the ways that animals fight — the dance of prey and predation drives primal creatures to create highly practiced and specialized techniques. For this reason, several monasteries have been established deep in the Beastlands. Therein, monks commune with animals imploring them to share their offensive and defensive techniques, and then form what is learned into a new and unique martial arts style. Monks of this tradition are as varied as the animal kingdom itself, and often take on traits of the beasts they study. Some become stalwart like an elephant, while others become as nimble as a mantis.

entries.subclassFeature: Hand of Claw and Fang|Monk|XPHB|Claw and Fang|Spaghetti0Patreon|3|Spaghetti0Patreon

subclassFeature.name: Hand of Claw and Fang
entries: You have trained your hands to tear like a tiger's claw and gore like a bull's horn. When you deal damage with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can change the damage type to Piercing or Slashing, instead of the normal Bludgeoning.

subclassFeature.name: Forms of the Beast
entries: You have incorporated the fighting style of beasts into your martial arts, teaching you special techniques which you incorporate into your fighting.

items.name: Learning Techniques
entries: You learn two {@filter techniques|optionalfeatures|feature type=BT} of your choice, and you learn one additional technique of your choice when you reach levels 6, 11, 14 and 17 in this class. Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one technique you know for another.

items.name: Performing a Technique
entries: You can perform no more than one technique on a turn, and can perform your techniques a number of times equal to your Dexterity or Wisdom modifier (whichever is higher, minimum once). You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Heightened Awareness
entries: You have learned to channel the sharp eye of the eagle, the hair trigger of the rabbit and the empathy of the orangutan. You gain proficiency with one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}, {@skill Insight|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}.

In addition, when you fail an ability check using one of these skills, you can expend one Focus Point to roll one of your Martial Arts dice and add the result to the check's total, potentially turning it into a success.

subclassFeature.name: Mixed Techniques
entries: Your mastery over your {@filter bestial techniques|optionalfeatures|feature type=BT} has allowed you the ability to mix them together. You can now use two Forms of the Beast techniques on the same turn.
In addition, when you use your Uncanny Metabolism feature you regain all expended uses of your Forms of the Beast feature.

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Blackbelt
entries: You have truly mastered your animalistic techniques. Once on each of your turns, you can use one of your Forms of the Beast techniques without expending a use. Further, you are no longer limited in the number of techniques you can use on a turn.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Lightning
entries: {@i Move Like Lightning and make Electric Attacks}

You have trained the ways of lightning: a martial art style inspired by the element bridging the sky with the earth. Your training and practice have allowed you to transform your Focus into concentrated bursts of electricity, and have allowed your body to flow like arcs of lightning from dipole to dipole. Monks of this order are known for their explosive elemental offense and unparalleled mobility. The storming electrical power within these monks can lead to aggressive outbursts, which they aim to control through meditation.

subclassFeature.name: Arcing Current
entries: You have learned to connect the electrical fields of two creatures such that you can travel across them.

items.name: Polarization
entries: Once per turn, immediately after hitting a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or a Monk Weapon, you can spend 1 Focus Point to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Lightning damage to the target and electrically Polarize it. The target remains Polarized for 1 minute, until you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or until you Polarize another creature. Once per turn when you hit a Polarized creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Monk Weapon you can deal this extra damage again without expending a Focus Point.

items.name: Arcing Body
entries: When you use your Step of the Wind feature, you can Teleport from a creature within 5 feet of you to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a creature you can see, provided you are within 5 feet of a different creature when you do so. At least one of the creatures must be Polarized by you and neither of them can be behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}. You must expend movement equal to the distance between the two creatures to perform the Teleport; if you cannot move far enough on this turn to cover this distance, the Teleport fails. You can Teleport in this way no more than once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Lightning Redirection
entries: You have learned to allow external lightning to flow through your body, as water flows through a river. You can use your Deflect Attacks feature to reduce Lightning damage you take. You can do so even if the damage was not dealt via an attack - damage dealt in this way counts as a ranged attack for the purposes of redirecting the damage.

subclassFeature.name: Heightened Voltage
entries: The power of lightning has suffused your body, and become truly second nature to you. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage. In addition, when you Teleport using Arcing Body, you can deal Lightning damage to the Polarized creature equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

subclassFeature.name: Chained Arc
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can transform your body into lightning and flow through several creatures. You instantaneously move to pass through the spaces of any number of creatures without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, expending movement as normal and ending the movement in an unoccupied space. Each creature you pass through must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your Focus save DC or take Lightning damage equal to five rolls of your Martial Arts die. A creature takes half as much damage on a success. You then reappear in your new space.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Additionally, when you deal Lightning damage with this feature, or your Lightning Redirection or Heightened Voltage features, it now overcomes {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage.

subclassFeature.name: Leaping Lightning
entries: Immediately after you Teleport with your Arcing Current feature, you can transfer Polarization to the creature you appear next to. Further, you are no longer limited in the number of times you can Teleport on a turn.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of Might
entries: {@i Overpower Foes with Incredible Strength}

Warriors of Might prioritize physical strength over nimbleness. These Monks condition their bodies to become a weapon – unstoppable, and incapable of being physically overpowered. Mighty Monks are known for being forces to be reckoned with while unarmed, throwing their opponents around the battlefield and inflicting devastating damage.

entries.name: Designer's note
entries: This is a monk that relies on Strength instead of Dexterity. DMs, if a player is interested in this, you may want to forgo the Dexterity requirement for multiclassing and/or allow them to use their Strength for Unarmored Defense before level 3, as levels 1–2 are going to be {@i rough}.

subclassFeature.name: Hardened Muscles
entries: Your toned muscles are so physically hard that they resist incoming blows, and potentially buffet attackers.

items.name: Mighty Defense
entries: You can use your Strength modifier in place of Dexterity when determining the AC of your Unarmored Defense feature, and the damage reduction of your Deflect Attacks feature.

items.name: Abs of Steel
entries: Whenever you take Bludgeoning damage dealt by a natural weapon (such as a creature's horns) or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the attacker takes Bludgeoning damage equal to half your Strength modifier (rounded up, minimum 1 damage).

subclassFeature.name: Wrestling
entries: You have learned to incorporate your physical strength into your martial arts. Once per turn when you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using Strength, you can expend 1 Focus Point to augment it, depending on the effect you choose. You choose to do so after you hit the target or after it fails its saving throw.

items.name: Damage
entries: The attack deals extra damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

items.name: Grapple
entries: Until the start of your next turn, attacks made against the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} target have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

items.name: Shove (Push)
entries: Roll {@dice 1d4}. The target is pushed an extra number of feet up to five times the number rolled.

items.name: Shove (Prone)
entries: The target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Reflexive Strike
entries: When you use your Deflect Attacks feature and reduce the damage of an attack to 0, if you expend a Focus Point to redirect the attack, you can instead make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the attacker, if it's within reach.

subclassFeature.name: Potent Maneuvers
entries: Once per turn when you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} using Strength, you can apply two different effects instead of one. For example, you could {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} the creature with the same attack. If you use your Wrestling feature on that Strike, you can augment both effects with the same Focus Point.

subclassFeature.name: Might Incarnate
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can direct your Focus into bolstering your muscles, allowing you to perform supernatural feats of strength. For 1 minute, or until you end the effect (no action required), you gain the following benefits.

items.name: Hulking Strength
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} and damage rolls using Strength, and to the saving throw DC of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

items.name: Titan Wrestler
entries: You can use the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} options on creatures regardless of how much larger they are than you.

items.name: Mighty Leap
entries: Once per turn, you can expend 20 feet of movement to leap up to 60 feet.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you expend 5 Focus Points to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Warrior of the Wandering Blade
entries: {@i Attack in Tandem with a Floating Weapon}

Warriors of the Wandering Blade learn to invest part of their own spirit into non-living objects, granting them powers to learn more about those objects and animate them with spiritual energy. These Monks use this power to bond with weapons, which they telekinetically wield with finesse and grace, forming a double-threat on the battlefield.

subclassFeature.name: Object Affinity
entries: You are able to forge connections with objects to control them and learn more about them. You can cast the {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} spells without Verbal or Material components, though you can only cast {@spell Identify|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and their effects are altered in the following ways.

items.name: Mage Hand
entries: When you cast {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}, the spectral hand is {@condition Invisible|XPHB}, and it is only able to interact with objects.

items.name: Identify
entries: When you cast {@spell Identify|XPHB} and target an object, you can spend 1 Focus Point to also learn the last time the object was moved by a creature, how far it was moved, and you receive a mental image of that creature.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Weapon
entries: Over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can imbue part of your spirit within a Simple or Martial melee weapon you are holding, thereby making it your Spirit Weapon. The weapon remains your Spirit Weapon until you die, or until you imbue another one. While it is your Spirit Weapon, you have proficiency with it, and it becomes a Monk weapon for you; however, you must use your Martial Arts die for its damage rolls instead of its normal damage dice.

items.name: Floating Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you can expend one Focus Point to throw the Spirit Weapon into the air. When you do, the weapon begins to hover, flies up to 30 feet and attacks one creature you can see within its reach (see Attacks below). The weapon remains floating for 10 minutes, until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or until you call it back early (no action required). When the weapon stops floating, it flies toward you, and you can choose to wield it if you have a free hand. Otherwise, it harmlessly falls to the ground.

items.name: Attacks
entries: The weapon uses your bonuses to attack and damage, as if you were wielding it. In addition, you can make use of its {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Mastery} property.

While the Spirit Weapon is floating, whenever you make an attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, or as part of your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} through your Martial Arts or Flurry of Blows features, you can make the attack using the weapon. You can also make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} through the weapon's space.

items.name: Moving the Weapon
entries: Once on each of your turns, immediately before you make an attack with it, you can move the weapon up to 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Refined Control
entries: Your Spirit Weapon's movements are improved. You can now move the weapon freely during your turn, instead of only once. The total distance the weapon can move on a turn is equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

Furthermore, you can now use the weapon as a platform. You can mount or dismount the weapon by entering or leaving its space, costing you no extra movement. You can balance on top of it for as long as it continues floating, though you fall off if you have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. While balancing on it, you can spend 10 feet of movement to jump 30 feet, using it like a springboard. The weapon can't move, make attacks or do anything else while it's supporting you, and once you dismount it, it still can't move until the end of that turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Spirit Weapon
entries: While your Spirit Weapon is floating, it improves in the following ways.

items.name: Flanking Strike
entries: Once per turn when you make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against a creature, you can expend 1 Focus Point to grant yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll, provided your Spirit Weapon is floating within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes extra damage of the weapon's type equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

items.name: Spirit Rider
entries: While you are balancing on your Spirit Weapon, you can expend your movement to cause the weapon to move, effectively giving yourself a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.
When you reach Monk level 17, the {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} changes to be equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Destructive Trajectory
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while your Spirit Weapon is floating, you can expend 5 Focus Points to cause it to fly in a destructive path you describe that is no more than 60 feet long. If you are balancing on the weapon, you move along with it, and do not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. Each creature within 5 feet of the weapon's path must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@damage 5d12} damage of the weapon's type on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Truth
entries: {@i Solve Mysteries. Uncover Truth.}

Paladins that take the Oath of Truth charge themselves with the responsibility of uncovering deceptions, seeking truth and bringing wrongdoers to justice. Often employed as detectives and bounty hunters, these paladins relish the challenge of unfurling a great mystery. There is no greater reward to them than the satisfaction of the solve.

entries.name: Tenets of Truth
entries: These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Seek truth, and uncover injustices.
Never look the other way when you discover foul play.
Leave no stone unturned in your investigations.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: When you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Truth Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Seek Evidence
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to become vigilantly perceptive. For the next 10 minutes, you gain a +5 bonus to your Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}), Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Divining Smite
entries: Immediately after you deal damage to a creature with a Paladin spell, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to reverberate divination magic through the target to learn more about it. You learn two of the following pieces of information of your choice:

items: Its alignment and creature type.
Its condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, if any.
Its damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities}, if any.
Which of its ability scores has the highest and lowest saving throw bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Awareness
entries: You constantly emanate a feeling of clear-headedness and awareness. You and friendly creatures within your Aura of Protection cannot be {@condition Surprised|XPHB}. Furthermore, you can see all creatures in the aura, even if they have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Analytical Defense
entries: When a creature targets you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to analyze its attack pattern and attempt to evade. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attacks it makes against you until the start of your next turn, including against the triggering attack.

subclassFeature.name: All-Seeing Sentinel
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can grant yourself sight beyond sight. You gain the following benefits for 1 hour:

items.name: Truesight
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

items.name: Lie Detector
entries: If you hear a lie, you know it to be one.

items.name: Analytical Retaliation
entries: When the target of your Analytical Defense misses you with an attack, you can make one weapon attack against it, provided it is within reach (no action required). You then cannot do so again until the start of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Guile
entries: {@i Beguile your foes with Fey tricks}

A Paladin's sacred oath is incredibly personal and spiritually significant to the paladin - it is a deeply important and defining aspect of who they are. Nobody said they needed to be particularly serious though.

Paladins who swear the Oath of Guile are committed to solving problems through quick wit and trickery, drawing power from the same source as many fey creatures. They are particularly adept enchanters, beguiling and tricking others to act on their behalf on the battlefield.

entries.name: Tenets of Guile
entries: Paladins who swear the Oath of Guile tend to be chaotic by nature, but do share some loose tenets:

items: Don't take life too seriously.
Prove that nobody is untrickable.
If someone is helpful, always consider their angle.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Guile Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Silver Tongue
entries: You can empower your lies with supernatural credibility. When you make a Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check, you can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to grant yourself a +5 bonus to that check, and all subsequent Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks you make for the next 10 minutes (no action required). You must do so before you roll for the check.

subclassFeature.name: Enchanting Presence
entries: You can use your Channel Divinity to dazzle all those around you. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can force creatures of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way, the creature cannot willingly move further away from you. An affected creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of False Allegiance
entries: You constantly emanate beguiling magic which can cause your enemies to turn on one another.

If a creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you, it is more susceptible to your suggestions while within your Aura of Protection. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can command a creature in your aura that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you to make an attack against a different creature that you can see. The creature takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against the specified creature. If the target is not in range, the creature expends its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} doing nothing. The creature is able to perform this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} even if it is {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} by the effect causing it to be {@condition Charmed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Convincing Defense
entries: When you are targeted by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to cast {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB} without expending a spell slot, targeting yourself. You must do so before the attacker rolls the attack roll.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times up to your Charisma modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Embodiment of Guile
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can begin to evoke a fey presence that beguiles those around you. For the next hour, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Charm Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Overwhelming Guile
entries: Whenever you force a creature to make a saving throw against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw.

items.name: Supernatural Charm
entries: Creatures that have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition can be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you. However, such creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against your Charm effects.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Aura Farming
entries: {@i Cultivate an Undeniable Presence}
Paladins that swear the Oath of Aura Farming, also known as the Oath of Presence, conduct themselves with absolute confidence - their every action deliberate, and their composure unshakable.

Tales of these Paladins tell not only of their heroic deeds, but of the shock and awe that their mere presence evokes: both inspiring allies and unsettling foes. However, commanding such an aura demands careful cultivation. One that swears this oath must never drop their composure, for even a single public embarrassment can tarnish the aura they have spent a lifetime perfecting.

entries.name: Tenets of Aura Farming
entries: These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Let your enemies detect no weakness.
Cultivate your legend. Let it speak for you.
Never drop the veil.

subclassFeature.name: Aura Farming Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Aura Farming Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of Aura Farming Spells
rows: {@spell Circle of Power|XPHB}, {@spell Yolande's Regal Presence|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Show No Weakness
entries: When you roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to ensure that even your failures somehow enhance your reputation (no action required). For 1 minute or until you use this feature again, once per turn when you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can gain one of the following benefits, depending on the type of test.

items.name: Ability Check
entries: You fail with total confidence, smoothly pivoting to another approach. If the check was made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB}, {@action Influence|XPHB}, {@action Study|XPHB}, {@action Search|XPHB} or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you immediately regain the use of the action you spent to take it. You cannot take that action again on this turn.

items.name: Attack Roll
entries: You turn your missed strike into a calculated glancing blow, as though that had been your intention all along. You can activate the {@itemMastery Graze|XPHB} Mastery property, even if your weapon doesn't have that property.

items.name: Saving Throw
entries: Your assailant immediately regrets challenging your aura. You can deal Psychic damage to the creature that forced you to make the save equal to half your Paladin level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Imposing Presence
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to augment your appearance to be more imposing. For 10 minutes, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) and Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks, and creatures within 30 feet of you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks to observe anything other than you.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Awe
entries: When a creature starts its turn in your Aura of Protection or moves into it for the first time on a turn, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it has the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition (your choice) until the start of its next turn. On a success, the creature becomes immune to this effect for 24 hours.

subclassFeature.name: Power Through
entries: When a creature forces you to make a saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to temporarily ignore that effect as if you had never been targeted by it at all. You instead make the save at the end of your next turn, at which point you become affected by the effect, provided it is still ongoing and you are within range to be targeted.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Overwhelming Presence
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can imbue your Aura of Protection with your supernatural presence, granting the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Unshakable Composure
entries: When you take damage from a creature in the aura, it is reduced by your Charisma modifier (minimum 1 damage reduced).

items.name: Striking Presence
entries: When you hit a creature that is {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by you within the aura with an attack, that attack deals extra damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1 extra damage).

items.name: Supernatural Aura
entries: A creature with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition can still be {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by you while it is within the aura.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Heroism
entries: {@i With Great Power…}

Paladins that take the Oath of Heroism bind themselves specifically and emphatically to the protection of the innocent and those in need. They are known for their ideals of leadership and bravery, and have a reputation of being self-sacrificing to a fault when an innocent's life is in the balance. Stories of heroic paladins line the annals of history, told by those whose lives they saved.

entries.name: Tenets of Heroism
entries: These paladins share the following tenets:

items: Protect the innocent at all costs.
Never stand idly by as atrocities occur.
Set the example for your allies to follow.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Heroism Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Protect the Innocent
entries: When you see another creature take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend a use of your Channel Divinity and move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} in its direction. This movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, and if you end it within 5 feet of the creature taking the damage, a glimmering shield of force protects the creature, absorbing all the inciting damage for them. If the damage is caused by an area of effect and this movement causes you to move into the area, you become a target of that effect.

subclassFeature.name: Hands of Liberation
entries: When you use your Lay on Hands, you can now target any creature within your Aura of Protection. When you do, you can also provide one or both of the following effects to the target by spending 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from the pool for each effect; these points don't also restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The effects last until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Agility
entries: The creature's movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

items.name: Freedom
entries: The creature gains the benefits of the {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Bout of Heroism
entries: You have a store of heroic potential you can draw upon in moments of great need. At the start of your turn, you can choose to gain the following benefits until the end of the turn (no action required). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Savior
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 30 feet.

items.name: Steadfast
entries: You can take an additional {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn, which can only be used to cast a Paladin spell with a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} casting time, to use your Lay on Hands feature, or to take the {@action Help|XPHB} action.

subclassFeature.name: Legendary Hero
entries: Your boundless heroism shines in your finest hour, and no peril can outmatch your will to protect others. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can gain the benefits below for 10 minutes. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Diversion
entries: When a hostile creature starts its turn inside your Aura of Protection, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks against your allies (not including yourself) until the start of its next turn.

items.name: Font of Health
entries: You gain an additional pool of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} for your Lay on Hands feature containing 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Any remaining {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} from the pool vanish when this feature ends.

items.name: Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Treachery
entries: Paladins who swear the Oath of Treachery hold no trust in their dark hearts. To them, the convictions of others are vapid, vain and foolish. Only power and survival endure. They twist divine power into weapons of deceit and malice, and turn on companions as easily as enemies when betrayal offers the promise of greater strength.

entries.name: Tenets of Treachery
entries: Many of these Paladins once swore nobler oaths, only to cast them aside in pursuit of their dark desires. Consequently, these dark Paladins do not follow tenets in the traditional sense. Instead, they cling to these grim beliefs:

items: Your word is ash.
Trust is weakness. Exploit it.
Power is survival. Sacrifice all else to claim it.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Treachery Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Treachery Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Conjure Duplicate
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to create a perfect visual illusion of yourself in a space you can see within 30 feet of yourself, called your Duplicate. The Duplicate is intangible and doesn't occupy its space. This effect lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. The Duplicate is animated and mimics your expressions and gestures. While it persists, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Move
entries: When you move on your turn, you can also move the Duplicate up to 30 feet to a space you can see that is within 120 feet of yourself. The space can be that of another creature - if that creature is your size or smaller, its form appears to overlap with the illusion.

items.name: Distract
entries: When both you and your Duplicate are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against that creature, given how distracting the illusion is to the target.

items.name: Redirect
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack roll while the illusion is within 5 feet of you, you can roll {@dice 1d6}. If it rolls a 3 or higher, the attack automatically misses you and the illusion is destroyed, but this effect does not end. For the duration, you can re-conjure the Duplicate using your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to a space within 30 feet of yourself, though doing so does not extend the duration.

subclassFeature.name: Poison Strike
entries: When you cast your {@spell Divine Smite|XPHB} spell, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to infuse the strike with a deadly poison. The spell's Radiant damage changes to either Poison or Necrotic damage, and each of the spell's damage dice changes to a {@damage d12}. Furthermore, the target has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Treachery
entries: If a creature within your Aura of Protection misses you with an attack roll, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to force it to reroll that attack against a different creature of your choice that is within 5 feet of it, or a different creature within the attack's range that is also in your Aura of Protection. The attack is made with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if your Duplicate is occupying the space of the target.

You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Deceitful Escape
entries: You gain the ability to use treacherous magic to slip away from your foes. Immediately after you are hit by an attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain {@condition Invisible|XPHB} until the end of your next turn. If your Duplicate exists, you can also move it to a space within 60 feet of your new position as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

Once you use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Icon of Deceit
entries: You gain the ability to embody the very conceit of treachery, becoming an avatar of deceit. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Invisibility
entries: You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. You can suppress or resume the condition at any time (no action required).

items.name: Trickery
entries: When a creature within your Aura of Protection deals damage to you, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, provided you don't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. On a failure, it is affected by the {@spell Command|XPHB} spell (you choose which command it is affected by when it fails the save). Once a creature succeeds on its save against this effect, it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to it for 24 hours.

items.name: Wrath
entries: If you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll, on a hit, you gain a bonus to its damage roll equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +1).

subclassFeature.name: Aerial Explorer
entries: {@i Take to the Air and Explore the Skies}

A common fantasy of ground dwelling creatures is to take to the skies - an act of absolute freedom. You are one such dreamer, and have practiced the magic of manipulating air and wind to achieve this goal. With the aid of a piece of specialised gliding equipment, the skies are now gleefully yours to explore.

subclassFeature.name: Aeromancy Magic
entries: Your practice in Aeromancy ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Ranger level specified in the Aeromancy Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Glider
entries: You have constructed, found or inherited a gliding apparatus which can keep you aloft with the aid of aeromancy. The glider has an appearance of your choice, though your choice doesn't affect its game statistics.

At any time while you are more than 10 feet off the ground and are falling, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to begin Gliding until you reach the ground or you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. If you stop Gliding while in the air, you fall. Your glider can support little more than your own weight; you cannot Glide while you are encumbered or while you are wearing Heavy Armor. You also cannot Glide while you are {@condition Grappled|XPHB|Grappling} a creature, or have a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0. Gliding imparts the following properties on you:

items.name: Descent
entries: You descend 5 feet at the start of each of your turns, and again each time you make an attack. You ignore this property if you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}.

items.name: Movement
entries: On your turn you can move through the air as if you had a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, but you cannot ascend. You ignore this property if you have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB}.

items.name: Volitant Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can propel the strike with bursts of wind, causing it to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d6} when you reach level 11.

subclassFeature.name: Updraft
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can call on elemental wind to launch yourself up into the air. When you do so, you ascend 30 feet. You can halt this movement at any time. The distance you ascend increases when you reach certain levels in this class: to 45 feet at level 7, and to 60 feet at level 11.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once). You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Evasive Maneuver
entries: You can deftly maneuver your glider out of the way of incoming hazards. While you are Gliding, if you are targeted by an attack or are forced to make a saving throw by an area of effect, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to maneuver out of the way, moving 15 feet in a direction of your choice without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. One of the following effects occurs, depending on what you were targeted with. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Alternatively, you can expend a use of your Updraft feature to use it.

items.name: Attack
entries: If this movement causes you to move out of range of the attack, it automatically misses. Otherwise, the attack is made against you at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

items.name: Area of Effect
entries: If this movement causes you to entirely move out of the area, you are unaffected by it. Otherwise you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Strength or Dexterity saving throw you make to resist the effect on this turn.

subclassFeature.name: Soaring
entries: Your skills in aeromancy have grown tremendously, improving your Glider feature in the following ways.

items.name: Movement
entries: While Gliding, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet and you can now move freely in any direction, including upwards.

items.name: Maneuverability
entries: While Gliding, you can {@action Disengage|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, which can be part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to cast or move your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}.

items.name: Volitant Strike
entries: When you use your Volitant Strike, you can additionally push the target 10 feet directly away from you, provided the target is no more than one size larger than you. If the target is on the ground, it is pushed horizontally in a direction of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Aerial Dominance
entries: You now regain all expended uses of your Updraft feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, when you use Updraft, you can now launch yourself in any direction of your choice, not just upwards, and you can maneuver through the spaces of other creatures and objects unimpeded (but not through walls or structures).

subclassFeature.name: Bounty Hunter
entries: {@i Hunt Down Villains, Collect their Bounties}

Bounty Hunters are experts at tracking and capturing dangerous fugitives, a task they perform in exchange for lucrative bounties. Once set on a quarry, the hunter's every waking minute is devoted to their target, relentlessly hunting them down.

Depending on the nature of the bounty, these Rangers may employ tactics to capture their target alive to return them to the client, or to execute them on the spot. For both tasks, they utilise special tools, magic or some combination thereof.

subclassFeature.name: Bounty Hunter Spells
entries: Your training as a Bounty Hunter ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Ranger level specified in the Bounty Hunter Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Bounty Hunter's Tactics
entries: You are an expert at tracking down your quarries from far distances, and capturing them alive or dead. Your Favored Enemy feature improves in the following ways.

items.name: Designate Quarry
entries: You can target a creature with your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} spell even if you can't see it, and from any range, so long as it is on the same plane of existence as you. To do so, you must know what the creature looks like and either its name or an alias it goes by.

items.name: Kill or Capture
entries: When you move your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} onto a creature, you decide whether you intend to Kill or Capture the target. Your choice grants you certain benefits while that creature remains marked by the spell.

items.name: Restricting Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit the target of your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} with an attack, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition as ropes, vines or chains enwrap it. The grapple's escape DC is equal to your spell save DC. The condition ends early if the spell ends on the target.

items.name: Preserve Quarry
entries: If you see the creature marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can prevent it from dying, causing it to gain the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition instead, as if it had been knocked out (no action required).

items.name: Deadly Strike
entries: Once per turn when you deal damage to a creature with your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, the spell's damage increases by {@damage 1d6}.

items.name: No Escape
entries: While the creature marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} is {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB}, you always know its precise location, provided it is within 1 mile of you, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet.

entries.name: Flavor Suggestion
entries: While this subclass makes use of spells like {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} and magical abilities like Restricting Strike to represent the Bounty Hunter's particular brand of skills and arsenal, you might consider flavouring these abilities as a practiced skill in tracking your quarries, and traps and equipment you use to capture them.

subclassFeature.name: Expert Bindings
entries: Over the course of one minute, you can tie and bind a Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of you that is willing or has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. The material required to tie up the creature depends on its size: 1 foot of {@item String|XPHB} if it's Tiny, 15 feet of {@item Rope|XPHB} if it's Small or Medium, and 30 feet of {@item Rope|XPHB} if it's Large.

A creature bound in this way has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions until it is untied. A creature within 5 feet of it can take an action to free the target by making a successful Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Hunter's Arsenal
entries: You can cast one of the spells you have prepared with your Bounty Hunter Spells feature without expending a spell slot. Once you cast a spell this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, you are able to {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on one of these spells at the same time as concentrating on {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}. If you need to roll to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, roll for each spell separately.
Starting at Ranger level 15, this benefit extends to any Ranger spell you have prepared, not just your Bounty Hunter spells.

subclassFeature.name: Enhanced Tactics
entries: You can deploy skilled tactics against your quarry, enhancing your intent to kill or capture it.

You can use one of these benefits a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Alternatively, you can expend a level 1+ spell slot to use it again.

items.name: Restraining Strike
entries: When a creature fails its saving throw against your Restricting Strike, you can also give it the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition, which lasts until the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition ends on it.

items.name: Lethal Strike
entries: When you deal your Deadly Strike damage, you can increase the damage of {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} by a further {@damage 2d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Sole Focus
entries: When you target a creature with your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, or when you start your turn with it active, you can choose to become hyper-aware of the marked creature and its tactics. Until the start of your next turn, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make against its spells and effects, and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to any damage it deals to you.

This awareness comes with a cost: until the start of your next turn, you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks you make against any other creature.

subclassFeature.name: Hell Walker
entries: {@i Traverse and Explore Every Level of the Hells}

By birth, circumstance or choice, some mortals find themselves living, and surviving, within the varied and horrible landscapes of the Hells. Referred to as Hell Walkers, these Rangers adapt to their environment out of sheer necessity, learning to utilize the infernal powers of the plane, cavort with its denizens, and traverse its many layers.
At the height of their powers, Hell Walkers are the premier guides to the Hells, and are even capable of opening portals between its layers.

subclassFeature.name: Hell Walker Spells
entries: Your experiences traversing the hells ensure you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Ranger level specified in the Hell Walker Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Twisted Insight
entries: Your exposure to the dark denizens of the hells grants you insight into the ways their twisted minds work. You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Fiend Expert
entries: You know the {@language Infernal|XPHB} language. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks made against Fiends, and you and your allies within 30 feet of you cannot be {@condition Surprised|XPHB} by them.

items.name: Negotiator
entries: You can add your Wisdom modifier to Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks made to inspect and understand contracts, and to Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks made to negotiate a deal.

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Strike
entries: You draw power and experience from all the layers of the hells, which you infuse into your weapon strikes. Once per turn when you hit with an attack made with a weapon or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can cause the target to take an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of a type listed below and produce its associated effect.
When you reach Ranger level 11, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d6}.

items.name: Bitter Frost (Cold)
entries: You activate the {@itemMastery Slow|XPHB} Mastery property, in addition to any other Mastery property you activated with the attack.

items.name: Fiery Wrath (Fire)
entries: The target begins {@hazard Burning|XPHB}. A {@hazard Burning|XPHB} target takes the extra damage of this feature at the start of its turns, instead of {@damage 1d4}.

items.name: Toxic Corruption (Poison)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.
Starting at Ranger level 7, you can choose to deal Acid damage with this option, instead of Poison.

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Survivor
entries: You have become adept at surviving the various layers of the hells. Select one of the following options. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can exchange your selection for another.

items.name: Frozen Wasteland
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} caused by ice or snow, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} made to avoid or end any reductions to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

items.name: Blazing Heat
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage, and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid gaining {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels due to extreme heat. Your Ranger spells also ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.

items.name: Fetid Swamps
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Acid and Poison damage, and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Hell's Hunter
entries: When you use your Infernal Strike feature, you can briefly open a Tiny localised portal to one of the corresponding layers of Hell, creating a 20-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on the target.
