The target and each creature in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or take damage equal to your Ranger level and suffer an additional effect. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage only. The damage type is the same as your Infernal Strike selection, which corresponds to the secondary effect shown in the Hell's Hunter table below.

You can open a portal in this way a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also use it again by expending a level 2+ spell slot.

entries.caption: Hell's Hunter Table
rows: A target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn, as it is encased in ice. The condition ends early if a creature within 5 feet of it takes an action to free it.
A target gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, which lasts until the start of your next turn, as its body falters under the sweltering heat.
Until the start of your next turn, a target is unable to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, as a toxic shroud infests its person.
{@note When you take this option, the target of your Infernal Strike only makes one Constitution saving throw for both the Infernal Strike and the Hell's Hunter effects.}

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Guide
entries: You always have the {@spell Plane Shift|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it without a spell slot or a material component, provided the destination is one of the layers of Hell. Once you cast the spell this way, you can't cast it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Hellish Escape
entries: When you take damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to open a portal to a safe location within the Hells and transport yourself there, halving the triggering damage. While in the Hells, you are unable to see or interact with the plane you departed from. You return to the space you disappeared from, or the nearest unoccupied space, at the start of your next turn.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Jungleborn
entries: {@i Swing through the Jungle and Wrestle Mighty Beasts}

Jungleborn Rangers typically don't adopt their lifestyle by choice, rather by circumstance. These Rangers are raised in the jungle, often brought up and cared for by local animals, forcing them to adapt to the ways of the wild to survive. They attune themselves with the plants and animals of their home, taking on animalistic characteristics and learning to traverse the environment with ease.
Jungleborn are known for their primal and uncivilized behaviors, and for their primal magic, which allows them to treat any terrain as their own personal jungle.

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Speech
entries: Raised by animals, you have learned magic to aid you in conversing and cavorting with beasts. You always have the {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} and {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} spells prepared.
You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Lean Muscle
entries: Surviving in the jungle has forced you to hone your physical prowess, such that you can wrestle with powerful beasts and climb trees with ease. You gain proficiency with the {@skill Athletics|XPHB} skill. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency with a different skill available to Rangers at level 1 of your choice.

Furthermore, you can use your Dexterity score in place of your Strength score when you make Strength checks, and when determining the saving throw DC of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} when you take the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Shove} or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} options.

subclassFeature.name: Jungle Fury
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can channel your primal aggression into one of the following effects:

items.name: Savage Strike
entries: The target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the weapon's type.

items.name: Primal Bellow
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Primal Physicality
entries: The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next ability check or saving throw it makes against one of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} options before the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Vine Swing
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can create a spectral vine which emerges from above you and reaches down into your hand. The vine is 20 feet long and leads from you to a point you can see within its reach, and you use it to swing through the air to an unoccupied space within its reach without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. The vine then disappears.
If you are {@condition Grappled|XPHB|Grappling} a creature when you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the creature moves with you, but if you drag it along the ground, the Grapple ends.
You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Complex Swing
entries: When you use your Vine Swing feature, you can swing through the air in a complex arc before landing, and can interact with creatures on your path. The vine now lasts until the end of your turn or until you move out of its reach, and while it exists you can continuously swing anywhere within its reach without using your Movement.

If you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action while swinging in this way, you can make one additional attack, but cannot use it to make a weapon attack against a target you have already hit on this turn.

subclassFeature.name: Jungle Champion
entries: At the start of your turn, you can unleash your primal nature (no action required). You gain the following benefits until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fearless
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Unstoppable
entries: Each time you take damage, you can reduce it by an amount equal to half your Ranger level (rounded down).

items.name: Jungle's Assault
entries: You can use your Jungle Fury feature on each of your attacks, not just once per turn.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore a use of it by expending a spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: The Outback Warrior
entries: You're a true blue kinda bloke or sheila, a battler of the outback: a dry land of desert and brush which is filled with some of the most dangerous critters known to man. Where most would turn away from such a harsh inhospitable place, you've embraced it and called it your home, and doing so has hardened your resolve.

subclassFeature.name: Outback Magic
entries: When you reach a Ranger level specified in the Outback Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Outback Weapon User
entries: You have become an expert at using the {@item Whip|XPHB}, the {@item Boomerang|Spaghetti0Patreon} and the Knife ({@item Dagger|XPHB}), which are your Outback Weapons. When you choose your {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Masteries}, you can select one of these weapons for free.

When you make an attack with one of your Outback Weapons, you can do so using either your Strength or Dexterity (your choice) for the attack and damage rolls, its damage die is {@damage 1d8} and it gains special abilities:

items.name: Boomerang
entries: After you make a ranged attack with a {@item Boomerang|Spaghetti0Patreon}, it always returns to your hand, regardless of whether the attack hits or misses.

entries.name: Returning Strike
entries: As the weapon is returning to your hand, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make one ranged attack against any target that is nearer to you than the target of the original attack. The damage die for this attack is a {@damage d4} instead of a {@damage d8}.

items.name: Whip
entries: The {@item Whip|XPHB}'s reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Painful Lash
entries: While wielding your {@item Whip|XPHB}, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to lash a creature in its reach, who must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half and it cannot make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Knife
entries: Your Knife gains the {@itemMastery Sap|XPHB} Mastery property. If you activate it, you can't use any other Mastery property with it until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Intimidating Weapon
entries: While wielding your Knife, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to force a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Venom Wrangler
entries: You are experienced in dealing with venomous creatures and can brush off their attacks. You can cast {@spell Protection from Poison|XPHB} without expending a spell slot, and then can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

In addition, you can use your Dexterity score in place of Strength to determine the saving throw DC of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} when you take the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} option.

Further, immediately after a creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with a melee attack, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to attempt to {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} the creature.

subclassFeature.name: Outback Weapon Master
entries: You are an unparalleled master of outback weaponry. When you use the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} of one of your Outback Weapon User features, you can temporarily enhance it:

items.name: Boomerang
entries: You make two attacks with your Returning Strike, but not against the same target.

items.name: Whip
entries: When a creature fails its saving throw against your Painful Lash, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn and it cannot take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}. On a success, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half and it suffers no other effects.

items.name: Knife
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition from your Intimidating Weapon feature, the only actions it can take on its turn are {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB}.

You can enhance a feature in one of these ways a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Jolly Swagman
entries: When you gain one of the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to suppress the effects of that condition with your brash confidence and bravado alone. The suppressed condition resumes after 1 minute, or if you use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} again, provided that its duration has not expired in the meantime.

subclassFeature.name: Vanisher
entries: {@i Vanish… and Strike!}

You have an innate ability to hide in plain sight, seemingly disappearing in thin air as your body, clothing and equipment become totally transparent. You may have inherited this power from a fey parentage, learned it through magic later in life, or have found an artifact capable of making you translucent. Regardless of the power's origins, it has shaped you into a premiere spy, pickpocket or assassin - as you can't catch what you can't see.

subclassFeature.name: Invisibility
entries: You have developed a power within yourself to make your body completely transparent, allowing you to hide in plain sight.

items.name: Invisibility Dice
entries: You have a pool of three Invisibility Dice, which are {@dice d6}s. You regain one expended die when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and all expended dice when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
You add one additional Invisibility Die to the pool at Rogue levels 6 (4 dice), 9 (5 dice), and 17 (6 dice).

items.name: Vanish
entries: You can take the {@action Hide|XPHB} action even when you are within an enemy's line of sight by expending one Invisibility Die. When you do, you gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition for up to 1 hour, or until you are no longer Hidden.

items.name: Stay Hidden
entries: While you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition from Vanish, if you take an action that would end your invisibility, like making an attack, you can roll the expended Invisibility Die. If you roll above a 1, you stay hidden and {@condition Invisible|XPHB}. Each subsequent time you roll the die in this way, the number you must roll above to stay {@condition Invisible|XPHB} increases by 1.

items.name: Unseen Attacker
entries: When you deal your Sneak Attack damage while {@condition Invisible|XPHB}, you can add one of your Invisibility Dice to the damage roll. This does not expend the die.

items.name: Share Invisibility
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action you can expend one Invisibility Die to cast the {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spell on another willing creature.

subclassFeature.name: Disorienting Strike
entries: You gain the following option for your Cunning Strike feature, which you can only use while {@condition Invisible|XPHB}.

items.name: Disorienting Strike (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or believe you are right next to it. On its next turn, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 and it wastes the turn attacking the air around itself.

subclassFeature.name: Selective Translucency
entries: When you gain the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition or give it to an ally, you can choose any number of creatures that you can see to be able to see the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} creature, which appears to those creatures as a faint outline of its form.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Invisibility
entries: Your Invisibility feature improves.

items.name: Invisibility Dice
entries: Your Invisibility Dice become {@dice d10}s.

items.name: Vanish
entries: While you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition from this feature you can't be seen by creatures with {@sense Truesight|XPHB}. This benefit extends to creatures benefiting from your {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spell.

items.name: Share Invisibility
entries: When you use this feature to cast the {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spell, it is cast at a level equal to one third your Rogue level (round down).

subclassFeature.name: Unseen Striker
entries: Making an attack can no longer end the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition on you. In addition, when you deal your Unseen Attacker damage, you can add two Invisibility Dice instead of one.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Striker
entries: {@i Infuse Weapon Strikes with Elemental Power}

Elemental Strikers are thieves of nature's power, channeling fire's fury, water's grace, earth's strength, and air's swiftness. They wield these stolen gifts with style, turning every skirmish into a dazzling dance of elemental chaos.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Artifact
entries: You have found or created an artifact capable of storing elemental energy. The artifact is a Tiny object with an appearance of your choice that can fit within one hand. The artifact has the following properties:

items.name: Known Elements
entries: Select two elements from Air, Earth, Fire and Water. These are your known elements. You can change your selections when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Starting at level 9 you can select three options, and at level 13 you gain all four.

items.name: Elemental DC
entries: Effects produced by the artifact use your Elemental DC, which is equal to 8 plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and your Dexterity modifier.

items.name: Restoring the Artifact
entries: If you lose the artifact or if it is destroyed, you can gain a new one by communing with the elements over the course of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Energy Infusion
entries: When you use Sneak Attack while the artifact is on your person, you can change its damage type to match one of your Known Elements, as shown on the Elemental Damage Types table.

subclassFeature.name: Empowerment of the Elements
entries: While your Elemental Artifact is on your person, you can use it to enhance your other features with elemental effects, depending on your Known Elements:

items.name: Air
entries: When you use your Cunning Action to {@action Dash|XPHB}, you can boost your movement with a tailwind of rushing air. Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet for that action, and until the end of your turn you can move along vertical and liquid surfaces without falling.

items.name: Earth
entries: When you use your Steady Aim feature you can draw earth to your body, keeping you steady and protecting you. You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Rogue level (round up), which last until the start of your next turn. While you have these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you cannot be moved against your will or be inflicted with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Fire
entries: When you use your Cunning Action to {@action Disengage|XPHB}, you create an instantaneous burst of flame as you move. Each creature within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your Elemental DC or take Fire damage equal to {@damage 1d6} plus half your Rogue level (round up).

items.name: Water
entries: When you use your Cunning Action to {@action Hide|XPHB}, you can use the air's moisture to create a misty cloud. The cloud appears in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around you, its area is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB} and you can {@action Hide|XPHB} within it. It remains in the space you created it until the end of your next turn, and it disperses early if it is subjected to a strong wind.

subclassFeature.name: Infused Strikes
entries: When you use Energy Infusion to change your Sneak Attack's damage type, you gain access to an additional Cunning Strike option, depending on your choice of damage type.

items.name: Bludgeoning (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The ground in a 10-foot radius around the target becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for 1 minute or until you use this option again. The target must be on the ground when you use this option.

items.name: Cold (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fire (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you cause the target to catch on fire for 1 minute. The target takes {@damage 2d6} Fire damage at the start of each of its turns while on fire. The flame persists until a creature within 5 feet of the target takes an action to douse the flame, or it completely enters a region the flame cannot burn, such as a body of water.

items.name: Thunder (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, it is pushed 15 feet straight away from you by an intense current of air.

subclassFeature.name: Conflux
entries: You gain the following benefits.

items.name: Mixed Elements
entries: When you use Energy Infusion to change your Sneak Attack's damage type, you can choose to divide the damage dice as you wish between Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire and Thunder. If you use Cunning Strike and only apply Infused Strikes options, you can apply a third one. Starting at level 17, you can apply all four.

items.name: Elemental Casting
entries: You can cast the following spells without the need for components or expending a spell slot: {@spell Control Water|XPHB}, {@spell Fire Shield|XPHB}, {@spell Fly|XPHB} and {@spell Stone Shape|XPHB}. Dexterity is your spellcasting ability for these spells. Once you cast a spell in this way, you can't cast it or any of the other options again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Elemental Assault
entries: When you use Energy Infusion to change your Sneak Attack's damage type, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around the target, other than the target itself, must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Elemental DC. On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 3d6} damage of one of the damage types you chose as it is assailed by earth, water, fire or air. On a success, it takes half as much damage.

subclassFeature.name: Scoundrel
entries: {@i Stack the Odds and Escape the Consequences}
Swindling, sweet talking and sneaky, you convince your marks that you are, in fact, extraordinarily lucky. Of course, the less they know about your loaded dice and the ace up your sleeve, the better.

Scoundrels are Rogues known by the public for their con-artistry and by the authorities for their elusiveness. Despite their perceived self-interest, they work best as part of a team. With partners at their side, they seamlessly plan and improvise schemes, splitting their winnings and encouraging tight teamwork.

subclassFeature.name: High Roller
entries: You have cultivated skills that allow you to win games of chance and skill - both legitimately and by cheating. You have proficiency in two kinds of {@item Gaming Set|XPHB|Gaming Sets} of your choice, and you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} when making checks with {@item Gaming Set|XPHB|Gaming Sets} with which you are proficient.

In addition, whenever you fail a Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check, you can re-roll the check, and must use the new roll. You can re-roll a check in this way a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Run!
entries: Sometimes, when your cheating gets found out, talking your way out of the situation isn't an option, and the only appropriate way to save your skin is to escape. You gain the following benefits:

items.name: Quick Dash
entries: When you use your Cunning Action feature to {@action Dash|XPHB} or {@action Disengage|XPHB}, you can move an extra 10 feet before the end of your turn.

items.name: Crowd Cover
entries: You can attempt to {@action Hide|XPHB} behind creatures that are your size or larger, and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check if you do so amongst a crowd of two or more creatures that are your size or larger and are within 5 feet of each other.

items.name: Disorient Pursuer
entries: When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Partner in Crime
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can designate one willing creature within 30 feet to be your 'Partner in Crime', a confidant that aids you in your exploits, and whom you aid in return. This creature continues to be your Partner in Crime until you designate a different creature, until another Rogue makes it their Partner in Crime or until you die.
While you and your Partner in Crime are within 30 feet of each other, you both gain the following benefits:

items.name: Silent Speech
entries: You can communicate with each other silently so long as you can see one another, using subtle gestures to convey your meaning.

items.name: Mutually Helpful
entries: You can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, but only to aid one another.

items.name: Watch their Back
entries: When the other creature fails a saving throw, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to allow them to re-roll the saving throw, taking the new result. You can each use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} once, and regain its use after finishing a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Exceedingly Slippery
entries: You have become extraordinarily difficult to pin down. The {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition no longer imparts {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your weapon attacks. In addition, when you use the Withdraw option of your Cunning Strikes feature, you can automatically end all instances of the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions on yourself.

subclassFeature.name: Tag-team Attack
entries: When you take the {@action Help|XPHB} action to give your Partner in Crime {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on an attack roll, or vice versa, if the attack hits, the target takes an additional {@damage 3d6} damage of the attack's type, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks against both of you until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Meta-Gambler
entries: {@i Roll the Dice With Fate}

To you, there's nothing more thrilling than a gamble - laying it all on the line for potential reward is more than a hobby - it's your calling. Whether by study, chance or some supernatural encounter, you have acquired magical abilities which permit you to gamble on your own actions. Perhaps you are a chosen of a God of Luck, or perhaps still, you sought out this power in an attempt to sate your unquenchable thirst for the gamble. Whatever your origin, you have much to gain by utilising these powers, but you will quickly find it is fickle, and the dice will not always roll in your favor. Gamble Responsibly!

subclassFeature.name: Gambler
entries: You have proficiency with two {@item Gaming Set|XPHB|Gaming Sets} of your choice. Whenever you make an ability check with a {@item Gaming Set|XPHB} with which you're proficient, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB}.
In addition, when you use your Cunning Action feature, you can make the action you take more potent by introducing an element of risk.

items.name: Dash
entries: Roll {@dice 1d6}. On an even number, you can move an extra number of feet equal to five times the number rolled as part of this action. On an odd number the number of feet you can move as part of the action is reduced by five times the number rolled.

items.name: Disengage
entries: Creatures can still make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you, albeit at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. However, if an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} misses you on this turn, the attacker takes Force damage equal to your Rogue level.

items.name: Hide
entries: You can attempt to {@action Hide|XPHB} even if you are not obscured, seemingly vanishing into thin air. You cannot add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to your Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check to {@action Hide|XPHB} when you do so.

subclassFeature.name: Raising the Stakes
entries: You have gained the ability to magically manipulate chance and elevate the stakes of your own actions. When you roll for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} with which you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, you can roll an additional d20, and take the highest result. However, if any of the dice roll a 1, the result of the roll becomes 1. You must choose whether to use this feature before you make the roll. Attack rolls made in this way are considered to be made at {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} for the purposes of triggering your Sneak Attack.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses after finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Gambling Strike
entries: You have learned to magically gamble on the potency of your own weapon strikes. You gain the following Cunning Strike Option.

items.name: Gambling Strike (Cost: 2d6)
entries: Before you roll damage for the attack, roll {@dice 3d6}. If two of the dice roll the same number, you can add the three dice together and add double the result to the attack's damage roll. If all three dice roll the same number, you instead add triple the result.

subclassFeature.name: Ace Up Your Sleeve
entries: You can use your gambling magic to prepare a contingency plan, which you can activate at a moment's notice when the timing is just right. Over the course of 10 minutes, which can be part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can take the {@action Ready|XPHB} action in a special way. When you do, the trigger you specify can occur any time before the end of your next {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, instead of before the start of your next turn. You lose the readied action if you use this feature again.
For example, you could use this feature to take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action when a creature moves within 5 feet of an ally, or the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action when you are targeted by an attack.

subclassFeature.name: Nudge Fate
entries: You have learned to cheat fate by subtly nudging the mechanisms of chance in a certain direction. Whenever you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you rolls for a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can manipulate its d20 roll. You can change the die's result to one of the three adjacent faces of the d20 of your choice. For example, if a d20 with standard arrangement rolled a 6, you could change the result to a 16, 14 or 9.
Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
For reference if you are playing without physical dice, the following is the standard d20 arrangement.

entries.name: DM Advice for Loaded Dice
entries: DMs, if you do not wish to share the actual number rolled on your d20 when a player uses 'Loaded Dice', it is recommended that you either tell the player their options for the modified roll, or let them choose between 'highest', 'lowest' or 'middle' to maintain ambiguity.

subclassFeature.name: Life Sorcery
entries: {@i Summon a Lifelong Companion}

The power to create life is typically one reserved by the gods, and even then, only of certain stations. But occasionally, following unintended divine intervention or perhaps a cosmic accident, a mortal individual is instilled with life-creating magic. These sorcerers carry a spark of Life, and are able to harness this magic to heal wounds, restore life to the lifeless, and to create new life, whole cloth from nothingness. When such a sorcerer casts a summoning spell, they have great latitude to form their creation into strange and unique forms, limited only by their magical prowess and their creativity.

subclassFeature.name: Life Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Life Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

In addition, whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace the {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB} or {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB} spells in the table with a different spell that is of a level you can prepare from the following list: {@spell Summon Aberration|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Celestial|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Dragon|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Elemental|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Fiend|XPHB}, or {@spell Summon Shadowspawn|TCE}.

entries.name: Other Summoning Spells
entries: If you have access to other summoning spells from another source, with your DM's permission you can replace {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB} and {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB} with those spells, so long as they do not summon a Construct or Undead creature.

entries.caption: Life Spells
rows: {@spell Aid|XPHB}, {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB}, {@spell Goodberry|XPHB}, {@spell Summon Beast|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Bolster Life
entries: Life bursts forth from your soul, and you can magically share a portion of it with your allies and your creations. Whenever you cast a spell of level 1 or higher that targets one or more creatures, you can grant one of the targets a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d6} + your Sorcerer level.
Alternatively, whenever you summon a creature with one of your Life Spells, you can grant these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} to the summoned creature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Custom Creations
entries: Whenever you cast one of your Life Spells that summons one creature, you can augment its physical form in one of the following ways:

items.name: Arcane Strikes
entries: When it deals Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage, it can choose to change the damage type to Force.

items.name: Fortification
entries: The creature gains a bonus to its AC equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down).

items.name: Size Change
entries: The creature's Size increases or decreases by one category.

items.name: Water Adaptations
entries: The creature gains a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and can breathe underwater.

items.name: Wings
entries: The creature gains a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, growing wings to accomplish flight.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Custom Creations
entries: Whenever you use your Custom Creations feature to augment a creature you summon, you can now make multiple augmentations on the same casting, costing one Sorcery Point per augmentation beyond the first. You cannot select any augmentation more than once.

subclassFeature.name: Lifegiver
entries: When a creature within 60 feet of you that you can see takes damage that would reduce it to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to spare that creature with the magic that flows through your body. The creature suffers no effects of being reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, and immediately regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} up to half its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point total}.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, unless you spend 7 Sorcery Points to restore its use (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Calamitous Sorcery
entries: {@i Channel Calamity and Cause Devastation}

When cataclysms occur, whether magical, artificial or natural, a huge amount of energy is drawn and expended, usually in a devastating and spectacular show of destructive power. On occasion, some of this destructive energy runs awry and gets stored, or trapped, within an individual.

Calamitous Sorcerers gain influence over the destructive powers that impacted their origin, and are known to wreak havoc and destruction. Whatever the circumstances of their origin, these sorcerers carry the consequences of this calamitous event with them, having fundamentally shaped who they have become.

subclassFeature.name: Calamitous Magic
entries: You've suffered a cataclysmic origin that has left you scarred forever. In its aftermath, you have found yourself in control of the dreadful power of {@filter Calamitous Spells|spells|class=sorcerer|damage type=acid;bludgeoning;cold;fire;force;lightning;necrotic;piercing;poison;psychic;radiant;slashing;thunder|Duration=[&Instant]}. These are any Sorcerer spells of Level 1 or higher that directly deal damage to one or more creatures and have a duration of 'Instantaneous'.

items.name: Free Preparations
entries: Select two Calamitous Spells that are of a level you can prepare. You always have the chosen spells prepared. You also select one additional Calamitous spell when you reach levels 5, 7 and 9 in this class. You can exchange one of your selections for another eligible Calamitous Spell whenever you gain a level in this class.

items.name: Calamitous Damage Type
entries: Select one damage type from Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison or Thunder. Whenever you cast a Calamitous Spell, you can change the damage type to your chosen type.

items.name: Calamitous Burst
entries: You know the {@spell Sorcerous Burst|XPHB} spell, which counts as a Calamitous Spell and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know. If you already know this spell, you learn a different Sorcerer cantrip of your choice. When you cast {@spell Sorcerous Burst|XPHB} and deal your Calamitous Damage Type, you can roll another {@dice d8} if you roll a 7 or 8 on a damage die for the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Explosive Spells
entries: When you roll damage for a Calamitous Spell and deal your Calamitous Damage Type, if any of the damage dice roll their maximum value, you can expend 1 Sorcery Point to infuse the spell with the devastation of your calamitous origin. Roll those dice again, and add the new rolls to the damage total. You can roll the dice again if they also roll their maximum value, adding their result to the total, and so on (no additional cost).

entries.name: Rules Note
entries: If you use a feature such as the Tempest Domain Cleric's 'Destructive Wrath' that allows you to automatically take the damage dice's maximum for a spell, Explosive Spells can't apply for that casting, since the dice were not actually rolled.

subclassFeature.name: Energy Barrier
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes a saving throw to avoid taking damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to send a wave of destructive energy to protect the target. Roll {@dice 3d6} plus your Sorcerer level. You can reroll the dice in the same manner as your Explosive Spells feature. The damage the target takes is reduced by an amount equal to the roll.

If the triggering damage is reduced to zero, the creature that created the effect takes damage of your Calamitous Damage Type equal to the remainder of the roll, provided it is within 60 feet of the target.

subclassFeature.name: Embodiment of Cataclysm
entries: You gain the harrowing ability to emulate the calamity that acts as the source of your power. While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Inescapable Wrath
entries: When you cast a Calamitous spell, you can change its damage type to Force, allowing you to affect otherwise {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} targets with it. You can still use your Explosive Spells feature when you do so.

items.name: Overwhelming Destruction
entries: When you cast a Calamitous spell with a spell slot of a higher level than the spell, you can add {@damage 1d8} per slot level above the spell's level to one of the spell's damage rolls.

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Sorcery
entries: {@i Master the Material and the Ethereal Planes}

Ethereal Sorcerers are beings split between two worlds: the corporeal world of the living and the Border Ethereal superimposed over it. The souls of these Sorcerers have been drawn across the two planes, perhaps by drawing lineage from some sort of ethereal being, or maybe resulting from some sort of arcane mishap. In any case, you are constantly flitting between these two worlds, perhaps not entirely willingly.

entries.name: Note on the Ethereal Plane
entries: In Forgotten Realms lore, the Ethereal Plane is only superimposed over the inner planes, meaning some features in this subclass may not work while travelling the outer planes. Players, you may want to consult with your DM as to whether this subclass is appropriate for your game.

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Magic
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Ethereal Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Ethereal Spells
rows: {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}, {@spell See Invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell Silent Image|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Shift
entries: Starting when you choose this origin, your body begins to shift back and forth to the Ethereal Plane, and you can use your momentary absence defensively. When you take damage of any type other than Force, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to that instance of damage.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and regain all uses after completing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Blink Master
entries: You have gained some control over which plane you occupy when you flit between the Material and Ethereal planes. When you cast the {@spell Blink|XPHB} spell you can choose to do so by expending 3 Sorcery Points instead of a spell slot. When you cast {@spell Blink|XPHB} in this way, you roll two d20s instead of one to determine whether or not you travel to the Ethereal Plane, and choose which one to use.

subclassFeature.name: Ethereal Banishment
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can attempt to briefly banish a creature you can see within 30 feet of you to the Ethereal Plane. The target must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it disappears and is transported to the Ethereal Plane until the end of your next turn, at which time it returns to the space that it left, or the nearest unoccupied space. Being on the Ethereal plane confers the following effects:

items.name: Visibility
entries: The target can see and hear the plane it originated from, which is cast in shades of gray, but it can't see anything there more than 60 feet away.

items.name: Incorporeal
entries: Creatures that aren't there can't perceive or interact with the target unless it has some special ability to do so, such as {@sense Truesight|XPHB}. The target cannot affect any creature that isn't also there.

items.name: No Reactions
entries: The target cannot take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, nor can it take the {@action Ready|XPHB} action.

Once you use this feature, you cannot do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, or until you expend 3 Sorcery Points to restore your use of it (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Planar Displacement
entries: When you activate your Innate Sorcery feature, your body shifts to and from the Ethereal Plane at high frequencies, giving you ghost-like properties while it is active:

items.name: Ghostly Travel
entries: You can move through solid matter as if it were {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and you take {@damage 1d10} Force damage.

items.name: Ethereal Sight
entries: You can see creatures on the Ethereal Plane up to a range of 60 feet and can affect them with your spells.

subclassFeature.name: Being of Two Planes
entries: When you cast {@spell Etherealness|XPHB}, in addition to stepping into the Ethereal Plane yourself, you can target a number of willing creatures up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one extra creature) to also be affected by the spell. Other affected creatures can use a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to end the spell's effect on themselves before the spell ends, but if you take an Action to dismiss the spell, it ends on all affected creatures.

subclassFeature.name: Sonic Sorcery
entries: {@i Control Vibrations and Manipulate Sound}

Your innate magic stems from the power of sound and vibrations. You or someone from your lineage may have drawn this power from the chaotic noise of Limbo, or perhaps your ancestor was the chosen of a god of Thunder.
Whatever the case, you are gifted with powers to create great thunderous booms, and to manipulate vibrations to confuse the mind, break down objects and negate sound entirely.

subclassFeature.name: Sonic Magic
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Sonic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Sonic Spells
rows: {@spell Dissonant Whispers|XPHB}, {@spell Shatter|XPHB}, {@spell Silence|XPHB}, {@spell Thaumaturgy|XPHB}, {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB}
{@spell Jallarzi's Storm of Radiance|XPHB}, {@spell Synaptic Static|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Resonation
entries: Your affinity for creating noise-based effects grants you the following benefits:

items.name: Sonic Spells
entries: When you cast a Sorcerer spell that deals damage, you can change its damage type to Thunder.

items.name: Violent Resonance
entries: When you cast a level 1+ spell that deals Thunder damage, you can tune the soundwaves to resonate within one creature that took the damage. Until the start of your next turn, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks, as violent vibrations rock its body.

subclassFeature.name: Resonant Soul
entries: You have become resilient to the vibrations that cause sound. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Thunder damage. In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Tremorsense
entries: You gain {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet, which counts as a form of sight when casting your Sorcerer spells.

items.name: Sonic Boom
entries: When a creature suffers the effects of your Violent Resonance, you can inflict Thunder damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) to the target and each creature of your choice within a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on it.

subclassFeature.name: Vocal Precision
entries: You can manipulate the sound waves of your voice such that it is inaudible except to one creature of your choice within 60 feet of you. Alternatively, you can make it such that all creatures within 300 feet can clearly hear it.

subclassFeature.name: Sonic Interference
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can amplify or mute the sounds of a creature of your choice within 60 feet of you for 1 minute. The effect ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, if you use it again, or if you end it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. An unwilling creature can avoid this effect by succeeding on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC, and it can repeat this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Select one of the following effects:

items.name: Constructive Interference
entries: Any sound the target makes is ten times louder. It automatically fails any Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check to not be heard and its attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Thunder damage.

items.name: Destructive Interference
entries: Any sound the target makes is entirely negated. It automatically succeeds on any Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check to not be heard, and it cannot speak, nor perform the verbal (V) components of spells.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Thunderous Ascension
entries: Your Resonant Soul feature improves, granting you the following benefits while your Innate Sorcery is active:

items.name: Echosense
entries: Your {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} now extends through air, and its range increases to 60 feet.

items.name: Sound Immunity
entries: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder Damage and to the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Sonic Explosion
entries: The size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of your Sonic Boom increases to 20 feet, and the damage increases by an amount equal to half your Sorcerer level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Spawn Sorcery
entries: {@i Spawn a Sorcerous Clone of Yourself}

You were not born; you were spawned as a feebleminded clone of a Sorcerer very much like yourself. A product of involuntary magical mitosis, you spent years serving your progenitor as a sort of apprentice, while your mind slowly matured. Eventually, you developed a will of your own and left them behind.
Now, you have spawned your own sorcerous offspring. It is both a helpful magical companion and a grave responsibility. In time, it will perpetuate this strange cycle.

subclassFeature.name: Sorcerous Spawn
entries: A pseudo-clone of yourself spawns off of your body, freshly born and ready to serve you. The spawn uses the {@creature Sorcerous Spawn|Spaghetti0Patreon} stat block, and has the appearance of an imperfect copy of yourself. The spawn is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It disintegrates if you die.

items.name: The Spawn in Combat
entries: In combat, the spawn shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} score, but acts immediately after your turn. It can move and use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} on its own, but the only action it takes is the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action unless you take an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to command it; allowing it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. If you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, the spawn acts on its own and isn't limited to the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action.

items.name: Restoring or Replacing the Spawn
entries: If the spawn has died within the last hour, you can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to touch it and expend a level 2+ spell slot. The spawn returns to life after 1 minute with all its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} restored. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can spawn a fresh {@creature Sorcerous Spawn|Spaghetti0Patreon}, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. If you already have a spawn from this feature, the old one disintegrates when the new one appears.

subclassFeature.name: Spawn Spellcasting
entries: Your Sorcerous Spawn has a limited capability to innately cast spells, just like you.

items.name: Prepared Spells
entries: Select three level 1 spells from the {@filter Sorcerer spell list|spells|class=Sorcerer}, which the spawn thereafter has prepared.
Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can exchange one of these spells with a different eligible spell.

items.name: Spell Slots
entries: The spawn has one level 1 spell slot. It regains all expended spell slots when it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: The spawn uses your Charisma modifier as its spellcasting ability for these spells. Similarly, it uses your spell attack modifier and your spell save DC.

items.name: Concentration
entries: The spawn's mind is too feeble to {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on spells. If it attempts to cast a spell that requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, the spell fails.

items.name: At Higher Levels
entries: The number of spells the spawn can prepare, the maximum level of those spells, and the number of level 1 spell slots it has all increase when you reach certain Sorcerer levels, shown on the Spawn Advancement table.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Investment
entries: When you use your Font of Magic feature to create a spell slot that is of a level your Sorcerous Spawn can prepare, you can grant that spell slot to the spawn, instead of yourself. The spell slot vanishes when it finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, as normal.

subclassFeature.name: Sacrificial Spawn
entries: You always have the {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB} spell prepared, and can cast it by expending 2 Sorcery Points instead of a spell slot.

When you cast the spell using this feature, the spell's school changes to Transmutation for that casting, as the duplicates are made of flesh, instead of being illusory. As a result, a creature is affected by the spell even if it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} or {@sense Truesight|XPHB}. Any remaining duplicates disintegrate when the spell ends.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Synchronicity
entries: While your Innate Sorcery is active, you form a magical link between yourself and your Sorcerous Spawn, which grants you the following benefits while you are within 60 feet of one another.

items.name: Roiling Arcana
entries: The spawn has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls using its Destructive Magic action, as well as any spell attacks it makes.

items.name: Spell Link
entries: Whenever you cast a spell, you can cast it as if you were in the spawn's space, briefly using its senses.

items.name: Magical Invigoration
entries: When the spawn casts a spell, you can treat the spell slot it used as if it was one level higher.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Maturation
entries: Your spawn's mind has matured, giving it normal mental faculties, granting it the following benefits.

items.name: Mental Scores
entries: Its Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma scores increase to match yours, unless they were already higher, and it gains all of your saving throw proficiencies using those abilities (if any).

items.name: Speech
entries: It can now speak, and it learns all of the languages that you know.

items.name: Concentration
entries: It is now able to {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on spells.

subclassFeature.name: Beastblood Sorcery
entries: {@i Unleash the Primal Savagery of the Beastlands}

Primal magic from the Beastlands has suffused you, granting you physical characteristics similar to the mighty beasts that populate the plane. Beastblood Sorcerers are known for mixing their spellcasting with savage attacks made with natural weapons that grow out of their bodies. Most Beastblood Sorcerers trace a direct lineage from the Beastlands, and are typically some kind of beastfolk, such as Aarakocra or Tabaxi, but members of other races have been known to take on this origin after some sort of magical encounter.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Spells
entries: Your connection to the Beastlands ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Bestial Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Bestial Spells
rows: {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Bestial Hide
entries: You are able to call on the resilient hide of your bestial ancestry. When you cast {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB} targeting only yourself, you can choose to do so by expending two Sorcery Points instead of a spell slot. When you do so, you additionally gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Sorcerer level plus your Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Primal Ferocity
entries: Your lineage to the Beastlands allows you to transform your body to become more bestial.

items.name: Primal Form
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, select one of the Primal Form options listed at the end of this feature. You gain the listed benefits until you next finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

items.name: Natural Weapon
entries: The primal form grants you a special way to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. You can use your Charisma modifier in place of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. You grow your natural weapon in a location on your body appropriate to its function: for example, claws would be grown on your hands, a horn would be grown on your head.

items.name: Appearance
entries: Your appearance is augmented by your transformation, embodying the traits of beasts you are drawing power from. For example, you might grow thick fur on your skin and fangs if you choose the Hunter form, or webbed fingers and gills for the Diver form. Your aesthetic choices do not affect your game statistics.

entries.name: Hunter (Level 3)
entries: You channel the traits of carnivorous beasts such as wolves, tigers and bears.

items.name: Natural Weapon
entries: Your Natural Weapon deals {@damage 1d8} Piercing or Slashing damage in the form of a bite or claws respectively (your choice).

items.name: Pack Hunter
entries: If you make an attack with your Natural Weapon against a creature and one of your allies is within 5 feet of that ally, you can activate the {@itemMastery Graze|XPHB} Mastery property on that attack.

entries.name: Defender (Level 3)
entries: You channel the traits of thick hided herbivorous beasts such as rhinoceroses, elephants and tortoises.

items.name: Natural Weapon
entries: Your Natural Weapon deals {@damage 1d6} Piercing or Bludgeoning damage in the form of a horn or a slam respectively (your choice).

items.name: Thick Hide
entries: When you use your Bestial Hide feature, your AC increases by a further +1 for the duration, and the amount of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} provided increases by an amount equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum +1). This AC bonus increases to +2 at level 6, to +3 at level 14 and to +4 at level 18 in this class.

entries.name: Diver (Level 6)
entries: You channel the traits of marine beasts such as fish, sharks and octopi.

items.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can breathe underwater.

items.name: Natural Weapon
entries: Your Natural Weapon deals {@damage 1d8} Piercing or Bludgeoning damage in the form of a bite or slam respectively (your choice).

items.name: Grappling Strike
entries: Once per turn when you take the Damage option for an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with your Natural Weapon, you can take the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple} option as well, as part of the same attack. You can use your Charisma for the saving throw DC of the {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Grapple}.

entries.name: Soarer (Level 14)
entries: You channel the traits of flying beasts such as birds and bats.

items.name: Aerial Adaptation
entries: You grow a pair of wings, granting you a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

items.name: Natural Weapon
entries: Your Natural Weapon deals {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage in the form of a bite or talons (your choice).

items.name: Flyby
entries: After making an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} with your Natural Weapon, your movement doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} from the target of the attack until the end of your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.
In addition, when you hit with an attack made with your Primal Form's natural weapon, you can change its damage type to Force, instead of its normal damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Pack Magic
entries: You have become attuned to the magical bond shared between bestial packs and can use its essence to enhance your spells. Whenever you cast a spell using a spell slot that targets an ally, that ally gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Sorcerer level (rounded down) plus your Charisma modifier. If the spell targets multiple allies, you choose one ally to gain the {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. While the creature has these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you.
In addition, you can now change your choice of Primal Form whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Chimeric Transformation
entries: Your body is so suffused with the primal magic of the Beastlands that you gain the ability to mix your primal forms together into a hybrid. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose two Primal Forms to embody, instead of one. You gain the benefits and the Natural Weapons of both options, and any special benefits that apply only to one of the Natural Weapons now apply to both.

subclassFeature.name: Ancient Dragon Patron
entries: You have made a pact with a particularly powerful dragon, gifted in the art of spellcasting from their centuries of life. The nature of a pact with a dragon will vary substantially on what kind of dragon is making the pact, but invariably a clause involves contributing to the dragon's hoard. Perhaps a metallic dragon sought you out to act in the capacity of a missionary, or maybe you delved into the far reaches of the world to find a gem dragon and had something to offer in exchange for psionic abilities. Most of the time, however, pacts are made with chromatic dragons, who enjoy stringing cultists along as part of their devious machinations.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Patron
entries: When you select this subclass, pick which type of dragon your patron is from the Draconic Patron Table. Several features in this subclass will refer to your patron's Kind and Damage Type.

subclassFeature.name: Patron Spells
entries: The magic of your otherworldly patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Draconic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed Draconic Spells prepared, as well as the spells of your Dragon's Kind: Chromatic, Metallic or Gem.

subclassFeature.name: Draconic Form
entries: Your patron grants you the ability to take on aspects of their draconic form. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed:

items.name: Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the damage type associated with your Draconic Patron.

items.name: Draconic Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The damage type is that of your Draconic Patron.

items.name: Limited Flight
entries: You have a limited capacity to fly. You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, but if you end your turn in the air, you fall.
You can transform twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Aspect of the Dragon
entries: You gain an aspect of your Draconic Patron, depending on their Kind:

items.name: Chromatic: Frightful Presence
entries: You gain the frightful imposition of your patron. When you enter your Draconic Form, you can force each creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns.

items.name: Metallic: Change Shape
entries: You gain the ability of metallic dragons to change their shape. You gain the {@optfeature Mask of Many Faces|XPHB} Invocation, which doesn't count against the number of Eldritch Invocations you know.

Starting at level 7, when you cast {@spell Polymorph|XPHB} on yourself, while you are in your new form you retain your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma scores and your ability to speak, but cannot cast spells.

items.name: Gem: Psionics
entries: You gain a limited form of telepathy, allowing you to communicate mentally. You learn the {@spell Message|XPHB} cantrip, which you can cast without components. {@spell Message|XPHB} does not count against the number of Warlock cantrips you know, and if you already know it you learn another Warlock cantrip of your choice.

Additionally, your patron teaches you the secrets of their Psychic Step. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of you. You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses after finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: True Draconic Form
entries: Your devotion to your Draconic Patron has allowed you to take on more of their traits. You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to their associated damage type and have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. When in your Draconic Form, you gain the following benefits, replacing the benefits you previously gained:

items.name: Immunity
entries: When you take damage of the type associated with your Draconic Patron, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to it until the end of the current turn, negating the triggering damage.

items.name: True Draconic Strike
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, you can deal extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The damage type is that of your Draconic Patron.

items.name: True Flight
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Wrath of the Dragon
entries: You are granted the privilege of calling on your Draconic Patron to rain destruction on your enemies. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, select a point you can see within 120 feet of you. From that point, in a direction of your choice, a portal opens through which your patron uses their Breath Weapon. The shape, saving throw and damage type depends on your Draconic Patron, as shown in the Patron Breath Weapon Table, using your spell save DC. The Breath Weapon deals {@damage 16d6} damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.
Once you use this ability, you cannot use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Optional rule
entries: If you have access to the stat block of your draconic patron, and it has access to a non-damaging breath weapon, that may be used instead, also using your spell save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Axiarch Patron
entries: {@i Create Perfect Order through Subjugation}

Paragons of justice and order, Axiarchs are powerful beings from the planes of Law. Whether they are a high ranking Modron, an angel of Arcadia, a powerful spirit of Acheron or an Inevitable, they value order, hierarchy and structure. Such creatures are serial delegators, forming a complex hierarchy of loyal subordinates.

As a result, these beings of law form finely drafted pacts with ambitious mortals to broaden their influence. In return, these Warlocks are granted powers to subjugate others into conformity, and to execute orders reliably and predictably - a finely tuned tool for their patron's use.

subclassFeature.name: Patron Spells
entries: The magic of your otherworldly patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Axiarch Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Axiarch Spells
rows: {@spell Command|XPHB}, {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB}, {@spell Sanctuary|XPHB}, {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Contract Expert
entries: Navigating the complexities of your pact grants you proficiency with the {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} and {@skill Investigation|XPHB} skills. If you already have either proficiency, you instead gain proficiency with a different skill that is available to Warlocks at level 1.

When you make an ability check with {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB} to bargain for or inspect a verbal or written contract, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with the check.

subclassFeature.name: Lawful Demand
entries: You are granted the ability to precisely subjugate others to your will. You can cast the {@spell Command|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot a number of times up to your Charisma modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
Furthermore, when you cast {@spell Command|XPHB} your command options improve in the following ways:

items.name: Approach/Flee
entries: The target takes the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, moving to an unoccupied space on the ground you mentally specify. It ends its turn when it reaches the target destination or can move no further. If you target multiple creatures, you can specify a different space for each target.

items.name: Drop
entries: You can mentally specify what the target drops, which can also include any single object it is carrying, even if it isn't holding it.

items.name: Grovel
entries: The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition immediately. On its turn, it does nothing.

items.name: Halt
entries: The target additionally can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Predictable Execution
entries: Your patron infuses your body and mind with reliability, such that you might better serve them. When you make a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can forgo rolling and choose to get a 12 (before adding modifiers).
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Greater Demand
entries: Your patron bestows a repertoire of subjugation magic upon you. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can select one {@filter Enchantment spell|spells|school=E|level=1;2;3;4;5} that is level 5 or lower, which can be from any class' spell list. You have this spell prepared until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Delegate
entries: Your patron grants you the power to delegate tasks to your inferiors, freeing your mind to focus on other matters. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can select one willing creature within 30 feet of you to be your subordinate for 1 hour.

When you cast a spell that requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, you can delegate the spell's mental load to your subordinate, causing it to {@status Concentration|XPHB|concentrate} on the spell for you, provided the following criteria are met:

items.name: Nearby Subordinate
entries: Your subordinate must be within 30 feet of you when you cast the spell.

items.name: Eligible Spell School
entries: The spell must be an Abjuration or Enchantment spell, or it must appear on the Axiarch Spells table.

items.name: Spell Level
entries: The spell must be cast at level 5 or lower.
Once you make a creature your subordinate, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Time Paradox Patron
entries: {@i Use Time Travel to Be Your Own Patron!}
You have been granted magical power by a version of yourself from the near future… who was granted magical power by a version of yourself from the near future… who was granted magical power…

Your magic is maintained by a powerful, yet fragile paradox made possible by chronomantic power of no discernible origin. This connection to your future self is blurry, and subject to the whims of a fluctuating future based on your present-day actions.

While your future self is a powerful ally for keeping you informed and prepared, you must also take on the daunting task of acting as patron for your past self. It can all get very confusing, but the one thing that's clear to you is: you must maintain the paradox.

subclassFeature.name: Paradoxical Mishap
entries: Several features in this subclass rely on a paradox you create to be upheld. If, for any reason, you fail to uphold a paradox, a paradoxical mishap occurs. The conditions that must be met to uphold a paradox are listed in a feature's text. When a mishap occurs, roll on the Paradoxical Mishap table to determine the effect.

entries.caption: Paradoxical Mishap
rows: You take a number of d8s of Force damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This damage cannot be reduced in any way.
You have the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.
You are unable to speak or cast spells with a Verbal component until the end of your next turn.
You are unable to use any feature that could potentially end in a Paradoxical Mishap for 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Paradox Spells
entries: The magic granted to you by your future self ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Paradox Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Paradox Spells
rows: {@spell Alarm|XPHB}, {@spell Augury|XPHB}, {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Mirror Image|XPHB}

entries.name: Messages from the Future
entries: This subclass includes spells that can put you in contact with deities, such as {@spell Divination|XPHB} and {@spell Commune|XPHB}. When you cast these spells, you instead contact your future self.

The DM still decides what your future self says, and chooses from what point in the future they contact you. Being from the future, your future self has specific knowledge of events to come, but the future is not set in stone; they cannot guarantee that any insights they give will remain true in your timeline.

subclassFeature.name: Alter the Past
entries: When you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, your future self can briefly appear and intervene, allowing you to reroll the test, and you must use the new roll. The roll either has a bonus equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum +2), or half as much (round up, you choose each time you use this feature).

On your next turn, you must take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to project your spirit back in time to aid your past self. If you only added half your Charisma modifier to the check, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} instead. If you fail to do so, you experience a Paradoxical Mishap at the end of the turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn. You can use it a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Temporal Maneuvers
entries: Your control over time has developed, granting you special chronomantic maneuvers. Once you use one of these maneuvers, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Predicted Positioning
entries: When you cast a spell or make an attack, you can choose to do so as if you were in another space that you can see. Mark that space - if you have not entered it by the end of your next turn, you experience a Paradoxical Mishap.

items.name: Time Loop
entries: On your turn, you can mark your current space (no action required). At the start of your next turn, you teleport back to the marked position. If the space is occupied, or otherwise uninhabitable, you don't teleport and experience a Paradoxical Mishap instead.

items.name: Warning
entries: When you are targeted by an attack, your future self intervenes, granting you a bonus to your AC equal to your Charisma modifier against that attack (minimum +1, no action required). Starting on your next turn, your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} becomes temporally locked for one round; if you use it, you experience a Paradoxical Mishap.

subclassFeature.name: Delayed Inevitability
entries: When you fail to meet the condition to prevent a Paradoxical Mishap, you can choose to delay the requirement to uphold the paradox until the end of your next turn. If you fail to meet the requirement again, you cannot delay it any further and you experience two Paradoxical Mishaps instead of one.

subclassFeature.name: Time Master
entries: Your Alter the Past feature improves.

items.name: Font of Time Travel
entries: You now regain one expended use of the feature when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, or when you use your Magical Cunning.

items.name: Greater Foresight
entries: When you use the feature, you now gain the bonus to all subsequent {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} you make until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Temporal Re-do
entries: You gain a new way to use your Alter the Past feature, in which your future self outright prevents you from taking some course of action. Immediately after you use your action or your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can use the feature to regain the use of that action, and any consequence of you having taken it is immediately nullified.

For example, if you used your action to cast a spell, and the spell's target succeeded on its saving throw, you could use this feature to prevent yourself from casting that spell, thereby restoring the action you used to cast it and the spell slot you expended, and nullifying any effects that casting the spell had.

You still gain the bonus to your {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} when using the feature in this way, and still must use your action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your next turn to uphold the paradox, as normal.

subclassFeature.name: The Mathemagician
entries: {@i Alter the Formulae of Spells}

Mathemagicians view the world through the lens of mathematics, seeing the complex formulae and equations that govern the interactions of both the physical world and magical spells. They use their knowledge of underlying mathematical principles to alter these functions, augmenting their spells.

subclassFeature.name: Calculation Savant
entries: You can determine the optimal way to perform a task by spending at least 1 uninterrupted minute performing mathemagical calculations. When you finish the calculations, you touch one creature and fill its mind with mathemagical knowledge of a task you describe for 1 hour or until it is targeted by this feature again. If the target makes an ability check to perform that task while it holds this knowledge, it adds your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1) to the check, and then the knowledge fades away.

You can perform the calculations for longer to optimize them further: the bonus increases by 1 for each additional 10 minutes of calculations. This extra bonus cannot exceed half your Wizard level (round up).

subclassFeature.name: Mathemagics
entries: You can use your mathemagical talents to alter an aspect of a Wizard spell that you cast in one of the following ways. You can apply an effect only once per turn. You can use one of these effects a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
