When you use your Arcane Recovery feature, you can regain up to half of your total uses (round up).

items.name: Fractalize
entries: When you roll damage for a spell, if you roll a 1 on any of the damage dice, you can use your Mathemagics to roll another die of the same type and add it to the damage for each 1 rolled. This process repeats if those dice also roll 1s, and so on.

items.name: Shift Origin
entries: When you cast a spell, you can use your Mathemagics to move its point of origin to a point you can see. The maximum distance the point can be from yourself is a number of feet equal to 10 times your Intelligence modifier (minimum 10 feet). If the spell lasts more than one round and would normally move with you, the spell's point of origin snaps back to your position at the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Mathemagics
entries: The following options are added to your Mathemagics feature:

items.name: Alter Geometry
entries: When you create a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}, {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} or {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} area of effect with a spell, you can use your Mathemagics to change the shape of that area of effect to one of the others. Use the Alter Geometry table to determine the new area of effect's range and size. For the purposes of using the table, consider the side length of a {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} to be equivalent to 2x the radius of a {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} (i.e. its diameter).

items.name: Infinitesimal Spell
entries: When you cast a spell with an Instantaneous duration that provides a saving throw to creatures in an area of effect, instead of creating that area you can use your Mathemagics to condense the spell's effects to an infinitely small iota and fire it at a single target. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature that would have been in the spell's area of effect. On a hit, the target is affected by the spell, and is considered to have failed its saving throw (though features like Legendary Resistance can still be used to change the outcome). On a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, roll any damage dice again and add them to the damage total, as normal for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. After the initial impact, the target is affected by the spell normally.

subclassFeature.name: Equation Vision
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can open your mind to seeing the world as a mess of arcane and mathematical equations. You gain the following benefits for 10 minutes, or until you end the effect (no action required).

items.name: Truesight
entries: You have {@sense Truesight|XPHB} to a range of 60 feet.

items.name: Equation Reading
entries: Whenever you fail a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to focus on the relevant equations and reroll it, and you must use the new roll.
Once you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Mathemagical Laureate
entries: You are now no longer limited in the number of Mathemagics effects you can use on a turn.

In addition, you gain two special Mathemagics options. These options are more complex and thus more taxing to use: once you use one, you can't use either option again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, though it doesn't count against the uses of your Mathemagics feature. You can restore its use by spending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

items.name: Complex Function
entries: When you cast a spell, you can use your Mathemagics to extend its effect into the imaginary domain for that casting, causing it to manifest through space in strange and unexpected ways. The spell can affect creatures in the Ethereal Plane, and you do not need a clear path to the spell's targets, allowing the spell to ignore {@variantrule Cover|XPHB} (including {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}) and any requirement to see a target. In addition, you gain a {@dice 1d6} bonus to attack rolls made with the spell, and its targets suffer a {@dice 1d6} penalty to their saving throws to avoid or end its effects.

items.name: Compound Function
entries: You can break down a complex spell into two simpler ones. When you cast a spell with a level 3+ spell slot, instead of producing the effects of that spell, you can use your Mathemagics to produce the effects of two other Wizard spells you have prepared. The new spells must be similar to the original: they must have the same spell school and the same casting time, and their combined levels must be equal to or less than the spent spell slot.

subclassFeature.name: Vitamancer
entries: {@i Manipulate the Energy of Life}

You have studied the inner workings of life, and can use this knowledge to bend vital energy to your will. While they lack the divine power to cast healing spells, Vitamancers use their power to augment their allies, summon forth new life and to rend vitality from their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Vitality Magic
entries: Your studies have revealed the intrinsic mechanisms of life in all of its forms. You have proficiency with the {@skill Medicine|XPHB} and {@skill Nature|XPHB} skills. If you already have either proficiency, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

Also, certain spells are added to the Wizard spell list for you, listed in the Vitality Spells table. When you gain this feature, and again whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one of these spells to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

subclassFeature.name: Manipulate Vitality
entries: You can manipulate the forces of life by drawing energy from living creatures, using Vitality Dice, which are {@dice d6}s.

items.name: Number of Dice
entries: You can harbor a number of Vitality Dice up to your Wizard level. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you have an amount equal to half your Wizard level (round up), regardless of how many you had before the rest.

items.name: Spending Limit
entries: The maximum number of Vitality Dice you can spend on a single effect equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

items.name: Capture Lost Life
entries: When you cast a spell with a spell slot, you can capture any lost life it causes. The first time that the spell deals damage to a creature, you gain one Vitality Die. If the spell targets a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|friendly} creature or summons one, you instead gain the dice the first time that creature deals damage to another creature, provided you are concentrating on the spell.
You can spend Vitality Dice in the following ways:

items.name: Amplify Harm
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with a Wizard spell, you can spend Vitality Dice to deal extra Necrotic damage to one of the spell's targets equal to one roll of the dice. You cannot use Capture Lost Life when you use this feature.

items.name: Transfer Life
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend Vitality Dice to heal one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to one roll of the expended dice.

subclassFeature.name: Life Link
entries: When you cast a spell that requires {@status Concentration|XPHB}, you can link your vitality with that of one willing creature affected by the spell. Until the spell ends on the selected creature, whenever either of you takes damage or regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to negate that damage or healing and cause the unaffected creature to take it instead. This damage bypasses {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

subclassFeature.name: Instill Resilience
entries: When you use your Transfer Life feature and spend at least 3 Vitality Dice to heal a creature, that creature's vitality is temporarily protected. Until the start of your next turn, the target has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage and its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum} can't be reduced.

subclassFeature.name: Vital Surge
entries: When you use either your Amplify Harm or Transfer Life feature, you can augment the effect by drawing on ambient vital energy. When you do, the Vitality Dice become {@dice d12}s, and the feature gains an extra effect:

items.name: Amplify Harm
entries: Each target of the spell cannot regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Transfer Life
entries: You can target more than one creature with the effect, spending Vitality Dice on each target separately. The total number of Vitality Dice you spend can exceed your Spending Limit, but you can't spend more than your limit on any single creature.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Moon
entries: {@i Adopt Animal Forms to Guard the Wilds}
Druids of the Circle of the Moon draw on lunar magic to transform themselves. Their order gathers under the moon to share news and perform rituals.

Changeable as the moon, a Druid of this circle might prowl as a great cat one night, soar over the treetops as an eagle the next day, and then crash through undergrowth as a bear to drive off a trespassing monster. The wild is in the Druid's blood.

subclassFeature.name: Circle Form
entries: {@note Alternate Wild Shape Variant: Substitute the level 3 Circle Forms feature with this feature. }
You can channel lunar magic when you assume a Wild Shape form, granting you the benefits below.

items.name: Bestial Traits
entries: Your number of Trait Points increases by 1.
In addition, there are certain {@filter Bestial Traits|optionalfeatures|feature type=BST} that only Druids with this subclass meet the prerequisite for, listed among the other Bestial Traits.

items.name: Major Beast Shape
entries: You can choose the {@creature Major Beast Shape|Spaghetti0Patreon|Major Beast} Shape stat block, instead of {@creature Tiny Beast Shape|Spaghetti0Patreon|Tiny} or {@creature Minor Beast Shape|Spaghetti0Patreon}.

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to three times your Druid level.
{@note See {@variantrule Alternate Wild Shape Rules|Spaghetti0Patreon}}

subclassFeature.name: Potent Bestial Traits
entries: When you assume a Wild Shape form, you have one additional Trait Point to spend on Bestial Traits. You can only use this Trait Point to contribute towards a Bestial Trait that costs more than one point.

optionalfeature.name: Swift Injector
entries: Whenever you enter your Brute form, you can cast one of the spells you have prepared with your Brutewright Spells feature as part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. The spell must only target yourself. Once you cast a spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Retained Intellect
entries: While you are in your Brute form, you can now add your Intelligence modifier to {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} using Intelligence as normal, you are no longer restricted in which spells you can cast, and you aren't restricted from using Mutagenic Shot.
This Upgrade requires you to attune to it in order to gain the benefit, as you would a magic item.

optionalfeature.name: Mass Augment
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can use your mutagens to augment each creature of your choice within 60 feet of yourself. Each target gains the benefits of your Mutagenic Shot (including your Augment Specialization) until the start of your next turn.
Once you use this action, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Barrier
entries: {@i Suggested forms: crate, scaffolding, door}
You gain the following action.

entries.name: Barricade
entries: Until the start of your next turn, you cannot move or be moved against your will. During this time, whenever an attack hits another creature within 5 feet of you, you can reduce the damage it takes by half (round down), and you take the same amount of damage (no action required). This effect ends early if you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Potency
entries: When you reduce the damage a creature takes using Barricade, the damage you take is halved.

optionalfeature.name: Climbable
entries: {@i Suggested forms: crate, ladder, scaffolding}
Your size can be Huge, instead of Medium or Large. Friendly creatures can climb your body without making an ability check. In addition, your Slam attack's range increases to 15 feet.

entries.name: Potency
entries: You can increase your size by one category, to a maximum of Gargantuan. Once per turn when you hit with a Slam attack, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d8} damage.

optionalfeature.name: Constructed Nature
entries: {@i Suggested forms: any}

You gain {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. Additionally, if you are targeted with the {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your Druid level (round up).

entries.name: Potency
entries: You also gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage.

optionalfeature.name: Fortification
entries: {@i Suggested forms: any}
You gain a +2 bonus to your AC, and to the saving throw DC of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

entries.name: Potency
entries: The bonus increases to +4.

optionalfeature.name: Hollow
entries: {@i Suggested forms: crate, dumpster, sewer grate}

Your form includes an internal space which can contain up to two creatures or objects that are of a size at least one category smaller than you, or one creature that is your size. For example, if you are Large, you can contain one Large creature or two Medium or smaller creatures.

When you successfully {@variantrule Grapple|XPHB} a creature, you can store it within this space. While there, it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition and has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} from outside effects. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against it. If the creature escapes the grapple or if you exit the form, it appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Potency
entries: Your internal space is toxic. Whenever a creature starts its turn there it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save it takes {@damage 3d12} Poison or Acid damage (your choice), or half as much on a success.

optionalfeature.name: Illumination
entries: {@i Suggested forms: streetlamp, traffic sign, beacon}

Your Urbanshape is capable of emitting {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB|bright light} in a 20 foot {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB} around yourself, and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB|dim light} to a further 20 feet. Once on each of your turns you can turn this light on or off (no action required). You also gain the following action. If you also have the Multiattack Augmentation, you can replace one of your Slam attacks with this action.

entries.name: Blinding Flare
entries: {@actSave con} DC equals your spell save DC, one creature of your choice in your {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB|bright light} {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB}. {@actSaveFail} {@damage 2d8} + your Druid level Radiant damage and it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

entries.name: Potency
entries: You can target each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB|bright light} {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB} when you use Blinding Flare.

optionalfeature.name: Multiattack
entries: {@i Suggested forms: any}
You can make two Slam attacks when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. You can replace any of these attacks with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Potency
entries: You can make three attacks instead of two.

optionalfeature.name: Roiling Tar
entries: {@i Suggested forms: barrel, pavement}
Your form overflows with tar. You can cast the {@spell Bubbling Tar|Spaghetti0Patreon} spell while in this form, and you can cast the spell without expending a spell slot once while in this form.

entries.name: Potency
entries: When you cast {@spell Bubbling Tar|Spaghetti0Patreon}, the spell is cast at one level higher than normal (maximum level 9).

optionalfeature.name: Safety Markings
entries: {@i Suggested forms: traffic cone, waste bin, traffic sign.}

Your appearance gives off the impression that danger is near. Creatures within a 10 foot {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB} of you have their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} halved, unless they have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Potency
entries: The {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB} increases to 20 feet, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, which can be part of the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} you use to change forms, you can force each creature of your choice in the {@variantrule Emanation|XPHB} to succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} dropped to 0. Creatures with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition succeed automatically.

optionalfeature.name: Unrestricted Movement
entries: {@i Suggested forms: any}
Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases to 30 feet.

entries.name: Potency
entries: You gain a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and can hover.

optionalfeature.name: Versatile
entries: {@i Suggested forms: A type of tool, weapon or ammunition}
You take on the form of a type of tool, a Simple or Martial weapon, or a piece of ammunition. Your choice provides the following effects.

entries.name: Tool
entries: Creatures that use you as a set of tools to make an ability check (potentially including yourself) gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1). (Potency: the bonus changes to be equal to your Druid level.)

entries.name: Weapon
entries: Your Slam attack improves. You can use the {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery} of the weapon you took the form of, the damage die increases to that of the weapon unless it is a {@dice d6} or lower, and you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls. (Potency: the bonus increases to +3).

entries.name: Ammunition
entries: If another creature fires you as part of a weapon attack, that attack gains a +1 bonus to the attack and damage roll. Furthermore, immediately after hitting or missing, you can choose to teleport back to the attacker. (Potency: the bonus increases to +3).

optionalfeature.name: Crane's Balance
entries: At the start of your turn you can enter a stance granting you improved balance and grace (no action required). Roll {@dice 1d4}. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a bonus to your AC and all ability checks and saving throws using Dexterity equal to the number rolled.

optionalfeature.name: Elephant's Stability
entries: At the start of your turn you can enter a powerful stance, planting yourself in place (no action required). Until the start of your next turn, you cannot be moved against your will or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength and Constitution saving throws.

optionalfeature.name: Falcon's Snatch
entries: When you hit a creature with a Monk Weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can use the Grapple {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} option as part of the same attack.

optionalfeature.name: Frog's Patience
entries: At the start of your turn you can enter an anticipatory stance, ready to strike incoming foes (no action required). Until the start of your next turn, when a creature moves to a space within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or a Monk Weapon against them. On a hit, you deal extra damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

optionalfeature.name: Lion's Roar
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can let loose a furious roar, shocking and intimidating your nearby enemies. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Focus save DC or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Mantis' Precision
entries: At the start of your turn you can enter a stance granting you enhanced precision in your strikes (no action required). Until the end of the turn, any attack you make with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or a Monk Weapon scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|critical hit} on a roll of 19 or 20, and you can roll one additional Martial Arts die when determining the extra damage for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|critical hit}.

optionalfeature.name: Monkey's Fling
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can make a ranged attack with a weapon with the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property or an {@variantrule Improvised Weapons|XPHB|Improvised Weapon} against a creature within the weapon's range. You have proficiency with this attack, and the weapon is considered a Monk Weapon when you make it. On a hit, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes within the next minute.

optionalfeature.name: Peacock's Dazzle
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can make dazzling and alluring movements with your body, confusing and beguiling your nearby enemies. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Focus save DC or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. While {@condition Charmed|XPHB} in this way, a creature cannot willingly move further away from you.

optionalfeature.name: Ram's Horns
entries: When you hit a creature with a Monk Weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can use the Shove {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} option as part of the same attack. If the creature fails its saving throw you can push the creature up to 15 feet away, instead of the usual 5 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Rhino's Charge
entries: When you move at least 20 feet in a straight line toward a creature, you can use this technique to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next attack you make against them before the end of your turn with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} or Monk Weapon. If that attack hits, it deals extra damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

optionalfeature.name: Snake's Strike
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can prepare your body, as if coiling like a snake, to make a single, devastating strike. Instead of making your attack(s) as normal, you make one attack with a Monk Weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, adding your Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) to the attack roll. If you have the Extra Attack feature, you can only make one attack as a part of this action, but if the attack hits you deal extra damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die for each attack you sacrificed.

optionalfeature.name: Tiger's Pounce
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can leap up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. If you land within 5 feet of a creature, you can make an attack with a monk weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|unarmed strike} against it as a part of the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die.

optionalfeature.name: Wolf's Teamwork
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use this technique to distract the target, allowing an opening for an ally to strike. The next attack roll made against the creature before the start of your next turn is made with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. You cannot benefit from this {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Aggressive (1 Trait Point)
entries: Your Bestial Strike deals an extra {@damage 1d10} damage on a hit.

optionalfeature.name: Aquatic (1 Trait Point)
entries: Choose one of the following.

entries.name: Amphibious
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet, and you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. In addition, you can breathe both air and water.

entries.name: Marine
entries: You can only breathe underwater, and you have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} of 50 feet. Your normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 5 feet.

entries.name: Swimmer
entries: You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Armored (1+ Trait Points)
entries: You gain a +2 bonus to your AC.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The bonus increases by 1 for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Blindsight (1+ Trait Point)
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to 30 feet.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} increases by 15 feet for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Charging Strike (1+ Trait Points)
entries: If you hit a creature that is your size or smaller with your Bestial Strike and moved 30+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the target, taking the Shove option (no action required).

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The attack also deals an additional {@damage 1d8} damage for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Climber (1 Trait Point)
entries: Choose one of the following.

entries.name: Grip
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and you have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} that is equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can climb difficult surfaces, including along ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

optionalfeature.name: Cold Adapted (1 Trait Point)
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage, and your movement isn't reduced by moving over ice or snow.

optionalfeature.name: Diminutive (1 Trait Point)
entries: Your form is extremely small, making you difficult to notice. Other creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made to notice or spot you, and you can fit through spaces as narrow as half an inch.

optionalfeature.name: Flight (2+ Trait Points)
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 40 feet, and your normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half.

entries.name: 3+ Trait Points
entries: You don't provoke an {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} when you fly out of an enemy's reach.

optionalfeature.name: Grappling Strike (1+ Trait Points)
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your Bestial Strike, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the target, taking the Grapple option (no action required). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB} in this way, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

optionalfeature.name: Huge (1+ Trait Points)
entries: Your Size is Huge. Your Strength score increases to 21 (+5), you gain a +2 damage bonus to your Bestial Strike attacks and the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} you gain increases by an amount equal to your Druid level.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} you gain increases by 10 for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Knockdown Strike (1 Trait Point)
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with your Bestial Strike, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against the target, taking the Shove option (no action required).

optionalfeature.name: Multiattack (1+ Trait Points)
entries: When you use your Bestial Strike, you can make two attacks, instead of one. You can replace any of these attacks with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: 3+ Trait Points
entries: You can make three attacks instead of two.

optionalfeature.name: Nimble Escape (1 Trait Point)
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Pack Tactics (1 Trait Point)
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your attack rolls against a creature if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the creature, and the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

optionalfeature.name: Pounce (1 Trait Point)
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can jump 20 feet by expending 10 feet of movement. If you immediately follow the jump with a Bestial Strike, you make the attack roll with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Standing Leap (1+ Trait Points)
entries: Your {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} is 20 feet and your {@variantrule High Jump|XPHB} is 10 feet, with or without a running start.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The jump distance increases by 10 feet for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Speedy (1+ Trait Points)
entries: Each of your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Speeds} increase by 20 feet.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by an additional 20 feet for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Spiny (1+ Trait Points)
entries: When a creature touches you against your will, hits you with a melee attack or starts its turn with you {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, it takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The damage increases by {@damage 1d4} for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Venomous (1+ Trait Points)
entries: Once per turn when you hit with a Bestial Strike attack, it deals an extra {@damage 1d8} Poison damage.

entries.name: 2+ Trait Points
entries: The damage increases by {@damage 1d8} for each Trait Point beyond the first.

optionalfeature.name: Web (1 Trait Point)
entries: You gain the following action.

entries.name: Web (Recharge 5-6)
entries: {@actSave dex} your spell save DC, one creature you can see within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the web is destroyed (AC 8 + your Wisdom modifier; HP equal to your Druid level; {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire damage; {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage).

spell.name: Primal Savagery (Revised)
entries: You channel primal magic to cause your teeth or fingernails to sharpen, ready to deliver a devastating attack. Make an attack with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}. On a hit, the attack deals Slashing or Necrotic damage (your choice) equal to {@damage 1d8} plus the modifier you used to make the attack, instead of the normal damage for the attack. After you make the attack, your teeth or fingernails return to normal.

If you have some kind of natural weapon that you can attack with, like a bite or claw attack, you can use that attack instead of an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} by temporarily augmenting those features.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Whether you deal Slashing or Necrotic damage, the attack deals extra damage of the same type when you reach levels 5 ({@damage 1d8}), 11 ({@damage 2d8}) and 17 ({@damage 3d8}).

spell.name: Guardian of Nature (Revised)
entries: A nature spirit answers your call and transforms you into a powerful guardian. The transformation lasts until the spell ends. You choose one of the following forms to assume: Primal Beast or Great Tree.

items.name: Primal Beast
entries: Bestial fur covers your body, your facial features become feral, and you gain the following benefits.

items: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet, and the distance you can jump with a Standing High or Long Jump increases to 20 feet, unless it was already higher.
You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 120 feet.
You make Strength- and Wisdom-based attack rolls with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
Your melee attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Force damage on a hit.

items.name: Great Tree
entries: Your skin appears barky, leaves sprout from your hair, and you gain the following benefits.

items: You gain 15 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.
You make Constitution saving throws with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.
You make Dexterity- and Wisdom-based attack rolls with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB|advantage}.
While you are on the ground, the ground within 15 feet of you is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for your enemies.

spell.name: Rip and Tear
entries: Your body briefly transforms, taking on aspects of a savage beast - your nails harden, your teeth sharpen, and your body becomes primed to pounce.

You leap up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and immediately make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of you. The leap does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. On a hit, the attack deals {@damage 4d12} Force damage.
You perform this leap and attack in this way up to four times in total. You can attack the same target more than once, but no two successive attacks can be made against the same target.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can leap and attack one additional time for each spell slot level above 5.

spell.name: Mason's Touch
entries: You subtly reshape stone or brick in a 5-foot square that is part of a structure, wall, street or some other surface. Choose one of the following effects.

items.name: Artistic Rendering
entries: You cause the surface to display a visual or tactile image, symbol or writing by subtly warping the surface.

items.name: Handholds
entries: You roughen the surface, making it more easily climbable. Creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to climb the surface.

items.name: Smoothen
entries: You fill in the seams and cracks in the surface, making it perfectly smooth. It cannot be climbed, except by creatures with {@spell Spider Climb|XPHB} or similar abilities.

spell.name: Brickfall

time.condition: which you take when you or a creature you can see within 90 feet of you falls

entries: You momentarily encase one falling creature's body in brick, and guide its swift path to the ground. You can move the target horizontally up to 15 feet, and the target has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to damage it takes from the fall. If the target lands on a creature, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take Bludgeoning damage equal to the falling damage roll and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. An object being landed on simply takes the damage.
The effects of this spell only last for the duration of the turn you cast it. If the target doesn't land on that turn, the effect is wasted.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Bubbling Tar
entries: You spew forth sticky tar in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} around yourself. Each creature in that area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become covered in tar for the duration, or until it or another creature within reach of it takes an action to scrape it off. However, the act of scraping the tar off a creature deals {@damage 3d6} Acid damage to it.

While covered in tar, a creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, and it cannot fly unless it can hover. If the tar isn't scraped off within 3 rounds, the creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 instead.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher Level Spell Slot
entries: For every spell slot level above 2, the damage increases by {@dice 1d6} and the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} grows in size by 5 feet.

spell.name: Urban Veil

components.m: a pinch of soot and a frayed thread

entries: You lay an illusory veil over a built structure that fits within a 40-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}, such as an alleyway, a wall, or the interior of a room. From outside, the veil visually appears as mundane urban clutter and shadows. Creatures within the area are {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB|heavily obscured} to creatures outside.

When you cast the spell, you can designate any number of creatures to be unaffected by it. These creatures can see through the illusion, and can see normally while within it. Whenever another creature enters the area for the first time on a turn, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, its mind cannot justify the discrepancy between what it sees and its surroundings - it fails to discern the illusion, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sight until it leaves the area. On a successful save, it sees through the illusion for the remainder of the duration.

spell.name: Sewer Passage
entries: You touch a pipe, allowing you to step into the undercity's conduits and emerge elsewhere along the same network. You instantly teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of a pipe that is part of the same network, at a location you describe that is within 1 mile.

If you cannot see the destination, you must succeed on an ability check using your spellcasting modifier or appear in a random location in the pipe network of the DM's choice. The DC is 10, but is modified using the following table. If the destination is more than 1 mile away, the check automatically fails.

rows: You have seen the destination before
You have drunk water from, or otherwise contributed to the pipe network at the location
The destination is behind Total Cover
The destination is inside a different building or structure

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher Level Spell Slot
entries: The total distance you can teleport increases by 1 mile for each spell slot level above 4. You can also bring one willing creature within 5 feet of yourself along with you for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Beacon of the Boulevard
entries: You kindle the city's guiding light, which radiates from you for the duration in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} of {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB|bright light}, which sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB|dim light} for a further 30 feet.

Whenever the {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB|bright light} {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} enters a creature's space and whenever a creature in the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} ends its turn there, you can cause one of the following effects, which lasts until the end of its next turn. Once a creature has been affected, it can't be affected again until the end of its next turn.

items.name: Respite
entries: The creature gains a +1 bonus to its AC, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet and it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Revelation
entries: The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 3d8} Radiant damage and it is outlined in light; while outlined, Attacks are made against it with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} and it can't benefit from the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition. On a successful save it takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher Level Spell Slot
entries: The Radiant damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 5.

spell.name: Instant Structure
entries: You instantly create a rudimentary structure at a point on the ground within range, constructed in any combination of wood, brick, clay and straw, arranged in a manner of your choosing, though it must fit within a 50 foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} and it cannot overlap with any existing terrain or structures. The structure is stable, even if it defies normal architectural practices, and lasts for the duration. You can adorn the structure with doors, stairs, windows, and any other built-in furnishings.

If any part of the structure occupies the space of a creature or object when it appears, the creature or object is shunted to the nearest unoccupied space. Each surface of the structure (walls, floors, ceilings, railings, etc.) has AC 15 and 30 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, regardless of material or thickness, and has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing a surface to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} creates a square hole that is 10 feet on a side.

If you maintain your {@status Concentration|XPHB} on this spell for its full duration, the structure becomes permanent and can't be dispelled, thereby consuming the Material component. However, the structure suddenly becomes subject to the normal laws of physics. Make a DC 15 Intelligence check, adding your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} if you have proficiency with {@item Mason's Tools|XPHB}; the DM may wish to set the DC higher if your design is particularly outlandish. On a failure, the structure instantly crumbles. If the spell ends early, the structure vanishes.

spell.name: Tar Pit
entries: You open up a square of ground up to 30 feet on a side which you can see within range and transform it into a roiling pit of sticky tar. The pit is 15 feet deep, and lasts for the duration. The spell fails if you target a floor which is not deep enough to contain the pit.

Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a successful save, the creature can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} to an unoccupied space that is outside of the pit. If this movement fails to get it out of the area, or if it fails the save, it falls into the pit.

When a creature enters the pit, or if it starts its turn there, it becomes covered in tar for the spell's duration, if it wasn't already. While a creature is covered in tar, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, it cannot fly unless it can hover, and it takes {@damage 6d6} Acid damage at the start of each of its turns. Provided it isn't in the pit, the creature, or another creature within reach of it, can take an action to scrape off the tar, ending the effect.
When the spell ends, the pit closes and creatures and objects within it are safely pushed upwards to the newly reformed ground above.

spell.name: Rat-alanche
entries: You conjure forth a surging wave of innumerable live vermin, which crashes into a point you describe as a {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube}, which can be up to 30 feet to a side. Each creature in the area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d4} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 6d4} Necrotic damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, which it can't remove until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage only.
On your subsequent turns, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to create a new wave, which crashes into a new region you describe within range.

spell.name: Animate Infrastructure

components.m: a key that no longer opens any door

entries: You bring each non-magical man-made structure of your choice in range to life, animating them with complex movements. When you cast the spell, select one affected structure and choose one of the following effects. You can select another option as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your subsequent turns.
Other effects may be possible at the DM's discretion, depending on the structure's design - they decide the precise effects when the spell is used in this way.

items.name: Easy Passage
entries: Until the start of your next turn, each creature of your choice can move through the walls of the structure as it helpfully creates gaps in any direction the creature wishes to go.

items.name: Fling Debris
entries: The structure tears loose pieces of itself and hurls them. Choose up to three creatures you can see within 120 feet of the structure. Make a ranged spell attack against each creature, dealing {@damage 4d12} Force damage on a hit.

items.name: Grasping Architecture
entries: Beams, gutters, railings or similar features lash outward. Each creature of your choice within 15 feet of the structure must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. A {@condition Restrained|XPHB} creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on a success. A creature that is larger than the structure automatically succeeds on its save, unless it is the only target of the effect.

items.name: Shake off
entries: Each creature standing on or otherwise supported by the structure must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be flung 60 feet in a random direction.

items.name: Slam
entries: The structure slams, rends, or otherwise attacks a square region of its surface that is up to 60 feet wide. Each creature in the region makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d12} Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

spell.name: Awaken Sorcery
entries: You awaken the dormant innate magic within a creature. Select one cantrip from the Sorcerer spell list. For the duration, the target can cast that spell, using your spellcasting modifier.
This spell has no effect on creatures with one or more levels in the Sorcerer class. When the spell ends, any ongoing spell that it granted also immediately ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Instinctive Magic
entries: You release unshaped magic on instinct, choosing one of the following vague effects.

items.name: Destruction
entries: You hurl destructive energy at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d8} Force damage.

items.name: Protection
entries: You or one creature you can see within range gains {@dice 2d8} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

items.name: Movement
entries: You or one Large or smaller creature you can see within range is pushed by magical force in a direction of your choice. Roll {@dice 3d8}. The target is pushed a number of feet equal to the result. An unwilling creature can make a Strength saving throw to avoid being pushed.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can add {@dice 1d8} to the damage, {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB|Temporary Hit Point}, or push distance roll for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Arcane Node
entries: You touch a willing creature and implant a mote of magic, linking the target's essence to yourself. For the duration, you know the target's location relative to yourself, so long as it's on the same Plane of Existence as you. Furthermore, whenever you cast a spell, you can do so as if you were in the target's space, provided it is no more than 60 feet away from you, but you must use your own senses.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Energy Conversion

time.condition: which you take in response to taking Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning or Thunder damage from a creature that you can see within range

entries: Your body takes on a portion of harmful energy dealt to you, converts it into another form, and then fires it back at your assailant. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the triggering damage, and send unstable energy hurtling back at the creature that dealt you the damage. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 3d10} damage; the damage type is your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning or Thunder, but cannot be the same type as the triggering damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Repelling Beam
entries: You fire three beams of concentrated energy at targets you can see within range. Make a ranged spell attack against each target. On a hit, a target takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage and is pushed 10 feet away from you.

If you fire multiple beams at a single target, you make a single attack roll against that target instead of several, adding the damage dice together for the damage roll and adding the distance it is pushed together. In addition, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a {@dice d20} roll of one lower for every two beams combined.

For example, if you fire all three beams at a single target, the damage roll changes to {@damage 3d12}, the target is pushed 30 feet on a hit, and you would score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a {@dice d20} roll of 19 or higher.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You fire one additional beam for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Obfuscate Magic

time.condition: which you take when you see a creature within range cast a spell

entries: Select one active spell, of which its effects are entirely within range. If you cast this spell as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, the target spell must be the triggering spell that is being cast. All visible and audible effects of the spell become invisible and inaudible for the duration. In addition, both this spell and the target spell's effects are obscured from divination spells, such as {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, that are cast at level 3 or lower.
This spell ends immediately if the target spell deals damage to a creature or causes one to make a saving throw.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell's effects are obscured from divinations that are cast at a level equal to or lower than the spell slot used to cast this spell.

spell.name: Sorcerous Explosion
entries: Roiling arcane energy erupts in a 20-foot radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on a point you can see within range. When you cast the spell, you select the type of damage dealt by the eruption: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, Psychic, or Thunder. Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d8} damage of the type you chose on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

If you roll an 8 on a {@dice d8} for the damage roll, you can roll another {@dice d8} and add it to the damage, rolling additional {@dice d8|d8s} if any of those roll a 8, and so on. This effect is not triggered if an ability causes you to automatically roll the die's maximum value.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Redirect Spell

time.condition: which you take when a creature within range targets you with a spell that isn't an area of effect

entries: You allow the triggering magic to flow through your body and out again at a different target. Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability, with a DC equal to 10 plus the spell's level. On a success, select one creature you can see within range - that creature becomes the target of the spell, instead of you. If the spell required an attack roll, you make a ranged spell attack in place of the caster.

spell.name: Destructive Sacrifice
entries: You open the floodgates of your innate magical power in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on yourself, unleashing devastation. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 6d12} Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice) and can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save it takes half damage only.
When you cast this spell, you can choose to expend one or more of your Hit Dice, to a maximum of the spell's level, and add those dice to the damage roll.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases by 10 feet for each spell slot level above 6.

spell.name: Consult Ancestry
entries: You enter a meditative state, looking deep within the magic of your bloodline to communicate with one of your ancestors. Select one deceased figure from your ancestry that you know of. Alternatively, you can blindly reach out to an ancestor you aren't aware of, which is selected by the DM.

Your consciousness enters into an illusory world appropriate to your ancestor, and a manifestation of your ancestor appears before you. You are then free to engage in conversation with your ancestor for the duration. The ancestor knows your name and that you are their descendant, but is not privy to your deeds. Otherwise, they know everything they knew at the time of their death.

While you are consulting with your ancestor, you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition and a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0, and your senses other than touch are cut off from the outside world. You can end the spell early at any time (no action required). Once the spell ends, you can't use it to contact the same ancestor again for 24 hours.

spell.name: Arcane Liberation
entries: You flex your mastery over arcane magic, allowing you to break some of the normal rules of spellcasting for the duration.

You can cast more than one spell using spell slots during the same turn, and your spells no longer require a clear path to their target. Furthermore, if a spell would normally require you to see a target, you can ignore that requirement, provided you know where the target is through some other method.

spell.name: Avatar of the Self
entries: You unleash the truest essence of your innate magic, becoming an awe-inspiring representation of the source of your magic. You gain the following benefits for the duration.

items.name: Spectral Form
entries: Your size changes to Gargantuan, as your body floats within the center of an enormous semitransparent spectral creature with an appearance of your choice. Your Strength score increases to match your spellcasting ability's score, unless it was already higher.

items.name: Temporary Hit Points
entries: You gain 120 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. These points vanish when the spell ends.

items.name: Arcane Sight
entries: You have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} and {@sense Truesight|XPHB} to a range of 60 feet.

items.name: Concentration
entries: Concentrating on this spell does not prevent you from concentrating on another spell. If you need to roll to maintain {@status Concentration|XPHB}, roll once; if you fail, both spells end.

items.name: Potent Spells
entries: Your spells become supernaturally potent. When you cast a spell that you have prepared, you can apply one of the following effects.

items: If the spell deals damage, you can add {@damage 4d6} to one of its damage rolls.

If the spell inflicts a condition, you can cause it to bypass its targets' {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to that condition. A target that would otherwise be immune has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any saving throw it makes to avoid or end the spell's effects.

If the spell deals damage, you can cause it to bypass its targets' {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to damage types it deals. A target that would otherwise be immune has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}.

items.name: Reversion
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can suppress the other benefits of this spell until you use another {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to resume them. When you resume the spell, the {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} return to the amount they were when you suppressed the effect.

hp.special: you continue to use your Hit Points and Hit Point Dice

trait.name: Leaping Object
entries: Immediately before you use your Slam attack, you can fly a number of feet equal to five times your Wisdom modifier (minimum 5 feet) toward the target without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Limited Spellcasting
entries: While you are in this form, you can cast the spell you have prepared with your Circle of the Urban Jungle Spells feature.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While you are motionless, you are nearly indistinguishable from a normal object of your appearance. A creature can discern your true nature by succeeding on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC as part of the {@action Study|XPHB} action.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hitYourSpellAttack your spell attack modifier}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage (choose when you enter the form).

hp.special: you continue to use your Hit Points and Hit Point Dice

trait.name: Extra Temporary Hit Points
entries: The number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} you gain when you enter this form increases to equal three times your Druid level.

trait.name: False Appearance
entries: While you are motionless, you are nearly indistinguishable from a normal object of your appearance. A creature can discern your true nature by succeeding on an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC as part of the {@action Study|XPHB} action.

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hitYourSpellAttack your spell attack modifier}, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 2d8} + your Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage (choose when you enter the form).

type.note: Creature of your size and type

hp.special: 4 + four times your Sorcerer level (the spawn has a number of Hit Dice [d6s] equal to your Sorcerer level)

trait.name: Physical Clone
entries: The spawn shares the following traits of yours. This trait does not confer any temporary bonuses or effects you experience to the spawn.

items: Your size, creature type, and Speeds.
Your Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores, as well as your proficiencies in saving throws using those abilities (if any).
All of your senses, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.
Your Species traits. For these traits, treat the Spawn's level as equal to half your Sorcerer level (round up).

action.name: Destructive Magic
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hitYourSpellAttack your spell attack modifier to hit}, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target it can see. {@h}{@damage 1d6} + your Charisma modifier Force damage. This damage increases by {@damage 1d6} at Sorcerer level 10.

baseitem.name: Boomerang
entries: Any creature proficient with the {@item Javelin|XPHB} is also proficient with this weapon.

entries.name: Special
entries: On a miss, the Boomerang returns to the thrower's hand.

variantrule.name: Alternate Wild Shape Rules
entries: Wild Shape is an iconic feature for the Druid class, but it suffers from design issues that can make it un-fun to use. This is especially true of the Circle of the Moon subclass, which is the only subclass expected to use it in combat. Following are some common grievances.

items.name: Scaling
entries: Wild Shape forms don't scale with your level. There is little difference between turning into a {@creature Brown Bear|XMM} at level 3 versus level 20, aside from {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}. This is most frustrating as it pertains to proficiency: you use the beast form's {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, which quickly falls behind your own. Even for utility, Wild Shape loses value over time.

items.name: Balance
entries: Circle of the Moon is poorly balanced. At level 3, it has extremely high power, gaining access to strong forms with high damage and multiattack. This power drops off quickly (see Scaling), and by mid-levels you struggle to hit, as your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} hasn't kept pace.

items.name: Diminishing Options
entries: Because of poor scaling, Moon Druids at higher levels are pushed toward the few available high-CR beasts, which aren't much better than lower-CR options.

items.name: Bookkeepin
entries: You must search through the Monster Manual for beast stat blocks and have them on hand whenever you use Wild Shape.

entries.name: The Alternate Approach
entries: This document uses templates in place of monster stat blocks, which are customizable via options called Bestial Traits. This approach addresses the above issues by ensuring your options grow with you, using your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and increasing the number and power of traits available to you as you level up. And since the options don't diminish in power, your list of viable forms don't diminish either.
By designing specifically with the Druid in mind, balance is much easier to achieve, and everything fits within just a few pages.

entries.name: Ways to use these rules
entries: There are a few ways I recommend using these rules.

entries.name: As Written
entries: If you like them, you can simply replace the normal Wild Shape rules entirely.

entries.name: Circle of the Moon Only
entries: The official Wild Shape rules are mostly functional as a utility feature for non-Moon Druids. You may prefer to use these rules only for the Circle of the Moon subclass.

entries.name: Known Forms vs Known Traits
entries: {@filter This section contains quick-reference tables for building beasts|tables|search=Example Wild}. Instead of constructing forms from traits you know, you and your DM may limit your options to these tables.

When using this approach, you select a number of forms you know (rather than traits), based on the table below, and choose from the Example Wild Shapes tables. Some forms list additional optional traits in square brackets. If a form you choose has fewer Bestial Traits than your Trait Point budget, you can select those options, or spend excess Trait Points on traits with variable costs that the form already has.

entries.name: All traits known
entries: The purpose of Known Traits is to streamline decision-making. Choosing two options from six is faster than choosing from sixteen.

For greater flexibility, your DM may allow you to ignore Known Traits or Forms entirely and access the full list. This option is best suited to experienced players who can plan ahead without slowing the game down.

entries.name: Action Surge
entries: You gain one use of the {@classFeature Action Surge|Fighter|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature from the {@class Fighter|XPHB} class. When you use the additional action to take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can only make one attack. Once you use Action Surge using this benefit, you can’t use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

If you have two or more levels in {@class Fighter|XPHB}, you do not regain this extra use when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, but you are not restricted in the number of attacks you can make with this action.

entries.name: Channel Divinity
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Cleric|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature from the {@class Cleric|XPHB} class, gaining access to the Divine Spark and Turn Undead abilities. You have only one use of Channel Divinity that you can use to fuel these abilities, which you regain when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Your spellcasting ability for these effects is the ability increased by this feat, and you add that ability’s modifier to the Divine Spark roll instead of Wisdom (if applicable).
If you have two or more levels in {@class Cleric|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your number of uses of Channel Divinity by 1.

entries.name: Eldritch Invocation
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Eldritch Invocations|Warlock|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature from the {@class Warlock|XPHB} Class. You only learn one invocation of your choice from the list available to Warlocks at level 2, but your selection must have no other prerequisites. Your spellcasting ability for the Invocation is the ability increased by this feat. Whenever you gain a level, you can exchange your chosen Invocation with another eligible choice.
If you have two or more levels in {@class Warlock|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your number of Eldritch Invocations by 1.

entries.name: Instrument Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with one musical instrument of your choice.

entries.name: Bardic Inspiration
entries: You gain a number of uses of the {@classFeature Bardic Inspiration|Bard|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature from the {@class Bard|XPHB} class equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round up). Your Bardic Inspiration die is a {@dice d6}, and you regain expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If you have any levels in {@class Bard|XPHB}, you use your normal Bardic Inspiration die instead of a {@dice d6}. These extra uses are not affected by the Font of Inspiration feature.

entries.name: Martial Arts
entries: You can roll {@dice 1d4} in place of the normal damage of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}, and you can use your Dexterity in place of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.

entries.name: Focus
entries: You have two Focus Points. You regain all expended Focus Points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can spend one Focus Point to perform one of the below maneuvers.

items: You make two {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}.
You take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} and {@action Dodge|XPHB} actions.
You take the {@action Dash|XPHB} and {@action Disengage|XPHB} actions, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

entries: If you have two or more levels in {@class Monk|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your normal pool of Focus Points by 2.

entries.name: Metamagic
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Metamagic|Sorcerer|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature from the {@class Sorcerer|XPHB} class. You learn two Metamagic options of your choice. Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one of these Metamagic options with another one.

entries.name: Sorcery Points
entries: You gain 2 Sorcery Points. You regain all spent points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If you have two or more levels in {@class Sorcerer|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your normal pool of Sorcery Points by 2.

entries.name: Divine Smite
entries: You always have the {@spell Divine Smite|XPHB} spell prepared, and you can cast it without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast it with any other spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Lay on Hands
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a creature and restore a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to it equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You regain the ability to use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

If you have any levels of {@class Paladin|XPHB}, you instead increase your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} pool for your Lay on Hands feature by twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Rage
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature from the {@class Barbarian|XPHB} class. When you use Rage using this feat, your Rage Damage bonus is +2, and the only way to extend your Rage is to take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to extend it until the end of your next turn. Furthermore, the Rage can only last for a maximum of 1 minute. Once you use Rage in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
If you have any levels in {@class Barbarian|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your number of uses of Rage by 1.

entries.name: Ranger Spellcasting
entries: You always have the {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} spell prepared, as well as one other level 1 spell on the Ranger spell list of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can exchange your spell choice for another level 1 Ranger spell. You can cast each spell once without expending a spell slot, and regain the ability to do so when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast them with any other spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Proficiency
entries: Choose one of the following skills: {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}, {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Investigation|XPHB}, {@skill Nature|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB}, {@skill Stealth|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}. You gain proficiency with the chosen skill. If you already have proficiency, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} instead.

entries.name: Sneak Attack
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Sneak Attack|Rogue|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature from the {@class Rogue|XPHB} class. Your number of Sneak Attack dice is equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round down).
If you have any levels in {@class Rogue|XPHB}, these dice are added to your normal Sneak Attack dice.

entries.name: Spellbook
entries: You gain a special {@item Spellbook|PHB|spellbook}, in which you can store Wizard spells with the {@filter Ritual|spells|level=1;2|class=wizard|components & miscellaneous=ritual;!reprinted} tag. You start with two such spells of your choice in the book, which can be of level 1 or 2. The spellbook can be replaced or expanded upon in the same way that Wizards can, described in the ‘Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook’ sidebar in the {@class Wizard|XPHB} class. You can only cast spells in this spellbook as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB}, and your spellcasting ability for them is the ability increased by this feat.

If you have any levels in {@class Wizard|XPHB}, you instead add two level 1-2 Wizard spells with the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag to your spellbook for free. Furthermore, you gain the ability to copy non-Wizard spells into your spellbook. The spells must have the {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB} tag, and must be of a level you can prepare as a Wizard. Such spells count as Wizard spells for you, but you can only cast them as a {@variantrule Ritual|XPHB}.
If you later gain your first level in {@class Wizard|XPHB}, you copy the spells you learned through this feat into your main spellbook for free.

entries.name: Wild Shape
entries: You gain the {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature from the {@class Druid|XPHB} class, and you know two of the forms that are available to Druids at level 2. You only have one use for the feature, which you regain when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you transform, the number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} you gain is equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} instead of your Druid level, and you can stay transformed for 1 hour, instead of Wild Shape’s normal duration.
If you have two or more levels in {@class Druid|XPHB}, you instead simply increase your number of Wild Shape uses by 1, and your number of known forms by 2.

feat.name: Agile Duelist
entries: Your proclivity with single handed weapons has granted you agility and protection on the battlefield.

entries.name: Nimble Footwork
entries: Immediately after you make an attack with a weapon held in one hand and are holding no other weapons, you can move 5 feet without provoking {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

entries.name: Evasive
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid being {@condition Grappled|XPHB}.

entries.name: Backstab
entries: While you are within 5 feet of a creature, you can attempt to slip behind it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} without expending movement. The creature makes a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier). On a failure, the next damage roll you make before the end of the current turn with a {@item Dagger|XPHB} deals additional damage equal to your level + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

feat.name: Blood Frenzy

prerequisite.other: Proficiency with at least one natural weapon

entries: You are capable of harnessing a deep, primal bloodlust, which you can channel into attacks you make with your fangs, claws, or other natural weapons that you bear.

entries.name: Flurry
entries: Whenever you use the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to make an attack with a natural weapon, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to make an additional attack with a natural weapon.

entries.name: Primal Mark
entries: Immediately before taking the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can mark a creature that is missing any of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls made with natural weapons against the marked creature until the end of your turn. You can mark a creature in this way a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You cannot mark Constructs or Undead in this way.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: For the purposes of this feat, a natural weapon is any weapon attack that you can make with your body that is granted to you by a race or class feature. They are typically bestial in nature, usually in the form of a bite or claws. Traditional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|unarmed strikes} (punches, kicks, headbutts, etc.) do not qualify.

feat.name: Critical Striker
entries: You have trained to make precise strikes with weapons of substance, requiring two hands. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Critical Strike
entries: When you make a melee attack with a weapon you're wielding in two hands, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a {@dice d20} roll of two lower than normal. The weapon must have the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} or {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} property and must lack the {@itemProperty H|XPHB|Heavy} property.

feat.name: Jouster
entries: You have trained in the art of the joust, and have become adept at dismounting adversaries, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Dismounting Strike
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@item Lance|XPHB} while mounted, you can attempt to shove the target as a part of the same attack.

entries.name: Runup
entries: When you make an attack with a {@item Lance|XPHB}, you can add {@damage 1d12} to the damage roll on a hit, provided that you move at least 30 feet in a straight line immediately before you make the attack. If you are mounted when you make this attack, the distance the creature is pushed on a successful shove attempt increases by 5 feet.

feat.name: Thrown Weapon Master
entries: You have specialized in the ways of throwing your weapons, doing so with impressive deftness. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Longthrower
entries: Attacking at long range doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on your ranged weapon attacks made with weapons with the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property.

entries.name: Swift Toss
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action and only make ranged attacks with weapons with the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property, you can make an additional {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} weapon attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Returning Weapon
entries: Immediately after hitting or missing an attack made with a weapon with the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property, the weapon returns to your hand.

entries.name: Flavoring Returning Weapon
entries: You may flavour the weapon returning to you however you like. Perhaps you have attached the weapon to a rope or chain that you can tug to bring it back to you, maybe you gain some magical power to call the weapon back to you, or perhaps still the weapon returns through a series of skilled ricochets. How you flavour this is up to you.

feat.name: Trident Master
entries: You have trained in the ways of the peculiar {@item Trident|XPHB} weapon, and can use its intricacies to your advantage.

entries.name: Disarm
entries: Immediately after you hit a creature with a {@item Trident|XPHB}, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to disarm the creature of one weapon it is wielding. The target can make a Strength saving throw (DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier).

entries.name: Reposition
entries: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack with a {@item Trident|XPHB}, you can move the creature 5 feet to an unoccupied space within your reach, as long as the creature is no more than one size larger than you.

feat.name: Whip Specialist
entries: You have mastered skills to take advantage of the pain-inflicting properties of the {@item Whip|XPHB}, as well as its usefulness as a grappling tool. You gain the following benefits:

entries.name: Light Whip
entries: You can use {@item Whip|XPHB|Whips} as if they have the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property.

entries.name: Whip Grapple
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@item Whip|XPHB}, you can choose to not deal damage, and instead use the {@item Whip|XPHB} to cause the creature to be {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you. You do not require a free hand to perform this grapple, but it ends early if you are no longer wielding the {@item Whip|XPHB} and you cannot make any attacks with it until the grapple ends. The target can be no more than one size larger than you.

entries.name: Painful Lash
entries: When you deal damage to a creature with an attack made with a {@item Whip|XPHB}, the target is wreaked with pain. The target suffers a penalty equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to Constitution saving throws made to maintain {@condition Concentration|XPHB|concentration} resulting from this instance of damage, and suffers the same penalty to ability checks it makes until the end of its next turn.
