backgroundFluff.name: Battle Chaplain
entries: Your devotion to your deity is only outweighted by your devotion to your allies on the battlefield. You were trained and deployed as a medic, with the sole purpose of healing the wounded and bringing them home alive. Whether memories of these battles bring you fond feelings of camaraderie or distress, they have thoroughly shaped your outlook on the world.

backgroundFluff.name: Environmentalist
entries: You were raised to believe that nature is beautiful and sacred - well worth protecting. You have spent long years immersed in the natural world, coexisting with animals and plants and learning to care for them. The lessons learned during this time stick with you, even when you travel to places far from the lush greenery you yearn for.

backgroundFluff.name: Extraplanar Emissary
entries: You have spent much of your life beyond the borders of the Material Plane, acting as a representative for your kind in far off worlds. Perhaps a courtisan in the Seelie Courts of the Fey, or perhaps an ambassador in Sigil, you have become accustomed to the strange, otherworldly customs of another plane and have learned the skills necessary to thrive in such an environment.

backgroundFluff.name: Fugitive
entries: You have spent your days in clandestine places, hiding from some ever looming threat from your past, never daring to spend too long in one place. Along the way you've learned to be scrappy and inventive, and have gone by many names. You have trouble forming strong bonds, as you never know when you'll need to skip town to stay ahead of those that hunt you.

backgroundFluff.name: Gladiator
entries: You are accustomed to performing feats of martial prowess in front of an audience. Surviving your career in gladiatoral combat has demanded you trust in your comrades and, perhaps even more importantly, play to the audience. You carry those skills with you well beyond the arena.

backgroundFluff.name: Improviser
entries: You constantly find yourself in situations one couldn't possibly be prepared for - yet your ingenuity always seems to pull through for you. You have developed a habit of pocketing seemingly random objects, which you excel at crafting into useful contraptions, right when the situation calls for it.

backgroundFluff.name: Luminary
entries: Thanks to some accomplishment in your past, crowds look to you for inspiration, wise words or assurance. Your skill with comforting the masses has proven a useful asset, and you have become accustomed to being welcome and well regarded in circles where your name is known.

backgroundFluff.name: Physician
entries: You have invested countless gruelling hours into the study and practice of medicine - such that you can mend wounds, cure ailments and tend to the sick. You find a beauty to the logic of the inner workings of humanoids, and gain immense satisfaction from doing good in the world. Why you picked this path over devoting yourself to a god for healing magic is a touchy subject, however.

backgroundFluff.name: Squire
entries: You aspire to great things - but before that comes the grunt work. Permanent impressions line your shoulders where the straps of heavy bags have lain for extensively long rides with your charge. However, it is all worth it for the valuable experience you gain from carrying gear, handing gear over, and writing correspondences for your knight. Surely important skills to retain for when you become a knight yourself. Right?

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-7 feet tall)

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Emerged from the Loch
entries: You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can breathe air and water.

entries.name: Equine Drag
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is not reduced by dragging a creature you have {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, so long as the creature is your size or smaller.

entries.name: Kelpie Magic
entries: You always have the {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell prepared. When you reach character level 3, you learn the {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} spell, and at level 5 you learn the {@spell Water Walk|XPHB} spell. You can cast each of these spells once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose the ability when you select this species).

entries.name: Sticky Skin
entries: Your Kelpie ancestry has granted you exceptionally sticky skin. Creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks made to escape being {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you. In addition, you cannot unwillingly be disarmed of anything you are holding.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-6 feet tall)

entries.name: Blubber
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

entries.name: Deep Senses
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet. Furthermore, while you are submerged in water, you also have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet, though this sense does not extend beyond the body of water you're in.

entries.name: Hold Breath
entries: You can hold your breath for up to 1 hour.

entries.name: Swim Speed
entries: You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Seal Slide
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can slide along the ground or dash through water up to 30 feet in a straight line without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. This effect doesn't expend your movement, but you can't use it if you have a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of 0.

Each creature whose space you pass through must make a Dexterity saving throw. The DC is equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier, and a creature that is two or more size categories larger than you automatically succeeds on its save. A creature that fails its save takes a number of d4s of Bludgeoning damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save it takes half as much damage only.

You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-7 feet tall) or Small (about 2-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species

entries.name: Hammerspace
entries: While you are wearing an article of clothing with a pocket, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to draw or stow an object up to Small size into or from an extradimensional space contained within the pocket. This space can hold a number of objects up to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The same extradimensional space is accessible regardless of what clothing you are accessing it through. If you die, all stored objects harmlessly appear within 5 feet of your corpse.

entries.name: Toon Resilience
entries: Whenever you take Bludgeoning damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce that damage by an amount equal to {@dice 1d12} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Animation Style
entries: When you select this species, choose one of the following animation styles.

entries.name: CG
entries: Your artificial body is prone to the occasional glitch in space, which you have learned to trigger on command. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Claymation
entries: Your body is composed of a malleable clay-like material, giving you an unsettling appearance. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks. In addition, you can reshape your face and body as a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, permanently changing your appearance, though you still look to be made out of clay. This change does not affect your clothing or equipment.

entries.name: Sakuga
entries: Your body and movements become exquisitely detailed in critical moments. Immediately before you roll for {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can choose to gain a {@dice 1d4} bonus to ability checks and saving throws using Dexterity and Charisma until the end of that encounter. You then suffer a {@dice 1d4} penalty to those checks and saves and can't use this ability again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, as you have depleted your daily animation budget.

entries.name: Rubber Hose
entries: Your limbs are flexible and stretchy. You can handle and manipulate objects from up to 15 feet away. In addition, the reach for your melee attacks and {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Saturday Morning
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can sacrifice 10 feet of movement to run in place to an audible bongo beat before speeding off. Creatures that are within 5 feet of you when you activate this trait can't make {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against you for the rest of the turn.

entries: {{desc}}

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-6 feet long) or Small (about 2-4 feet long), chosen when you select this species

entries.name: Sensitive Sniffer
entries: Your sensitive nose grants you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on smell.

entries.name: Canine Bite
entries: You have a fanged maw that you can use to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you hit with it, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength modifier Piercing damage, instead of the Bludgeoning damage normal for an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}.

entries.name: Dextrous Maw
entries: You can use your mouth to perform actions that humanoids can do with their hands. You can wield one weapon, Shield or spellcasting focus in your jaws, you can have one creature {@condition Grappled|XPHB} in them, and you are able to effectively wield weapons with the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property with it. You are able to speak and perform Verbal and Somatic components of spells even if your mouth is being used to hold something.
You are not able to use your forelimbs to effectively wield things, however, and must use them to walk on.

entries.name: Distracting Bark
entries: You have a very noisy and distracting bark. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can unleash a barrage of loud barks at a creature within 60 feet of yourself that can hear you. The barking can be heard from up to 300 feet away. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against targets other than you until the start of your next turn. The DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + either your Constitution or Charisma modifier (choose when you select this species).

You can use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Zoomies
entries: When you take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on {@action Opportunity Attacks|XPHB|Opportunity attacks} against you until the end of the turn.

race.name: Three Little Guys in a Trenchcoat

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium together, Small separately

entries.name: Triple Threat
entries: You are, in fact, three Small sized creatures stacked on top of one another, using a floorlength piece of outerwear to disguise yourselves as one larger one. This affects your game statistics in the following ways.

entries.name: Hit Points and Damage
entries: Evenly divide your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} into three pools, which you track separately. Whenever you take damage from an effect that isn't an area of effect, roll {@dice 1d3} to decide which Hit Point pool is affected. When you take damage from an area of effect, divide the damage evenly between the three Hit Point pools. If you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you can distribute the Hit Points between the three pools as you like.

entries.name: Spells and Other Effects
entries: If you are targeted by a spell or some other effect that targets a single creature, all three parts of you are affected. See 'Hit Points and Damage' for how to handle damage.

entries.name: Separation
entries: If your parts are separated for any reason, those parts can move separately using your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, though they are unable to take any action granted to you by your class features or feats, and they share action economy: they collectively can only take one action, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} each round, as normal for a single creature. They use your ability scores, and your unarmored AC.

You can separate at any time (no action required), and automatically become separated if you gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition against your will. You can come back together as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, provided all three parts are within 5 feet of one another.

entries.name: Dying
entries: If one of your Hit Point pools drops to 0, the part of you associated with that Hit Point pool falls {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} and begins dying. You roll death saves for each part of yourself separately.

While one or two parts of you are dying, you can't take any action granted to you by your class features or feats, as if you were separated. You can move, but at half {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, as your conscious parts have to drag the dying ones around. If all three parts of you are dying, you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition like a normal creature who is dying.

If one of your parts dies, your remaining parts typically part ways, no longer able to meaningfully contribute to an adventuring party until the event occurs that the dead part is revived. Alternatively, at your DM's discretion, you can choose to continue your character as one of the surviving parts, taking on the species traits of your chosen lineage (see 'Lineages' below) in place of this species.

entries.name: Lineage
entries: You are composed of three Gnomes, three Goblins, three Halflings, or three Kobolds (choose when you select this species). Your lineage grants you one of the following traits.

entries.name: Gnomes' Cunning
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Goblins' Escape
entries: You can take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} or {@action Hide|XPHB} actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns.

entries.name: Halflings' Luck
entries: When you roll a 1 on the d20 of a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can reroll the die, and you must use the new roll.

entries.name: Kobolds' Cry
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you let out a cry at your enemies within 10 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any of those enemies who could hear you. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Halflings' Luck

_versions.name: Three Little Kobolds in a Trenchcoat

items.name: Lineage
entries: You are composed of three Kobolds. Your lineage grants you the following traits:

entries.name: Kobolds' Cry
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you let out a cry at your enemies within 10 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against any of those enemies who could hear you. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium or Small, chosen when you select this species.

entries.name: Undead Nature
entries: You do not need to breathe, eat or drink to survive, though you do need to sleep to gain the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Furthermore, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.

entries.name: Play Dead
entries: As an action, you can collapse onto the ground and play dead, giving yourself the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. While in this state, you are nearly indistinguishable from a normal corpse of the species you originated from. A creature can take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to attempt to discern your true nature by making a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. The DC is equal to 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma modifier (choose when you select this species). You can reassemble into your normal form at any time (no action required).

entries.name: Spooky & Scary
entries: Your appearance is unsettling to other creatures. Unless you have completely obscured your undead nature, whenever you take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action you must roll {@dice 1d4}. If the ability check you make as part of the action uses the {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} skill, you can add the result to the check - otherwise, you must subtract it. The DM can choose to ignore this trait if the creature being influenced is not bothered by your being Undead.

entries.name: Bone Patrol
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can detach one of your arms without any harm coming to you. While it is within 30 feet of you, the arm remains animate and you can control it remotely, though you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any ability checks you make with it if you can't see it. The detached arm is a Tiny object which shares your pool of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, uses your unarmored AC, and has a {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

While detached, the arm's bony fingers can be used as {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}, and the arm itself can be used as a Simple melee weapon with which you're proficient. The weapon has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} and {@itemMastery Sap|XPHB|Sap} properties and deals {@damage 1d8} + the attack's modifier Bludgeoning damage.
You can reattach the arm as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, provided it is within 5 feet of you.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 5-7 feet)

entries.name: Full of Electrolytes
entries: Your body is naturally suffused with minerals which keep you refreshed and energetic. When determining the penalties you suffer from any {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels you have, you treat your current {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level as if it was one level lower (to a minimum of 0). You still die if you reach 6 levels.

entries.name: Revitalising Body
entries: Your tasty pulp is nourishing and revitalising. Other creatures within 5 feet of you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take a bite out of you. When one does, you can choose to expend one or more of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} and roll them. The creature regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier (minimum 1 Hit Point). The maximum number of dice you can roll at once using this feature is equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (round up). Alternatively, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to feed yourself to a willing or {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} creature within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Ripening Aura
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can exude a hormone which causes living creatures to ripen in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on you for 1 minute. Whenever a creature starts its turn in the Emanation, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier). On a failure, it becomes ripened until the start of its next turn; once per turn when a ripened creature takes Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing damage, it takes extra damage of that type equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Slipping Strike
entries: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can force it to make a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + the ability score used to make the attack). On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, which it can't remove until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

raceFluff.name: Kelpling
entries: Kelplings draw a distant ancestry from Kelpies, lakebound equine creatures legendary for dragging hapless victims to a watery grave. Kelplings have the general appearance of a human, while retaining their ancestors' sticky green skin, seaweed-like hair and aquatic habitat.

Drawing from their territorial heritage, Kelplings tend to segregate themselves to one family per lake. This isolation results in strong familial bonds, but an inconsistent overall Kelpling culture. Some families use their inherited traits to uphold the murderous reputation of their ancestry, though most actively reject it by becoming famously friendly, using innate charm to win over new friends.

raceFluff.name: Phocan
entries: Phocans are human-like folk with the thick, oily skin and head of a seal. Native to polar regions of intense cold, they sport a thick layer of blubber, which allows them to survive the harsh weather and the ice-cold waters in which they hunt. Their faces feature large round eyes and sensitive whiskers, which grant them enhanced sight, especially underwater.

Phocan communities have long since mastered the art of dealing with the cold and have progressed from merely surviving to thriving there. They are renowned for the impressive structures they build out of ice and snow, ranging from the humble igloo to spectacular palaces built of packed snow. Visitors speak warmly of their hospitality, as well as the games they play, which often feature one Phocan sliding (or sometimes rolling) their rotund bodies in attempts to knock down objects or other Phocans.

Phocans rarely become adventurers, typically preferring the comforts of their icy homes, but every so often one will seek a life of excitement and discovery. Others find themselves swept up in a grand quest, often in the interest of protecting their homeland.

raceFluff.name: Toonkin
entries: Toonkin are cartoon-like beings brought into existence by otherworldly animators, who instil their creations with zany characteristics and off-the-wall energy to be supreme entertainers. Displaced from their native medium by some cosmic accidents or multiversal shenanigans, they are drawn to adventure - literally.

These wacky creations vary widely in appearance depending on their creator's animation style. Regardless of their style, they are obviously foreign to the plane they occupy, with the very fabric of their being sharply visually clashing against their surroundings. Toonkin do not age normally and tend to remain perpetually the same age. Their bodies defy conventional physics, shrugging off deadly blows and seemingly producing objects from thin air.

raceFluff.name: Doggo
entries: You're a dog! Whether you were awakened by a Druid, magically gained sentience on your own, or are just a naturally smart dog, you have developed a complex mind of your own, along with the capability of speech. In your pursuit of a life of adventure, you have undergone rigorous training to use your maw as dextrously as your humanoid companions use their hands, allowing you to wield weapons, cast spells, or otherwise make meaningful contributions to your party.
The magic that grants you your sentience does nothing to expand your lifespan - dogs typically live up to 10-13 years, and reach maturity at 1 year old.

raceFluff.name: Three Little Guys in a Trenchcoat
entries: You are not one, but three! You are the result of three Small sized creatures of the same species deciding to band together and disguise yourselves as one Medium sized creature, stuffing yourselves into one piece of outerwear, or one suit of armor. Through extensive training and collaboration, you have managed to learn to act together effectively. What synergy!

The most typical culprits of this gambit are Kobolds, who work together to pass themselves off as a Dragonborn, and Goblins who pass as Hobgoblins. Occasionally, however, Halflings and Gnomes also pull off this scheme to pass themselves off as Humans and Elves respectively.

raceFluff.name: Spooky Scary Skeleton
entries: Once alive, now dead, and thanks to necromantic rites your skeletal remains rise once again! Unlike typical undead minions, the magic that animates your corpse is permanent, and you harbor an intelligence and personality, whether it derives from your time amongst the living, or a new sentience.

Skeletons, such as yourself, tend to be outcasts from civil society and are typically feared by the commonfolk. Nonetheless, lacking the pesky trait of being alive grants you many perks, such as the ability to convincingly pretend to be dead, and to control your detached limbs.

raceFluff.name: Bananite
entries: Native to remote tropical islands, Bananites are sentient plant creatures with a strong resemblance to the yellow fruits with which they share a name. Their magical forms exude natural gasses which cause other living creatures to ripen, and their strikes carry juices which cause their foes to comically slip over. For such is the wrath of the Bananite.
